There is two ways I can review this game: the short way and the long way. Here's the short review. THIS GAME IS FANTASTIC.
Really, if you are contemplating buying this game that should be enough, much less the thousands of people that agree with me. Now here's the long review, for people who want a more specific description. The game presents itself as a facade of a low-quality RPG game, but don't be fooled. Without the 8-bit graphics scheme this game would be a lot worse off. The game's plot is based roughly on you, a human, who has fallen into an underground world filled with monsters. It fells like an RPG, but there's many, many differences. Difference #1 is the battle system. No longer are you picking off countless armies of emotionless foes, most of the monsters and enemies in this game ACTUALLY HAVE PERSONALITIES! Also, if you don't feel particularly genocidal, you can spare the enemies and some of them will be your friends! Strangely, some characters are not who they seem, be careful. Difference #2 is a big one. The characters in this game are some of the most memorable you'll ever see. Among some of them are a kindly goat-person, a depressed ghost, a lazy skeleton, and a killer television-host robot. But that's just the tip of the iceberg. Adding to the memorable characters, no longer does every character have that monotonous, RPG-stereotype medeival tone. The main characters are extremely modern and, in my expert opinion, ANYONE who plays this game can relate closely to at least one of them. #3 on my list is the storyboard. The story seems simple enough as you start, but as you continue on the main storyline fades away and a new, more in-depth, more surprising storyline appears. The story is NOT as simple as it seems, not by a longshot. #4 on my great big list is the VARIETY of play-modes. So far there's three, Pacifist, Neutral, and Genocide. Neutral is very simple. Just go through the game and play it through, kill some monsters, spare others. Depending on who you spare or kill, you'll get a different ending. Pacifist is my personal favourite; to do this rout you must go through a Neutral route killing NOTHING. then after you befriend all the great characters, finish the route, go back in, and help your new friends a bit more. This route explains a bit more of the games obscure storyline. Genocide is my least favourite. As you can tell, you go through this route mercilessly killing everyone you meet. Surprisingly, in the Neutral and Pacifist routes you feel like the good guy, but the genocide, beleive me, WILL make you feel like a genuinely bad person. (Tip: don't play this route first, you'll be VERY confused.) This route reveals a lot more of the storyline. Each route has its own final boss. Technically, the Pacifist and Neutral bosses are the same person, but not the same person at the same time. #5 is the second-to-last  one, the secrets. This game's easter eggs are not pointless. They will sometimes reveal more of the storyline if you manage to find them. Some easter eggs will make you question the game EVEN MORE. #6 is the very last. The game's protagonist-antagonist system is INGENIOUS. Some routes you are the protagonist, others, you're the antagonist. The game adds a creepy feeling to certain routes, which can be unnerving. Well, that's my review. If you read this review and want to know more about this wonderful game, take my advice: DO NOT watch someone else play it first. Play it for yourself! It is a wonderful game and I can't reccomend it enough!

TL;DR: Story is really promising so far, improves upon the decision-making aspect of the original life is strange.
Pros:

- Graphics is the same hand-painted style as usual
- many familiar characters appear agin, also some interesting new ones are introduced.
- Story is getting very interesting as mor episodes are coming out
- The original soundtrack is AMAZING
- Chloe's voice acting is actually surprisingly good for a different VA
- Same attention to detail as the original life is strange
Cons:
- optimization issues (bugs, animation glitches)
- certain parts of the dialogue are kind of cringe and awkward

I've been watching this game since it went into Beta. The graphics look great, but the developers just fall short on the basics...
- 3440x1440 has message boxes showing up off screen. Only the edges can be seen, while all of the text and general data is offscreen. Making it much harder to tell what is going on in game. Wide screen and custom resolutions are just basic functionality that should simply work on ANY PC game. If you don't support custom or at least standard resolutions, then you can't really call yourself a PC game in my opinion.
- Going prone on an incline causes a graphical glitch allowing you to see through the world. How did this ever make it through both QA and Beta? This is another bug dealing with basic functinality. How do you produce a game that allows for prone and crawling and never once notice the clipping? Either that or they were simply too incompetent to fix it, neither of which is a good sign.
- AI got stuck in the water. Two deer were walking in the water and just got stuck on nothing. While this bug is a little more forgivable given that these types of bugs generally require very specific locations/actions, on top of other basic functionality it all just points to Devs who either don't care about the quality of the game, or who are too incompetent to ensure the quality of the game. In either case I do not recommend buying it, though I will say it looks beautiful when it isn't glitching out.

eyes) the game looks pretty nice. Wonderful scenery and grand vistas abound – both of which, I feel, can be pretty awe inspiring. When looking at the world around you, from both ground level and from an observation tower; you get a sense of how big the world you’re in really is. Sound wise – the voice acting, the music, and sound effects has been done pretty well. The detailed sounds of the animal living life & their movements about, along with the enviromental effects such as; the rain, wind, cracking branches, and the crunch of the ground under foot all add to the sense of immersion and brings to life the feeling of truly being in the woods stalking / hunting my prey.

While the game is nice, it’s not perfect. A few complaints worth mentioning are:
Optimization could be a little better, and on the graphics front – I would like to see SLI support added.
Scene coloring, as well as the overall “crispness” of the textures could be better – perhaps a few in-game adjustment sliders could help with this?
UI wonkiness...like not being able to exit the settings menu without going to the map??
Game pad support, even keyboard control binding could definitely be improved upon. The lag between trying to rebind a key, and the time the game accepts is pretty strange. Usually you have no idea if you’re currently rebinding or not, because we are given no confirmation and/or feedback from this system. Controller wise, I was unable to you the controller exclusively without using the keyboard to bail me out…I’m looking at you menus! For most this won’t be an issue, as many will probably not dare use a controller, but some of us (with semi-worn out joints) find comfort in using the gamepad from time to time.
This game and others like it won't be for everyone. Overall though, I would, and do recommend this game for purchase! However if you're not a fan of the genre, but find yourself curious – I would suggest a "buy & try" during a sale sometime. That being said...

I love it, great game, somewhat unfinished but everything these days is. A lot of people expect a finished game upon release which I find silly... Expectations of games in the modern day is insane, people think every game is a AAA title will hundreds of millions backing it. While the game isn't finished and many bugs are still out there it isn't game breaking and I have had no issues progressing. I had to adjust playstyle to accomodate bugs, mainly making too much sound while moving in any kind of stance (this includes the lower noise perks).
I think give this game a little time and things will iron out, not all bugs are going to disappear but they will fix the major ones or at least I hope they do.
The Animals are great, a huge range to shoot at and the bedding/feeding/drinking zones make finding a required animal a lot easier. The movement is pretty solid along with the animations of reactions to bullet fire or getting hit. I see a lot of people complaining about not being able to down a deer with the starter rifle and sorry to say but you are just a terrible shot. A heart or decent lung shot is going to drop a deer straight away if not a lung shot is going to have them run an extra 50m then die, anything else is just punishment for a terrible shot. Leading animals also appears to work well, more often then not I am able to get a 2nd or 3rd shot in before the animal is in cover or I have lost sight.
These are fine, I never played the original but having a background in FPS I am able to aim the rifle and hit my target at anything under 200m pretty easily. The 223 is a neat little fox hunting rifle which I have used on countless foxes including my 48,000,000 score kill (another bug). I have recently unlocked the 270 and it will drop pretty much any deer with a chest/shoulder shot. Progression on weapons is fine, its not too slow and definately not too fast. I would like to see more customization however this could happen in the future.
Currently I am level 15 and it hasn't been a quick ride, having explored 80% of the map and killed over 100 animals it hasn't been easy. With that said I do like the progression, it isn't fast and I really have to work at it to get the unlocks I want. There is no quick level option in the game (that I know of) so doing what I am doing seems to be paying off in the long run. I also like how you have to progress with the weapon of choice, instead of just having a level requirement to shoot the best gun in the game. On that note by the time you unlock a better rifle you should be a better shot with rifles.

I'm going to strongly recommended this game. I fortunately paid only $20 for it, but definitely would be willing to pay $60 now that I'm getting close to the end of the story. The open world mechanic is much like the Arkham series, and I can see it not being for everyone; but the story is really where it shines, I think. It stays true to feeling like the films. I'd even say it does well to take from the best parts of all four of the films.
What I'd say about the gameplay itself is that it's super fun, while maybe a bit tedious after 30+ hours of driving and fighting. The game has a way of bringing back the flair when you least expect it though. Whether it's in the form of a huge, crashing storm that forces you right into an enemy camp that's lobbing fiery molotovs at you, or the brief but endearing "horror" sections that send you deep into the earth. It's those moments, alongside the world building and atmosphere that make it all worth it. Granted I'm the type of person who reads the lore entries you get throughout the game.
I do wish that they'd allowed for some more customization of your car and character. There is a lot, but most of it is pretty linear. I could do for maybe some kind of skill tree or more ways to make yourself look like even more of a BAMF.
It can also start to get too easy at times if you don't actively stop yourself from gaining too much scrap or levelling too fast. It can take a bit of balancing on the players part to keep things interesting, which is unfortunate but understandable given the open world nature and all there is to do in that world.

4 hours into this game, and I have not been able to put it down. Each character has a single life to assault the castle. When he/she dies, you pick up the quest with one of your children... from the beginning of the castle! And every entry into the castle produces a new, random map!
The cycle repeats itself, and you continue to commit generational suicide over and over again. One more turn... okay, seriously thought, I got it now. One more turn...
You will die... a lot. There are "level gates" in the game that force you to spend time gathering gold, dying, gathering more gold, and dying some more in order to be a high enough level to take on the monsters. The mechanic allowing you to "freeze" a dungeon in order to practice on a specific boss or go back for a chest that you didn't get really helps this leveling process along. And as much as I thought it might get stale, the game remains fresh, even though the ultimate quest continues to be the same.
Overall, really fun platformer with a lot of replayability!

For me, Rogue Legacy is one of those games that I would sit and think up of, saying "Hmm... It would be awesome if a game had this and that, along with the ability to do such and such..." Not very descriptive? Well, what I mean is it has certain aspects that you'd like to have in a side-scrolling rogue like game. The ability to level up certain stats, get new armor and powerups, several classes, and a not-so-punishing death system, all while being challenging to the point where it can be frusterating, but still fun and rewarding.
Story-wise, unless you read the books, you could skip the story and beat the game, which would be a shame, cause the story pulls ties things up for the ending (It's not an immersive story though, like I said, you have to sit and read it.) It has a New Game+, where everything is carried over into a harder game, and I'd say it's quite replayable. No new bosses or areas, just harder enemies.
It does have flaws, like enemy attacks can glitch through walls sometimes, healing items are too scarce, you can very, very rarely fall into the floor (It's happened about 5 times, you can always get out though) and near and far sightedness slows the game (It runs great normally, but it may be my computer's fault)
I'd recommend it for anyone who likes 2D Castlevania and Metroid mixed with leveling up and different classes (PS, the classes all behave and fight the same, it's mostly stat distribution and special abilities, plus certain traits.) Try to get it on sale, cause though I enjoy it, others may not enjoy the style.

A "good" TPS gameplay, "okay" game mechanics, this game could have just been "one of these TPS shooter". But it's more than that.
Instead, it chose to also have an interesting approach to storytelling (coming in several different forms) and an original interpretation process, it chose to innovate in that part (but not too much - no Molyneux-ing here, there is actual innovation), and I have to admit that it actually succeeded.
It may be a bit short (finished it in normal difficulty in 9 hours - replayability is possible, but I don't think I'll spend more than 20 hours in total in it), but it's really worth it.
It's a game worth investing yourself in, worth staring the scenery (they really nailed an extremely impressive Dubaï - there's the good/average battle arenas sure, but some places, some viewpoints, damn I had to stop and stare, I wanted to stay there for several minutes (and did, sometime)), worth immersing yourself in the story and the characters.
I'm not saying it's a masterpiece (it's probably too soon to judge anyway), but it's a really interesting take on violence/war and personal responsibility.
If you're interested in violence (in societies, in psychology, in games), in war, in morality in life threatening situations, and enjoy beautiful landscapes in the desert, I recommend this game.

I'm going to strongly recommended this game. I fortunately paid only $20 for it, but definitely would be willing to pay $60 now that I'm getting close to the end of the story. The open world mechanic is much like the Arkham series, and I can see it not being for everyone; but the story is really where it shines, I think. It stays true to feeling like the films. I'd even say it does well to take from the best parts of all four of the films.
What I'd say about the gameplay itself is that it's super fun, while maybe a bit tedious after 30+ hours of driving and fighting. The game has a way of bringing back the flair when you least expect it though. Whether it's in the form of a huge, crashing storm that forces you right into an enemy camp that's lobbing fiery molotovs at you, or the brief but endearing "horror" sections that send you deep into the earth. It's those moments, alongside the world building and atmosphere that make it all worth it. Granted I'm the type of person who reads the lore entries you get throughout the game.
I do wish that they'd allowed for some more customization of your car and character. There is a lot, but most of it is pretty linear. I could do for maybe some kind of skill tree or more ways to make yourself look like even more of a BAMF.
It can also start to get too easy at times if you don't actively stop yourself from gaining too much scrap or levelling too fast. It can take a bit of balancing on the players part to keep things interesting, which is unfortunate but understandable given the open world nature and all there is to do in that world.

I didn't expect to love this game as much as I do. I bought it on a lark during a Steam sale for under $3. I've plowed about 70 hours into it over the last few months, playing almost every night. There's something very peaceful about this driving game -- almost completely the opposite of the average racing game. It's about driving carefully, obeying traffic rules, and slowly building your truck empire. The graphics are lovely - you'll send a lot of time driving around, just looking at the scenery and the wonderful little touches that make the in-game locations look like their real-world counterparts. My favorite part of the whole game is the ability to listen to (European) radio stations while you're driving. I grew up in Belgium and now live on the West Coast of the US; as a result, I can now listen to the Belgian morning radio shows as I drive around at night. You may be skeptical about a truck sim game -- I was -- but put plain and simple, this is some of the most fun I've had playing a PC game in years. Recommended!

ETS2 is a very casual truck driving sim. You manage your own company with garages all over Europe, and buy trucks and hire drivers to get things running. While your drivers will find jobs by themselves, and do not really need your input, you can either do jobs for other companies, or do the jobs with your own truck. Or simply go freeroaming if you're in the mood for that.
The driving itself works great. Easy controls and fairly realistic physics. I have no complaints here.
Graphics are good. Not great, but decent enough for me. Music and sound effect are also good, but there's no music while you drive. However, you can either add mp3s to a playlist, or tune in on internet radio channels, if you want to.
I only have two issues with this game, none are gamebreaking:
1. Traffic AI is sometimes kinda silly, but they are constantly working on improving it.
2. No cloud save. This means that if I want to play in my house, then continue in my apartment, I have to copy save files and bring them with me. Very annoying for those of us who lives two places with a stationary PC both places.
If you'd like a casual driving sim, without the big challenges, this is the game for you. I recommend you get the Going East DLC too, as it adds more countries, and remember to check out the Scandinavia DLC when it gets released. The rest of the DLCs are just paintjobs for your trucks, I don't recommend spending a lot of money here, get them while on sale, which they often are.

A very solid, if not too familiar open world game. If you have played any modern open world game in the past 5 years or so than you already know what to expect out of Mad Max. There's lots of stuff to collect, build, and plenty of side missions to do for each stronghold keeper.
The combat is ripped right from the Batman Arkham games which seems to be a staple in Warner Bros. published game now and I am perfectly fine with this, it really suits Max since he is a very good fighter and does whatever he has to do to win the fight. I did find a few little glitches like Max doing a finisher move without the enemy even being in his hands or Max punching an enemy so hard his head would go through a wall or the ground, but these instances do not happen that often.
As you would expect in an open world Mad Max game there is A LOT of driving and car combat. The way your vehicle handles depends on the car body and other components that you choose such as suspension, tires, and bumpers that can make the car more a death dealer on wheels or a speed machine to get yourself out of close call battles if you do not like the car combat. As for me, I LOVED the vehicular combat. Watching enemy cars blow up, fall apart, or even use the torpedo to grab the driver and yank him out of his vehicle was very satisfying.
Mad Max is a very fun game and a sleepr hit for this year for me. The game does get repetitive but at its core Mad Max is a game about having fun and blowing things up. [Ep.1 thoughts written September 3rd] Before the Storm is off to a strong and promising start. The character writing succeeds in breathing life into old and new characters; the voice acting, while a few of the replaced voice actors due to the VA strikes can stick out like a sore thumb, do a fine commitment and Chloe's new voice grows to become a believable younger image of her; the choice-making really impacts your decisions throughout this single episode, which I advise that it's very worth exploring as much of the environment and talk to every character you find.
Deck Nine has proven themselves to live up to the expectations of building a worthy prequel, so far at least. This is also the longest amount of time I've put into an episodic story-focused game, clocking in almost 5 hours into this alone which makes me optimistic that with just the three episodes alone the price, albeit already lower, will be worth it. Can't wait to see the story unfold!
[Ep.2 thoughts written October 20th] This second entry did a good job quickly pulling me into its story once again. Chloe and Rachel's relationship takes stronger bouts into some of the more ridiculous fantasies of an adolescent's living and gets to some borderline fanservice-y elements, but I loved every scene played out. The choicemaking continues to be tough and bitter, yet still grey and engaging while yielding some tangible outcomes within the episode the more you progress (outcomes ranging from the significant to the very subtle). Rhianna DeVries' performance as Chloe has now quelled my doubts, and she's since disappeared into the role. The music from Daughter is again terrific.
I think something Deck Nine is doing better than DONTNOD is fleshing out the supporting characters more. In the original game, I personally only really cared about Max and Chloe and several of the students at school or the teachers or the folks around town felt like underdeveloped caricatures/archetypes. Playing as Chloe in this game, more of the students come across as cool or interesting and a few characters are revealing themselves to be more endearing than the first episode established.
One minor thing I'm concerned about is how they're going to wrap this all up with just one more episode. Not that these episodes have felt short (plenty of people/stuff to interact with and I already have ~10 hours into just two episodes!), but the way it's paced feels like there should still be at least a few more episodes (not counting the bonus Max episode, at least for now).
Loving Before the Storm. Each episode so far has had some wonderfully memorable scenes and I know it's going to be bittersweet saying goodbye to these characters once it finishes.
[Ep.3 thoughts written December 22nd] Episode 3 is a little more disappointing compared to the last two episodes. The pacing is a bit off, some critical character relationships got less screentime and attention, and the final driving plot theme and decisions didn't feel quite as impactful and reflective of the entire game. In the end, it really did feel like the game needed at least one more episode to make for a more thorough conclusion to the story.
However, the decision-making of the side plotlines and smaller details make for an impressive number of so many different outcomes. The music is intense and the final string of cutscenes is beautiful.
For Before the Storm as a whole, I highly recommend for fans of Life is Strange and definitely for anyone who likes interactive-story/Telltale-style games and who can endure teenage angst.

'Frustration is fun' must have been the motto of the designers.  I will destroy them.
Not because this is a bad game.  It's a great game - the graphics are perfectly thought out as a silly retro platformer, the controls are super tight and worked out of the box with my ancient POS logitech gamepad, the designs are consistently challenging.  Everything you wanted from a roguelike plus everything you expected from the best of the NES/SNES platforming generation of games.
No, the reason I will destroy the developers is because this is a great game made by people who hate you and especially hate progression.  Let me explain.
Complaint the first: Charon.  There is no bleeding reason for Charon to be in this game.  Every time I have to pay the toll without buying an upgrade, I hit alt-f4, because I hate him and what he does to the gameplay that much.
Complaint the second: Upgrade costs.  The game calculates your upgrade costs by adding an amount, N, to the base cost of every upgrade.  N is figured from the number of upgrades you have bought already.  (Same deal at the smithy and the enchantress, but harsher.)  The cumulative effect of this is to create an atmosphere of wildly upspiraling inflation.
I would cheerfully endure either of these challenges by themselves, but both together is unforgivable.  This game makes me too angry to play for more than a few minutes at a time, because about half of my sessions end too soon for me to make any progression.

initially, looking at this game without reading any reviews or additional information, one would think that it is just another generic looking, dime-a-dozen military 3rd person shooter, absolutely devoid of any interesting content and essentially created for the sake of making some extra money in some random video game franchise and nothing else...however, all of that couldn't be farther from the truth.  SPEC OPS: THE LINE is a bold new step into previously untraversed territory that almost no other video game has ever had the balls to take. this is a game that, through its clever use of seemingly predictable tropes and ideas, tricks the player into a place that they would otherwise never want to reach. citing jospeh conrad's infamous short story HEART OF DARKNESS as its chief inspiration is already miles beyond the forgettable pap that constitutes most modern military shooter storylines, so it's no real shock that as i kept on playing the game and getting further into its dark expanses, i wanted to get out.  this is the first video game i've ever played where the only way that you can actually beat the game is to commit acts that even in your worst nightmares, one couldn't even comprehend attempting against another human being. this game destroys the completely ridiculous and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t macho machine scenarios that seem to flood the market (thanks to COD and its ilk) by taking the genre and putting it out of its own misery.  you can not be a hero in this game and the violence that you beget is not some awesome adventure meant to make you feel like a warrior, but it instead reduces you to a former shell of yourself and then asks you to keep going on without stopping long enough to realize what you just did.  this is the first game that i know of that has genuinely succeeded in using the very violence that most military shooters use as a selling point and internalizing it into a message that essentially shames every single player who finishes the game. the story and overall message is game changing stuff; it's what most game developers would be too afraid to tackle and most gamers too squeamish to contemplate honestly. while its gameplay is forgettable, quite possibly on purpose, the overall story and the ideas behind it all is something so powerful and unnerving, no other recent video game has reached its level and it is doubtful that any others will.

Great sim, true to the original in most respects.   A few minor bugs, but nothing that ruined my 4-hour long hunt (at least not until the very end, but more on that later).   Nice graphics, an environment that pulls you in and a nice change of pace from fast-paced shooters.   Was in a tower and shot downwards at a really nice buck, missed his vitals and spent the next couple of hours stalking him.  Finally got him well after dark, what a task.   It reminded me of the original game in that you really felt like you'd been on a hunt and had created a memory that you want to share with others that play the game.
I only experienced these bugs, and most didn't create any issues in playing/enjoying the game, as I know they will be fixed soon:
- My gun makes no noise when fired, you see the smoke and the recoil and it hits the animal, but no sound
- My animal calls/lures only make sound once every 5 or 6 times they are used
- There was a thin line on my GPS in the map and when I approached it there was an invisible wall I couldn't pass.  At first I thought maybe I had hit the edge of the map, but it was close to the start.  Had to walk along the invisible wall for about 20 feet before it let me pass, then I went back to see if it was still there and it had cleared
- The only bad bug (that would affect gameplay in a major way) is when I hit around midnight in-game all of the animals froze.   I was trying to call in a buck that I'd heard and I saw his harem first (the does) and they wouldn't move.  The buck kept calling and I waited several minutes before I figured out that they were stuck.  I approached them all and they could look around, but not move in any direction.  Luckily, this was at the end of my 4-hour initial session.
Despite the early flaws, this game is fantastic.   I had been waiting a long time for a new version of this game and it was worth the wait...

Apart from the dungeon randomizing every time you die, you have to pay all of your gold to re-enter it (though I read there's something you can do remedy that -- but the game didn't hold my attention long enough for me to bother).
If there was a difficulty ramp-up with each new area, I might be more inclined to play it, but when you enter the first room and your task is to jump across a pit of spikes while enemies are shooting several bullets at you, and all you have to stand on is character-wide platforms that keep you from a spikey demise, it becomes abundantly obvious this game wasn't designed with any type of casual play involved at all. And don't even get me started on the bosses... ♥♥♥♥ me running, the only one I fought was a giant eyeball that shot so many bullets, the only place I could go that was safe was a panel with retracting spikes. Thanks, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s...
There needs to be more blueprint drops, there needs to be a way to block bullets (without sucking up your MP), there needs to be more health drops, and there needs to be better randomization. I'm sorry if you're one of those people that enjoys being punished by a game, but I am not. I bought it to have fun, not to be given the desire to pour copious amounts of caustic liquid down someone's throat.

Ok I dont normally write reviews but for this one I felt I had too based on others negative comments as I nearly didnt buy this game as a result of those negative reviews...
If your like me and you always read reviews before buying a game and are normally put off by negative comments about system performance but accept that a new game will always have some bugs then this is aimed at you.
I run an I7 6700K 16GB 980TI and have no issues running this game at max settings.
The visuals and sounds of this game are simply great and the size of the open world is huge. If your worried about those saying you spend a lot of time walking about doing nothing, yes you will spend a lot of time walking around trying to find animals only to never find them as they see \ hear you coming before you see them and scare them off. Or you find the animal your tracking it sees you and then runs off... But isnt that the point... Its a hunting game its about tracking and not being seen, its about a slow methodical approach, its not supposed to be easy and if it was we would all moan and say its too easy and arcady...
In summary I would say you need patience to play this game, practice to get better and yes a few bugs to be patched by the developer. But while your doing all that you will be walking through lush amazing enviroments thinking wow the grass and trees actually move with the wind in the right direction and I need to pick my path so I dont get heard stomping around unlike other games.
As for bugs I have encountered three so far:
(1) GAME DOESNT ALWAYS LET YOU LEAVE A MENU WITH ESC LIKE YOU SHOULD. For this I found choosing another menu topic and then hitting ESC works fine.
(2) MAIN MAP GOES FUNKY OR DOES NOT START CENTERED ON YOU. For this I simply zoom out then back in again or exit and re-enter main map and it is fine then.
(3) DIFFICULTING SWITCHING WEAPONS & ITEMS FROM STORAGE TO BACKPACK. By far the biggest bug I have found and only way to resolve is keep entering and exiting storage until it will let you select and drag an item to your back pack and only do one item at a time before exiting and coming back. THIS IS STILL NOT A GAME BREAKER.....

No longer do you have to pay to get necessary items. That's a win in my book.
Edit: Sometimes, you just can't win in life.

[Ep.1 thoughts written September 3rd] Before the Storm is off to a strong and promising start. The character writing succeeds in breathing life into old and new characters; the voice acting, while a few of the replaced voice actors due to the VA strikes can stick out like a sore thumb, do a fine commitment and Chloe's new voice grows to become a believable younger image of her; the choice-making really impacts your decisions throughout this single episode, which I advise that it's very worth exploring as much of the environment and talk to every character you find.
Deck Nine has proven themselves to live up to the expectations of building a worthy prequel, so far at least. This is also the longest amount of time I've put into an episodic story-focused game, clocking in almost 5 hours into this alone which makes me optimistic that with just the three episodes alone the price, albeit already lower, will be worth it. Can't wait to see the story unfold!
[Ep.2 thoughts written October 20th] This second entry did a good job quickly pulling me into its story once again. Chloe and Rachel's relationship takes stronger bouts into some of the more ridiculous fantasies of an adolescent's living and gets to some borderline fanservice-y elements, but I loved every scene played out. The choicemaking continues to be tough and bitter, yet still grey and engaging while yielding some tangible outcomes within the episode the more you progress (outcomes ranging from the significant to the very subtle). Rhianna DeVries' performance as Chloe has now quelled my doubts, and she's since disappeared into the role. The music from Daughter is again terrific.
I think something Deck Nine is doing better than DONTNOD is fleshing out the supporting characters more. In the original game, I personally only really cared about Max and Chloe and several of the students at school or the teachers or the folks around town felt like underdeveloped caricatures/archetypes. Playing as Chloe in this game, more of the students come across as cool or interesting and a few characters are revealing themselves to be more endearing than the first episode established.
One minor thing I'm concerned about is how they're going to wrap this all up with just one more episode. Not that these episodes have felt short (plenty of people/stuff to interact with and I already have ~10 hours into just two episodes!), but the way it's paced feels like there should still be at least a few more episodes (not counting the bonus Max episode, at least for now).
Loving Before the Storm. Each episode so far has had some wonderfully memorable scenes and I know it's going to be bittersweet saying goodbye to these characters once it finishes.
[Ep.3 thoughts written December 22nd] Episode 3 is a little more disappointing compared to the last two episodes. The pacing is a bit off, some critical character relationships got less screentime and attention, and the final driving plot theme and decisions didn't feel quite as impactful and reflective of the entire game. In the end, it really did feel like the game needed at least one more episode to make for a more thorough conclusion to the story.
However, the decision-making of the side plotlines and smaller details make for an impressive number of so many different outcomes. The music is intense and the final string of cutscenes is beautiful.
For Before the Storm as a whole, I highly recommend for fans of Life is Strange and definitely for anyone who likes interactive-story/Telltale-style games and who can endure teenage angst.

The Borderlands franchise is very well-known within the gaming community. Most people instantly recognise it because of its colourful graphics and insanely fun and rewarding co-op and singleplayer expeiriences. The purpose of this review is to briefly explain whether to buy this game or not.
Graphics:
Borderlands 2 is suprisingly being driven by a heavily modified version of Unreal Engine 3. This provides decent visuals with above average light shafts but it lacks high-res textures (most notibly the environment textures). The world of Pandora is very cartoon-like in appearance. (This is intentional). The Borderlands series uses a technique called Cel Shading. This outlines all edges of the environment, guns, charactermodels, and vehicles. Some people say that this is a very ugly add-on and it is possible to turn it off, but the game was built around a colourful world, and removing the cartoon-like shadings is a pretty bad idea. In terms of performance, this game runs  butter smooth. I was using an AMD Radeon HD 7570 2GB Vram, and maxed out at 1280x720, my frames were hovering around the 45 FPS mark. For low-end computers, the game will still run fine.
Gameplay:
OMFG how did Gearbox invent such an amazing and addictive combat system? Seriously, if you don't believe me ask anybody else that has played this game! There are (i'm not exaggerating) literally a gazillion guns, or at least gun combos. Each gun handles differently and each will yearn for a different playstyle. The more traditional assault rifles are extremely effective at gunning down hordes of enemies while the long range Maliwan sniper rifles electricute any enemy it touches. Furthermore, guns can be outfitted with "special abilities". The Bandit style of guns are your traditional  guns (SMGs, short range rifles, etc) while other guns handle differently. Hyperion weapons have high recoil, but they straighten out the longer you hold the trigger down. Obviously, to find your favorite weapon, you have to try different styles to see which gun fits your playstyle.
DLC's:
Normally, I would recommend not buying any DLC's unless you are absolutely sure you will play the game long enough to finish them, but for Borderlands, its impossible not to! I got the GOTY edition and on top of the regular vanilla game, I recieved all of the available DLC's. This is about 80-85 hours of DLC game time alone.
Value for Money:
BUY IT! It's worth every penny of its price. The gameplay is fun and it's even better if you've got buddies to play with.

Ive been a huge supporter of this game, with 3000+ hours on my main account, I can tell you that DayZ has had its ups and downs. It was the first game I ever got on steam and I played it day-in, day-out enjoying every moment when the game was first released, yes there were a few bugs a glitches, but it was a lot more playable then now. Ive read other reviews and agree that the devs definitaly put a lot of their time into things they shouldnt, like new guns, cars, locations, etc, but they have changed the game significanlty since it first came out. For any new poeple coming into the game now, it is a huge learning curve comparred to some other survival games. For example, learning the map and spawns is difficult when you spawn in the middle of nowhere everytime, only once in a while close to a town. One thing I dislike about DayZ at the moment is how it is all based around PVP and not so much PVE. That being said, they have put some work into the zombies, making them harder to kill and run away from, but there is still a lot of work to be done. Item/gun spawns are also a lot diffrent than before, which I can understand since you usually dont find an M4 in an office building, but sometimes I can only find 2-3 items throughout a whole town. They have worked a bit on the de-sync issues but I still find myself time-to-time getting hit through a wall, or shot while I am inside a building. Dont ghet me wrong, the devs have put a lot of work into DayZ, and I knew coming into it there would be a long process of developement, but I did not expect it to take this long, and for the devs to focus on areas that dont matter as much. Overall this game can be very fun, especially played with friends. In the end I would recommend buying this game, but dont get mad if it's not what you expected.

Ah yes, it's another typical 3rd person open world sandbox (no pun intended) game.
Originally looking at the trailers and such I was hoping this would be different to the rest, sadly it has not been the case. Everything down to the tedious and typical "Go here, climb this, reveal map" scenario is included just incase you were scared of straying from the familar. The game challanges nothing, the only new and sorta' interesting aspect being the car combat.
Now this was supposed to be the primary selling point of the game. You have your car which you can upgrade with scrap and basically make more deadly, or generally customise it to your play style/look. This is great for the most part, however, the game blocks you from purchasing certain upgrades until you've passed certain mission points and such. This is an absolute pain in the♥♥♥♥♥♥ In comparison, a reason why I and many others loved MGSV was due to that freedom to essentially unlock anything right from the start as long as you had the currency, with very few items needing pre-requisists. Even if they did require these, you could generally pick them up at anytime. Mad Max is not the case, so basically you are following the progression the game WANTS you go.
Car combat once again however is great fun, it's satisfying just slamming into the side of an enemy and watching them explode in a hail of fire like the game was directed by Michael Bay. It can become a bit rinse and repeat, but once again its just made to feel extremely satisying. Also hooking enemies out of their cars and watching them fly off is hilarious and will never get old. The game however forces you out of the car a lot, odd for a game where that is advertised as the focus yet 80% of the game is more on foot and fighting with your fists Arkham style.
Now, plot and characters. So far I have no bloody idea what the actual main plot point is supposed to be. The game begins with Max's famous car being stolen from him, and so you'd assume the rest of the game would be his epic quest to retrieve it from the villainous warlord that stole it from you. WRONG. The car gets instantly scrapped from the start, hence why he now has the "Magnum Opus". After this point it just seems like its Max randomly bumping into people and doing tasks for them for no good reason. Along with that the characters are all generally dull, it's all just not engaging at all. The most interesting character is probably your companion Chumbucket, though he is essentially Gollum but obsessed with cars rather than a magic ring. Some of the characters logic is rather interesting as well, after running into lady "Pink Eye" (I know, fantastic names right?) and saving her from an untimely death she says (and I paraphrase here) "Thank you for risking your life to save me for no reason, now why shouldn't I kill you?". I know this is the wasteland and all, but that logic just defies me.
Overall as I stated before, gameplay is the same as any other open world game really, it borrows too much and changes too little. Except maybe the control scheme which is just awful (Should note, I am playing on a 360 controller). Max's movements are all incredibly slugish, it makes it seem like there is almost a slight lag with every command. The default mapped controls are so counter-intuitive as well. Left trigger for jump? WHY?! And B being quickfire has led to many instances of me wasting shotgun rounds by accident. This issue may just be a more personal thing, but I just don't see why it's mapped the way it is for controller when previous schemes clearly work just fine.
Yeh, I'm gonna' stop there. There are plenty of gripes with this game I have compared to pro's. It's just an incredibly unoriginal and uninspired game. Thank god I only picked it up for £10. If you need something to kill time and it's cheap then sure, get this. Other than that, I'd avoid it, you've played it before.

THE GOOD - There's plenty of things to like about this game. There's a creative, daring premise, a tutorial that does an excellent job at not only teaching you the basics but setting the mood for what's to come, a grant system that gives you directions during the game's main sandbox mode and a reliable update schedule that keeps bringing the game closer to completion.
THE BAD - After playing the tutorial, you might feel a little disappointed that the main game doesn't quite offer anything story mode-ish yet. Given the aforementioned update schedule though this isn't that big a deal, there's still plenty of other things to keep your interest and I feel reasonably confident when I say that it's only a matter of time until we get story content as well.
TO SUM THINGS UP - Prison Architect currently is an Early Access game, but don't let this fool you - unlike many other such games, it actually offers plenty of playable content, a dev team that is actually dedicated to their work and monthly updates bringing the game closer to completion. It's definitely worth a try.

I'll be honest, I came into Spec Ops: The Line thinking it would be another ''MURICA!'' shooter, and I left absolutely blown away. The combat feels very Gears of War-esque, but I found it to be quite nice for this game (No, there's no wallbouncing or anything like that). The great thing about SO:TP isn't the combat, but the story. Rarely, do I feel empathic for the charcters in a game, but Spec Ops is a fantastic exception. The game follows Martin Walker and his squad, in an attempt to evacuate the refugees in the now destroyed Dubai because of heavy sandstorms.  As the game progresses, you find out you HAVE to make tough descisions to move on. You realize that true war isn't about right or wrong, but whether the choices you make are intended for the greater good. I won't spoil the endings for you, but the game tells you that YOU did this. YOU could've stopped the senseless acts of violence at any point, but YOU kept going on. Sadly, the multiplayer is dead, therefore I can't comment on that. However, Spec Ops The Line is a great buy if you're looking for a compelling story and a different experience from the ''B-b-bloody screen! SO REAAAAL!'' mainstream war games.

This is for anyone who has yet to purchase TheHunter: Call of the Wild.
So far I have clocked in over 10 hours + playing TheHunter and from what I have seen so far the game has a lot of good, bad, and broken in it.
Bad points:
-The menu doesn’t work half the time, doing something as simple as switching weapons can take me 10-15 min’s just trying to get it to work sometimes.
-Frame rate drops from time to time.(I have a higher end PC)
-Animals get stuck all the time, in my 10+ hours it has happened more than a few times.
One time I wiped out an entire herd, just walked up to them and popped them all one at a time.
-Can fall quite a distance with taking minimal damage, but fall a few inches next to a rock and you die?
-The sound the game makes when you brush up against… brush doesn’t sound right to me. When I walk through brush I turn around time after time because it sounds like it's off in the distance and not me making the noise. Might just be me though but drove me nuts!
-The most success I had hunting was running through the forest, not sneaking. It is still way more realistic than other hunting games, but I shouldn’t be able to jog up a road and drop 5 animals.
-Do not try to switch keybindings or you might get stuck for a bit. If you already messed with the shoot button just scroll down to the bottom and reset everything and don’t touch it until patches fix that monstrosity.
-Few crashes throughout the day.
-Sound sometimes cuts in and out, usually when it’s raining.
-Camo does nothing...
The GOOD!
-Graphics Look AMAZING, game does need to be optimized a bit though.
-It feels like a new game but does keep a lot of the core components of the original game, If you played TheHunter Classic you will feel at home with this game.
-MASSIVE BEAUTIFUL world.
-I am satisfied every time I pull the trigger, and the animal animations are awesome.(when they aren’t stuck running in place from a rock,tree, or one foot hill)

But with all of that the game is still great, I have enjoyed spending the whole day on the game and haven’t felt bored. So for a new buyer I would have to say hold off until they fix a few of the bugs. The game is not unplayable by any means but I feel like some standards need to be held, especially for a $30 game.

The game I never knew i'd like.
Among all the terrible simulator games out there, this one shines out like a diamond, and yet its such a simple idea.
Your a truck driver who starts out with nothing but your drivers license and your own rundown-shack of a home garage, so to start earning money you work as a driver for hire with the employer supplying the truck, but soon enough you have the money to buy your own truck, unlock the free roam mode and start makeing your own deliveries. Later on you can improve your own delivere company and hire other drivers to work for you.
The more you drive the more you level up and unlock more challengeing deliveries, like long distance, fragile, and urgent deliveries or be given more hazardous cargo to transfer like dynamite or diesel.
Also, if your getting bored on the road the game has a built-in radio which plays live broadcasts from an available list of radio channels or you can add your own favorite radio channel from the internet. Theirs also an mp3 player so you can listen to your own tracks or your favorite podcasts.
Mention must also go to the world map, which isnt to actual scale (because that would be quite a pain to drive through) but still is quite amazing in size and includes quite a few beutiful vistas.
Sadly, the game also has a few problems. The AI of other vehicles tends to misbehave every now and then, causeing an unescapable road block at an exit from the highway or hitting my truck at an intersection when they werent supposed to be moveing, landing me a fine, ruining my perfect delivere and just plain frustraiting me. But i seem to have only met with these situations once up to now so there probably pretty rare.
A few nit picks i have are the fact that you barely see any people on the street as you drive through the citys, you do see a few individuals on the street, but i doubt Paris is populated by about 5 people unless everyone else is either driving or at home watching TV.
Also the option to control the camera while the game is paused would be nice, it would make it a lot easier to take screenshots.
All things considered Euro Truck Simulator 2 is definetly a fun game and very much worth the asking price. d(^_^)b

Prepare thine buttox, ye who enter this realm of criticism.
I'm not trying to be a prick here, I just want to be honest about what I actually think and experienced.
While this game has cool GRAYFIX and all that, gameplay is lacking pretty hard.
Here's the generally good stuff;
*Very nice visuals, as I mentioned.
*Even though the world is mostly sand and rock, each territory has nice variety and cool locations to check out.
*Melee combat has a lot of fun moves and contextual things like slamming heads into walls or pushing people over rails to their doom.
*Vehicle combat is satisfying and visceral.
*Story is fairly good, not much to complain about here, except the ending is a bit anticlimactic in my opinion.
*Characters are interesting and memorable.
*Voice acting is superb.
*Low usage of invisible walls, instead uses level design and deadly storms to create boundries, that's a plus in my book.
And here's the rest;
*Poorly balanced, very easy to get very overpowered.
You can reach close to Max (ohoho) level before you leave even the first territory of the game, obviously designed towards being rushed through, which is a bit sad.
*Supplies are extremely abundant, fuel, water, food, ammo, whatever.
Never once did I run out of anything other than water, which I promptly refilled moments later.
Skill upgrades are detrimental to the game, making supplies 'even' more abundant, giving you a ton of health turning you into a tank (combine with good armor and you'll be unstoppable), making combat even easier, etc.
*The only thing that ever got me killed was me being silly where I fell off cliffs or such, oops.
*Melee combat is pizz-easy(yay censorship), even if you use no combat upgrades.
Melee combat also had potential to be a bit more interesting, but for no actual reason everyone fights with their fists, nobody except you has a gun (not counting snipers), and melee weapons are fairly useless and magically break after a handful of hits.
You also can't store melee weapons, not even in your car.
*Vehicle combat is pretty fun and provides some challenge, only real complaint here would be that you'll never ever leave the main vehicle to drive any of the other tons of vehicles available, because you can't bring cumbucket with you on anything else.
*Vehicles handle poorly with keyboard controls, so get a controller if you wanna have more fun driving.
Additonally, vehicle physics are a bit strange, with vehicles uprighting themselves constantly and being near impossible to flip.
*Some vehicle upgrades are a bit silly, for example Armour upgrades where you stick a few guard rails on the side of your car and suddenly it weighs enough to warrant a military tank licence.
You also can't even unlock and purchase the V8 stuff until there's like, 5-10% left of the game to play.
*Gameplay is very (VERY) repetative, all bosses (yes literally all) are copy-pasted with different colours and voice lines.
That is a huge point deduction in my little book.
*Side missions are fun for the first few times, until you realize they're all copy-pasted as well, sadly.
*Sub-par freedom of movement, unbefitting a modern game with a modern engine,
you can only climb specially marked areas, nothing else, not even a belly-high fence.
It feels very primitive and unorganic, especially for a modern 3rd person game.
*Racing is, as you probably would guess by now, pizz-easy.
You either outrace every other driver within 20 seconds or shoot out all their tires within 10 seconds ( ͠° ͟ʖ ͡°)
I can't write much else about it since it nullifies its own existance so quickly.
*Exploring can be fun for eyecandy alone, but don't expect to be rewarded with anything substansial, only generic supplies, and Project Parts here and there, but..
Projects makes the game, once again, even easier, giving you infinite fuel, ammo, water, health refills, etc.
"But hey, it's fun to upgrade strongholds you big meanie!"
So thought I, as I assumed it actually had purpose, but it turns out it has no function whatsoever. None.
Unless you count looking less arze with each stage, but yeah..
*So this is supposed to be related to Fury Road right?
Supposedly, but there are no real ties between the movie and the game, in either direction.
Max himself also acts wildly differently between the movie and the game, it doesn't even seem like they're the same person.
Compared to the movie, in the game barely anybody has guns and Max can't fight anywhere near as good in the movie as he does in the game.
But now I'm stepping towards reviewing the movie instead of the game so let's drop it here shall we.
All in all, if you like Mad Max, you'll get a thrill or two out of this generally casual game, but it's certainly not worth full price, it's more along the lines of 15-20 euros.

I did not enjoy Spec Ops: The Line, and I think you should play it.
It has stodgy gameplay, and is ocassionally punishing. The experience is not pleasureable. Equally, the narrative makes you uncomfortable at best, sick at worst.
All of this is a good thing.
I won't go into spoilers, because this is something you need to experience, but I hope I can get across what this game is in the abstract sense. Spec Ops: The Line questions the typical bro shooter experience whilst, at the same time, aping a lot of that genre's trappings. However, its narrative turns the whole thing on its head and doesn't positively reinforce you as the All American Hero that other games in this genre do. Instead, it makes you feel filthy for doing exactly the same thing that Call of Duty or one of the many hundred other shooters does. On those merits alone it is probably worth your time.
The crowning achievement of this game is that in turning the narrative conventions of games which aren't ever really lauded for them in the first place, Spec Ops: The Line tells us how important plot, scenario and characters are to this medium, even if people want to pretend they're not. As I said, I did not enjoy this experience. It wasn't rewarding or fun. It was the feelshit game of 2012, and it's made me not want to play another shooter again.

I think that now would be a good time to write a review on Rust as there is massive controversy if FacePunch have ruined their game or if they have infact launched it to new heights and where they plan on taking it in the future with the infamous devblog 158, that and I've had a good bit of experience over the past 8 months playing this game on and off.
Rust is one of if not thee best survival game out there. You start off naked, literally butt naked on the shore with a torch and a rock. You are completely stranded and must find food and shelter to survive and thrive. The only way to thrive in this game is to team up with some fellow nakeds, playing solo in Rust is not the best idea and I've had plenty of first hand experience so take it from me.
Once you've built your base you must defend it, but sadly when you go off it may not be there in the morning. One thing people love doing in this game is offline raid. Just a heads up, be prepared for your blood to boil when you get raided. Something about working your♥♥♥♥♥of to build a base and coming on with plans to improve it but just to find out some 10 year old Russian kid has set a light to it invokes some kind of anger that you have never felt towards a video game.
I'm going to give you some free 'pro' tips which you don't have to be 'pro' to know it's really just common sense:
1. Don't trust anyone, not even a naked!
2. Watch your back at all times... ALT + Mouse!
3. Bears and wolves are not friendly, neither are boars... they will molest you, quite literally!
4. Don't type in Global chat, all you will receive is abuse and 10 year olds calling you unimaginable names!
Now I'm going to move onto the huge controversy that is DevBlog 158. Firstly I want to say that I get why people are angry with this update and that yes it has made us have to totally reconsider the way we build and the way we play with base defense and construction but it doesn't mean that this update is bad. Before the update was released everyone knew how to stop people from getting on their base, and that was simply to put down a tool cupboard and block it off... but now anyone, including fresh spawns can mine a tree with their little rock and build stairs all the way to the top or all around it. The answer to people getting mad about this is now we just have to get more creative with our base builds, if anything this is what the next step is. It is not the end of Rust but infact just a completely new era of base building and defense.
P.S this is only my second review so go easy, I may add to this review in the future if necessary or if any new DevBlogs get released that change the gameplay dramatically.

Though my only complaint is that the game is a tad bit too...slow. Grindy. It takes quite a while to manage enough money to kickstart your bussiness and actually have people working for you. And it takes a pretty long while to level up enough to be able to buy other types of trucks. It felt weird that by the end-game I had 40+ employees raking in millions in a day and I was still driving one of the first few trucks you can buy.
Other than that, for some relaxing enjoyable evenings, definitely a recommend from me.

Life is Strange: Before the Storm is everything and more than I could have expected from a prequel to one of my favorite, and most affecting, games. The only person to whom I would not recommend this game is someone who hasn't played the original, not because this game is difficult to follow, but because the tiny flourishes that honor the original Life is Strange would be missed and that would be a shame.
The familiar sets of Arcadia Bay are present to be explored again, but from the perspective of Chloe, three years before the events of Life is Strange. As before, the settings display a believable, lived-in world. While the grafitti might not be realistic, per se, it is often authentic to the tenor of the scene, telling us more of Chloe's story. All around are props and pieces for Chloe to comment on, using some great writing and a wry delivery to add depth to the already beautiful graphics and arresting lighting effects.
I was worried when I heard that the actor who had voiced Chloe in the original Life is Strange was unavailable due to a SAG-AFTRA strike, but I found her replacement more than adequate. While there were moments when I missed the original actor's ugly/beautiful commitment to expressing the rawest of emotions with such edge and passion, the actor they chose for this game instead lends an excellent cynical bite to Chloe.
A small but persistent detraction from the actor's performance was the distracting choice to have all of Chloe's thoughts sound like she's talking into a naked microphone in an empty bathroom. The echoing effect felt cheap, a throwback to a movie from the 60's or something. I think audiences are used to characters narrating their thoughts. We can generally tell when they're actually talking to other characters or for only our benefit.
A tremendous number of details litter the world, foreshadwing the events of the first game. Backstory is filled in, rewarding those who played the first game and remember the reference, but none of it is required for enjoying the story; though, Chloe's fixation on Max might seem outsized (or even pathological) to someone who wandered into Before the Storm without having played the original, first.
Chloe's journal, much like Max's from the original Life is Strange, is funny, moving and expresses a level of honesty and vulnerability rarely seen in games. Before Life is Strange, I ignored almost all lore in any video game I ever played, only using a journal to keep track of quests. In these games I relish new entries, often stopping in mid-exploration to read the latest.
Though I'm more than twice the age of the two leads in this game, their dramas and challenges still ring authentic. Even if years have given me perspective and experience has taught me that everything that end begins again, and everything that begins must end, I'm still taken with the vulnerability expressed by Chloe and, ultimately, her friend Rachel. A good story is a good story, regardless of the ages or backgrounds or preferences of the characters, and Life is Strange: Before the Storm has excellent characters.
Much like the teen age years themselves, the dailog does frequently feel disjointed. Tone varies wildly within a scene. Often, noticable pauses, not within the lines themselves (i.e. pausing for dramatic effect), but between characters speaking make exchanges feel awkward. If I had to guess, I'd say that they had too few reads of a particular line or choices of dialog available when they finished recording and tried to stitch the threaded conversations together. This is a relatively small criticism, and it was also a distraction in the original Life is Strange; at least it's consistent.
Beyond the well-written dialog and the generally good acting, the highly detailed and characterized sets and great lighting, enable animation, camera angles and music that to levels of story that transcend language.
In this sumptuous experience, Life is Strange: Before the Storm also follows in the steps of the original, by beautifully illustrating the more bitter than sweet path that lies ahead for Chloe.

★★★★★ - "Do not miss this game"
PROS:
- Huge content, there is just so much to do. Including Story Missions, Wasteland Missions, Death Run (Races), Scavenging (Looting), camps to build, camps to take down, mines to detect, objects to destroy and much more.
- Combat, yes it follows the mould of the Arkham games and Shadow of Mordor but its even more satisfying in my eyes. Theres no gadgets, just your fists, a shiv or other enemy weapons. Its brutal, you feel every blow and it makes for many satisfying moments as you activate fury mode or improvise with your environment.
- Magnum Opus, by far the best part of this game is the desire to grind look in the way of scrap to build up the ultimate battle machine. Ive never felt this in any racer or simulation I've ever played but here your car counts for everything and customisation is very detailed.
- Racing, most of the games moments result in you trying to survive in your car as you pass patrols or take on the story/side missions. This is fast and frantic. At first its hard but once you build up your car you feel like a total badass.
- The game is very clever at making the most of all its options as you must meet requirements to continue the story. Some people might not like this but it helped immersion for me as i can lose interest in these open world games.
- Chumbucket, he's a delightful character who accompanies you, fixing your car and giving tips.
- Optimisation, like many I put off this game due to WB recent messes but Avalanche have done a fine job and runs smooth as butter.
- Beautiful environment, the wasteland is ugly but its vast and ultimately stunning as a result. An odd beauty.
- Storms, these raid you game and unpredictable moments. They are intense.
- Camera mode, this mode is  really detailed. It brings out the games beauty and the photographer in you.
- Max himself has a pretty decent levelling system in two ways also.
CONS:
- So the story is okay, its pacing is strange. Its sudden and didn't feel very long, I preferred the wasteland missions to be honest.
- Characters, another minor moan that the characters were pretty dense. They're bold but other than Max and Chumbucket they failed to provide any real solid moments.
- My only major gripe is that some of the meetings with friendly wastelanders are totally pointless. They are meant to serve a few purposes, give you loot, give you intel on camps and to ask a favour in order to gain secret loot. Now the interactions are all very samey and feel like a total after thought. The characters all look the same and are poorly detailed. The voice actors are pretty much the same for each and there reasoning is daft. I would have preferred if they were left out!
VERDICT?
Mad Max is my game of 2015. Caught me by surprise. Its immensely satisfying and very immersive but above all its value for money. Im nearly 50 hours in at this point and still have side missions and camps I want to finish completing.

I have played DayZ since the Mod days and have red every single devblog/status update from the developers.
As I am writing this review the game is in alpha (0.62)
Read the description and EA warnings carefully. Think twise before buying a Early Access title.
It`s Risky.
I am not going review every single aspect of the game but point out things that I feel are important.
DayZ is awesome but it is not for everybody. It`s harsh, punishing and buggy but still incredible immersive.
I recommend to watch Youtube videos or Twitch streams of the game so you know how the game plays.
Basicly it`s a FPS game + Survival simulator in its core. You shoot and melee but the hook is in the atmosphere and unscripted nature of the game. Its very player driven so you cannot really know how things will go. You can for example talk yourself out of situations which is suprisingly rewarding.
There is different play styles for the game and you have to choose it yourself. Very little hand holding. You will need to research and online map will help too.
At beginning you will probably fail and die a lot but after you learn how to play the game, getting geared up and fed becomes quite easy. Later you will still probably fail and die a lot but you understand your mistakes. Research and practice and you will survive.
Some people like to kill on sight, some like to be friendly and others just simply play sneaky and try to avoid player interaction completely. I mostly prefer playing sneaky and loot weapons and equipment to hidden stashes.
People complain about K.O.S mentality but in my opinions it gives the game that extra level of horror that it needs. You can never know when somebody is watching you or attacks you without any warning. You are not 100% safe anywhere.
I love it that there is bandits roaming around the apocalyptic world of Chernarus. You don`t have to hunt for player encounters because there are so many doing it already. You can choose a peaceful play style that you only return fire. Which can be rewarding.
You can set up camps and you can also steal stuff from other peoples camps. Camps and cars are persistent on the servers but your character disappears from the game when you log out.
This is good and bad thing. For more casual players it is good thing that you can just log out and all carried gear is safe. This also creates a situation that anybody can log in and out everywhere anytime. Which is creepy and super unrealistic.
Many survival games have sleeper mechanism where the players characters stays in the world. Its a good mechanism but it can lead to the situation that you worry about your character too much and/or you cannot have long break from the game because otherwise you get wrecked.
In DayZ you can have long breaks without worrying is your character alive or dead. This really depends from you is it good or bad.
At the moment it is so that anobody can walk into your tents and take your stuff but barrels can be hidden so they are 100% invisible unless player is close by and opens inventory.
That is how I play. I hide all my important stuff to barrels and hide them well. If I die I can go to my secret hideout and gear up fast. This also gives some end game activity to keep stashes well equiped.
Player interaction are rare which creates this build up when they happen.
Do you try to kill? do you run away? Do you try to speak to them? Do you take them as prisoners? Rob them? Torture them? Try to start a conversation and get new friends? This is completely your choice and responsibility.
If you are creative and social you can have super fun time in this game. Playing solo just surviving and avoiding players is fun too if you are into that kind of thing.
Dayz can be super exciting or super boring. It really depends of you.
DayZ was originally suppose to be a survival simulator for military and this shows. For me this is the best game if I want be afraid or test my skills in panic situation.
I have also felt bad when killing a player. If the games immersion works for you can have powerful experiences and strong feelings in this game.
There is lots of "down time" in DayZ. you just walk or run to other cities and nothing special happens. This can give sometimes a bit empty feeling. But as development (slowly) progress Chernarus is becoming more and more lively.
DayZ can be quite entertaining to watch and many people make videos of the game. It has this way of producing experiences and stories which are fun to share.
There is lots of hate and false information spreading about DayZ so i am trying to clear some things up:
The original creator of DayZ Dean Hall DID NOT run away with money.
When Dayz Standalone was first released to Early Access Dean Hall always said: "Do not buy this game".
Do the research and you can find this out for yourself.
DayZ went to Early Access too early. It was corporate decision from the behalf of Bohemia Interactive. It was a test if DayZ is still relevant.
They noticed that it is still relevant  (sold well)  and started to build the engine. This has caused lots of frustration in the players and later they have admitted that it was a mistake to go Early Access so early.
DayZ development has been slow and simply super late from their original road maps.
There is also a reasons for that.
One main point people seem to forget that from the beginning DayZ has been an experimental project and it`s new a demanding type of game to develope.
The scope of the game is huge (large map, many players, zombies,moddable ) but at the same time the gameplay mechanics are detailed and varied.
Most of the Early Access survival games are not ready because it is difficult and a new thing to develope a game engine that can do something like DayZ is trying to do.
I entertain myself by following development of Early Access games and I`m interested to know who will be able to build a working Survival game engine.
Because building working survival game engine is difficult many survival game developers don`t even try to finish their games. Reign of Kings, ARK: Survival evolved, Life is Feudal, developers of these games basicly just announced their game is ready eventhough they are not. Either they cannot or they simply don`t want to finish their games.
Many people also wonder why some aspects worked and run more smoothly in the mod than in the standalone.
Arma 2 was built so that it mainly runs on the clients PC. This way there is not so much pressure on the servers. Good system but easily exploitable by cheaters and losers also known as "hackers" Hackers basicly ruined DayZ mod for me.
Community fought back well with private servers and active admins though but this forced the developers to build DayZ Standalone so that it mainly runs on the servers.
This is the reason why the DayZ mod in some ways runs better that the Standalone.
But for DayZ i see hope because they are openly admitting their problems and using their time and efforts to fix the problems and build this Enfusion engine.
Everybody who follows DayZ knows the amount hate DayZ gets. Partly I understand it. Development has been slow and frustrating but we also knew what we were getting into.
Many of the hateful opinions and arguments stated are simply from people who don`t know what they are talking about.
People should be thankful to Dean Hall. He created DayZ mod. Mod is free and he did not get any salary from making it. That mod really put speed to the birth of the survival game genre and it is an awesome thing.
He have made and huge positive impact to gaming and there is no denying that.
As I said do research of the game before you buy it (As you are doing by reading these reviews) and maybe dont buy it yet. Wait for a 6-12 months. It will be alot more easily enjoyable. Watch youtube videos/streams and see if this is a good game for you. For me it is.
