You play as a slave worker in in a totalitarian vision of the european union who is not permitted to leave the cabin of his truck until he has died working for the state. His every move and action are tracked by speed cameras allowing the government to know immediately the instant he ever breaks the slightest traffic law.
Seriously though, this is a fantastic game. There's nothing more relaxing than just spacing out while driving across the enormous map listening to some decent music. I'd definately recommend going into the settings and turning off the speed limiter and the fatigue simulation as the game is much more enjoyable without these. I also found it helpful to set the quicksave button to tab so I can easily back up the game before my reckless driving gets me into an accident.
The only downside I can think of is the sense of sameness in the places you visit. I mean a lot of them are really memorable, driving through the swiss alps is very scenic and it's very enjoyable driving along the atlantic coast, but most towns just feel like the same industrial park arranged in slightly different ways. Sure there are some landmarks in the background but you don't really get to get anywhere near them. I don't so much mind this though as it's truck simulator not a tourism simulator.
This is a game I've played for ages and will continue to play for ages, something I can say about fewer and fewer releases these days

I have now played this game for 951 hours, I've driven 592779 km in game and I'm still playing it!
Believe me when I tell you that I've tried to understand what keeps me playing this game and when I bought this game several years ago I didn't really think I'd like it.
The scenery is beautiful as you drive around in a compressed version of Europe with landscapes reflecting reality and with distinctive landmarks. Just seeing them in game knowing they exist in real life is very nice! SCS have added everything from aircrafts landing and taking off to riverboats and pedestrians to make the game feel alive. SCS also added AI-cars and trucks which you will love to hate! This leads me to the less good things with this game.
ETS2 isn't really a simulator, you drive a truck which seem realistic enough to drive but there are too many things which ETS2 lacks to be called a simulator. Like proper damage, brake wear etc. For anyone playing other simulators, I guess ETS2 feels a bit arcadish. The AI or "Annoying Idiots" as I call them tend to drive very badly at times, for example in roundabouts. The company you own and run is made so simple it would've been better if SCS left it out.
There are as of today three major map addition DLC and a fourth coming soon. ETS2 has numerous other DLC too, everything from cosmetic such as national flags to different kind of cargoes. The map DLC adds new achievements and so does some of the other DLC. I see a danger with SCS releasing too many DLC as the total cost of the game constantly increase. However, you have to consider what SCS gives you for free, such as new cars for the AI to drive around in and other updates. I haven't seen a released game being updated this frequently ever so buying the DLC makes SCS constantly updating ETS2.
If this doesn't convince you, download the demo, buy the game on a sale but you should treat you to this game.

I have played DayZ since the Mod days and have red every single devblog/status update from the developers.
As I am writing this review the game is in alpha (0.62)
Read the description and EA warnings carefully. Think twise before buying a Early Access title.
It`s Risky.
I am not going review every single aspect of the game but point out things that I feel are important.
DayZ is awesome but it is not for everybody. It`s harsh, punishing and buggy but still incredible immersive.
I recommend to watch Youtube videos or Twitch streams of the game so you know how the game plays.
Basicly it`s a FPS game + Survival simulator in its core. You shoot and melee but the hook is in the atmosphere and unscripted nature of the game. Its very player driven so you cannot really know how things will go. You can for example talk yourself out of situations which is suprisingly rewarding.
There is different play styles for the game and you have to choose it yourself. Very little hand holding. You will need to research and online map will help too.
At beginning you will probably fail and die a lot but after you learn how to play the game, getting geared up and fed becomes quite easy. Later you will still probably fail and die a lot but you understand your mistakes. Research and practice and you will survive.
Some people like to kill on sight, some like to be friendly and others just simply play sneaky and try to avoid player interaction completely. I mostly prefer playing sneaky and loot weapons and equipment to hidden stashes.
People complain about K.O.S mentality but in my opinions it gives the game that extra level of horror that it needs. You can never know when somebody is watching you or attacks you without any warning. You are not 100% safe anywhere.
I love it that there is bandits roaming around the apocalyptic world of Chernarus. You don`t have to hunt for player encounters because there are so many doing it already. You can choose a peaceful play style that you only return fire. Which can be rewarding.
You can set up camps and you can also steal stuff from other peoples camps. Camps and cars are persistent on the servers but your character disappears from the game when you log out.
This is good and bad thing. For more casual players it is good thing that you can just log out and all carried gear is safe. This also creates a situation that anybody can log in and out everywhere anytime. Which is creepy and super unrealistic.
Many survival games have sleeper mechanism where the players characters stays in the world. Its a good mechanism but it can lead to the situation that you worry about your character too much and/or you cannot have long break from the game because otherwise you get wrecked.
In DayZ you can have long breaks without worrying is your character alive or dead. This really depends from you is it good or bad.
At the moment it is so that anobody can walk into your tents and take your stuff but barrels can be hidden so they are 100% invisible unless player is close by and opens inventory.
That is how I play. I hide all my important stuff to barrels and hide them well. If I die I can go to my secret hideout and gear up fast. This also gives some end game activity to keep stashes well equiped.
Player interaction are rare which creates this build up when they happen.
Do you try to kill? do you run away? Do you try to speak to them? Do you take them as prisoners? Rob them? Torture them? Try to start a conversation and get new friends? This is completely your choice and responsibility.
If you are creative and social you can have super fun time in this game. Playing solo just surviving and avoiding players is fun too if you are into that kind of thing.
Dayz can be super exciting or super boring. It really depends of you.
DayZ was originally suppose to be a survival simulator for military and this shows. For me this is the best game if I want be afraid or test my skills in panic situation.
I have also felt bad when killing a player. If the games immersion works for you can have powerful experiences and strong feelings in this game.
There is lots of "down time" in DayZ. you just walk or run to other cities and nothing special happens. This can give sometimes a bit empty feeling. But as development (slowly) progress Chernarus is becoming more and more lively.
DayZ can be quite entertaining to watch and many people make videos of the game. It has this way of producing experiences and stories which are fun to share.
There is lots of hate and false information spreading about DayZ so i am trying to clear some things up:
The original creator of DayZ Dean Hall DID NOT run away with money.
When Dayz Standalone was first released to Early Access Dean Hall always said: "Do not buy this game".
Do the research and you can find this out for yourself.
DayZ went to Early Access too early. It was corporate decision from the behalf of Bohemia Interactive. It was a test if DayZ is still relevant.
They noticed that it is still relevant  (sold well)  and started to build the engine. This has caused lots of frustration in the players and later they have admitted that it was a mistake to go Early Access so early.
DayZ development has been slow and simply super late from their original road maps.
There is also a reasons for that.
One main point people seem to forget that from the beginning DayZ has been an experimental project and it`s new a demanding type of game to develope.
The scope of the game is huge (large map, many players, zombies,moddable ) but at the same time the gameplay mechanics are detailed and varied.
Most of the Early Access survival games are not ready because it is difficult and a new thing to develope a game engine that can do something like DayZ is trying to do.
I entertain myself by following development of Early Access games and I`m interested to know who will be able to build a working Survival game engine.
Because building working survival game engine is difficult many survival game developers don`t even try to finish their games. Reign of Kings, ARK: Survival evolved, Life is Feudal, developers of these games basicly just announced their game is ready eventhough they are not. Either they cannot or they simply don`t want to finish their games.
Many people also wonder why some aspects worked and run more smoothly in the mod than in the standalone.
Arma 2 was built so that it mainly runs on the clients PC. This way there is not so much pressure on the servers. Good system but easily exploitable by cheaters and losers also known as "hackers" Hackers basicly ruined DayZ mod for me.
Community fought back well with private servers and active admins though but this forced the developers to build DayZ Standalone so that it mainly runs on the servers.
This is the reason why the DayZ mod in some ways runs better that the Standalone.
But for DayZ i see hope because they are openly admitting their problems and using their time and efforts to fix the problems and build this Enfusion engine.
Everybody who follows DayZ knows the amount hate DayZ gets. Partly I understand it. Development has been slow and frustrating but we also knew what we were getting into.
Many of the hateful opinions and arguments stated are simply from people who don`t know what they are talking about.
People should be thankful to Dean Hall. He created DayZ mod. Mod is free and he did not get any salary from making it. That mod really put speed to the birth of the survival game genre and it is an awesome thing.
He have made and huge positive impact to gaming and there is no denying that.
As I said do research of the game before you buy it (As you are doing by reading these reviews) and maybe dont buy it yet. Wait for a 6-12 months. It will be alot more easily enjoyable. Watch youtube videos/streams and see if this is a good game for you. For me it is.

PUBG is a much better (still EA) game than ARMA 2 Dayz,  so do not buy any Bohemia products. They are scammers. Survivor stories, or whatever it ended up being called, is better than this game.

★★★★★ - "Do not miss this game"
PROS:
- Huge content, there is just so much to do. Including Story Missions, Wasteland Missions, Death Run (Races), Scavenging (Looting), camps to build, camps to take down, mines to detect, objects to destroy and much more.
- Combat, yes it follows the mould of the Arkham games and Shadow of Mordor but its even more satisfying in my eyes. Theres no gadgets, just your fists, a shiv or other enemy weapons. Its brutal, you feel every blow and it makes for many satisfying moments as you activate fury mode or improvise with your environment.
- Magnum Opus, by far the best part of this game is the desire to grind look in the way of scrap to build up the ultimate battle machine. Ive never felt this in any racer or simulation I've ever played but here your car counts for everything and customisation is very detailed.
- Racing, most of the games moments result in you trying to survive in your car as you pass patrols or take on the story/side missions. This is fast and frantic. At first its hard but once you build up your car you feel like a total badass.
- The game is very clever at making the most of all its options as you must meet requirements to continue the story. Some people might not like this but it helped immersion for me as i can lose interest in these open world games.
- Chumbucket, he's a delightful character who accompanies you, fixing your car and giving tips.
- Optimisation, like many I put off this game due to WB recent messes but Avalanche have done a fine job and runs smooth as butter.
- Beautiful environment, the wasteland is ugly but its vast and ultimately stunning as a result. An odd beauty.
- Storms, these raid you game and unpredictable moments. They are intense.
- Camera mode, this mode is  really detailed. It brings out the games beauty and the photographer in you.
- Max himself has a pretty decent levelling system in two ways also.
CONS:
- So the story is okay, its pacing is strange. Its sudden and didn't feel very long, I preferred the wasteland missions to be honest.
- Characters, another minor moan that the characters were pretty dense. They're bold but other than Max and Chumbucket they failed to provide any real solid moments.
- My only major gripe is that some of the meetings with friendly wastelanders are totally pointless. They are meant to serve a few purposes, give you loot, give you intel on camps and to ask a favour in order to gain secret loot. Now the interactions are all very samey and feel like a total after thought. The characters all look the same and are poorly detailed. The voice actors are pretty much the same for each and there reasoning is daft. I would have preferred if they were left out!
VERDICT?
Mad Max is my game of 2015. Caught me by surprise. Its immensely satisfying and very immersive but above all its value for money. Im nearly 50 hours in at this point and still have side missions and camps I want to finish completing.

This is from the perspective of someone who has been a huge fan of theHunter: Classic for many years and have quite a bit of time and money invested in it.
Call of the Wild is a beautiful game environment and solid hunting mechanics; which will feel familiar to veteran Classic players and not too daunting for new hunters to the 'series'.
I've seen a lot of people ask if this is anything like Cabela's. I would have to say that CotW is FAR superior to Cabela's; but still maintains a 'casual' hunter feel to it.
There are still a few launch issues and bugs however, which really should have been ironed out from the Beta before retail release; including some issues that aren't dissimilar to what has or is being experienced in theHunter: Classic (specifically MP issues).
Pros:
-Gorgeous graphics
-Great sound design
-Reserves are very well designed and visually interesting.
-Dynamic weather system is well implemented.
-Smooth animations and weapons feel like they have weight.
-Players can jump! This might sound ridiculous to put on a pro's list; but it's one of the biggest features I wanted in Classic.
-Stalking animals is MUCH easier. This could also be listed as a Con.
-Progression system with XP, Money and Weapon skill, that will keep you striving to improve.
-MASSIVE hunting reserves.
-Similar game mechanics to Classic, that makes the game familiar for veteran Classic players.
-Good tutorial and hint system for new hunters.
-Much further render distance for all the long-shot enthusiasts.
Cons:
-A few UI issues (unable to click some elements, or non-responsive elements)
-Experienced a couple of crashes due to entering the System Settings menu. (work-around is to change settings, then restart the game. Another suggestion is to disable cloud-sync in Steam).
-Animals aren't as 'hard' when it comes to Spook range and flee distance from weapon firing.
-MP has a few issues. Most noticeably with desync (shooting animals that aren't actually there).
-Joining an MP game can spawn you out of bounds, or with 0 health. (This isn't game breaking from my experience as it respawns you near the host. )
-Can't quit to Main Menu - only to Desktop.
-Can't progress your characters environment/lore/tower unlocks in MP.
-No in-depth stats tracking and weapon skill progression compared to Classic.
-Progression flow is a bit off (Receiving missions and being advised to use specific callers; which you can't yet unlock due to level or money requirements)
-No truRacks system.
-Some may find the game too grindy to unlock new weapons and items
All in all, I would still recommend this game in spite of its launch issues; if you can tolerate a few bugs.
If you are expecting a 100% flawless release, then perhaps give this title a miss until the developers have ironed a few creases out.
I'll happily update this review in the near future to accurately reflect any developer changes to anything listed above; or anything new they introduce.
I hope this helps!

I don't really know what to say. There's a lot of amazing reviews that basically speak my mind; so this'll sound a lot like them.
When I first heard there was a prequel for this game being made I fangirled really hard. As time went on however my expectations did lower a bit. Between the different cast of voice actors and the fact this game was being made by another studio I kind of didn't know what to expect. Well I was blown away to say the least.
Just like the first game I've fallen in love with Chloe almost right from the beginning. Sure I was taken aback by her new voice a bit but it's already grown on me. ( Unlike a certain squad 11 captain.... ) I will say it felt weird at first not being able to time travel; after my first conversation I thought to myself "maybe I should time travel and see if I can try for a better outcome" then I realised there isn't timetravel in the game. It doesn't bother me as much as some people as the timetravel mechanic in the original Life is Strange wasn't the highlight of game for me; it was more of a cool side thing.
The first episode itself was much longer than I thought it'd be. (Took me over 3 hours to finish) Judging by that we could end up getting another 8+ hours from the other two episodes which is pretty great. I love the chance to go back into the LiS universe and I've been dying to meet Rachel ever since I first saw her posters hanging up in the school and heard about how Chloe seemed to idolize her. I really like Rachel's character so far. She really shows how even the most perfect of people can have their own demons on the inside. I already ship her and Chloe so much.
Despite being made by a different studio, Before the Storm really has captured that Life is Strange feel. Not just visually, but the soundtrack, the characters, and the emotions just this one episode has made me feel. The soundtrack itself is great, it's got that Life is Strange vibe but more suited to Chloe's personality. It's in the same universe but centered around a different character so to speak. Kind of like how the Lord of the Rings and the Hobbit soundtracks go hand-in-hand yet are so distinct from one another.  It's crazy how my opinions of characters have changed so much meeting them for the first time in this game compared to when I met them the first time in Life is Strange. I have such a deeper understanding of them. For example
I also enjoyed meeting the new characters, I love some of them already and can't wait to see more of them.
I'm probably gonna be bawling my eyes out as I come closer and closer to the end of this game; the first episode already shook me up. I'm serisouly stoked to see what happens. Amazing work so far Deck Nine!
----- Conclusion -----
All in all, hella good job Deck Nine! ;P
P.S. If anyone who hasn't played the original LiS picks this up, I would love to hear your thoughts. It would be interesting to see what someone who hasn't experienced this universe before thinks of the characters and the game itself.

ETS2 is a very casual truck driving sim. You manage your own company with garages all over Europe, and buy trucks and hire drivers to get things running. While your drivers will find jobs by themselves, and do not really need your input, you can either do jobs for other companies, or do the jobs with your own truck. Or simply go freeroaming if you're in the mood for that.
The driving itself works great. Easy controls and fairly realistic physics. I have no complaints here.
Graphics are good. Not great, but decent enough for me. Music and sound effect are also good, but there's no music while you drive. However, you can either add mp3s to a playlist, or tune in on internet radio channels, if you want to.
I only have two issues with this game, none are gamebreaking:
1. Traffic AI is sometimes kinda silly, but they are constantly working on improving it.
2. No cloud save. This means that if I want to play in my house, then continue in my apartment, I have to copy save files and bring them with me. Very annoying for those of us who lives two places with a stationary PC both places.
If you'd like a casual driving sim, without the big challenges, this is the game for you. I recommend you get the Going East DLC too, as it adds more countries, and remember to check out the Scandinavia DLC when it gets released. The rest of the DLCs are just paintjobs for your trucks, I don't recommend spending a lot of money here, get them while on sale, which they often are.

I think it's time for me to redo my old review about this game. When i wrote the first review i had around 2-300ish hours or so on the game. Now i got a bit more hours added, i think that i can pinpoint pro's and con's more precise and easily.
The game itself is very enjoyable and relaxing. Having the option to drive different types of trucks, being able to customize them with the big amount of DLCs you can get for the game, really makes it refreshing and varying. That being said, if you don't like doing the same thing over and over again, this game might make you bored really easy, since it is a very repetetive game. There are three things you'll do, which this game almost consists of; that is, pickup your trailer, drive to your destination, park and dropoff your trailer. Then, you'll do it again, but this time to another location. The game is fun if you're into trucks and driving, and with a steering wheel (g27 e.g) it can be even more fun, and quite educational. The reason it can be educational (was for me) is that you get the same situations in-game like you would in real life. Being that you're driving with realism in mind, you got to pay attention to the road, traffic, signs, etc. And you could learn a lot when reversing with a trailer.
Positive things:
- Very detailed trucks
- Great steering wheel/headtracking support
- Lots of unique and real-life places to visit
- Big variety of trailer types and loads
- Beautiful graphics
- Internal radio/music-player
- Challenging roads/drop-off spots.
- Tons of mods for the game
- Lots of customization options
Negative things:
- Unrealistic truck physics/suspension
- No visible damage on truck/trailer
- No tyresmoke, tyreslip sound
- A bit too much unnecessary paintjob dlcs
- No ability to change color of roofbar, bullbar etc.
- Unrealistic high beam enlightenment/light zone
- Not the best of horn/truck sounds
Thank you for supporting Linux with this awesome game!

Gameplay wise, Spec Ops: The Line is a standard third person cover shooter. The graphics and sound are all outstanding. Even though Bulletstorm sorta did it first, the environments are still interesting. The real star here is the story. Again, credit where credit is due, this is essentially Heart of Darkness (or Apocalypse Now if you prefer) the game. If you've never read it, this will almost certainly be one of the most intense gaming experiences you've ever had ("the feels"). If you have? It's a slight twist on one of the most thought provoking stories ever written. While the story can be cynically boiled down to "you followed orders...you monster!", it's the journey, not the destination. Much like Dear Esther, Shadow of the Colossus or Journey, this is a prime example of the power and importance of story telling in a video game. Naturally, I have to recommend the source material over the game, but you owe it to yourself to play Spec Ops: The Line.

An early game review:
So i think most people reviewing this negatively are being way dramatic about the state of the game. It's a bit buggy but it's nothing that cant be fixed with a good few patches.
This game is one of the most beautiful games out there right now, runs fine for me personally, quite well really.
Points starting from bad to good:
- Yeah there are bugs, for sure. Menu buggitude, people sayin bears are bugged a bit too. And whenever i would harvest an animal my game settings would get reset. Im hopeful these things can get fixed pretty easily tho. As far as stuck animals go, as a game developer, problems like this can be really difficult to solve and are common in a ton of games. I think they should maybe look into it but im not going to blame them too hard if i see the occasional stuck animal. i only encountered one stuck animal in my play time and it was just a dinky rabbit.
Edit: After some more time i have noticed a few more stuck animals which is unfortunate but not game breaking really, id say youd end up seeing one stuck animal per 2 hours or so of gameplay. Some more bugs as well such as scope clipping and bugged animation on scope zoom, some fps drops wen tracking animals long distances using the phone thing, and game freezing occasionally, sometimes recovering other times not.
- Some people talking about the game being too easy and too many animals but id like to know what game they were playing because for me, trying to get a good shot and then not being able to and spooking the animals and then having to track em down for like an hour without seeing anything,, i dont think the game was too overflowing with animals. However there are a lot more animal calls sometimes it seems, which i think is fine and turning off the audio visualzation is good idea as well.
Edit - A little more detail on this: Sometimes there can definitely be quite a few animal calls, a lot more than were in theHunter classic. Personally i dont really have a problem with this as they are just calls, and they arent distracting if you have the vocal visualizations off. While running around you are likely to never actually see any of the animals calling unless you run into a field where there may be a few animals grazing (but this doesnt feel unrealistic to me at least) but it does hark on to my point about sound where animal calls are louder than they should be really. Maybe putting the calls on a seperate audio slider or something. Its also important to NOTE: if you hunt out an area and scare off animals its totally quiet out there. So in all, i still dont feel there are "too many" animals as the likelyhood of encountering one is not astronomically high or anything.
- I've seen some people say its lacking content? But from what i can tell the maps are huuge and vary pretty good in the areas and there are a fair number of animals to hunt right now, as well as a fair amount of weaponry. The game is not like a full price AAA release, its half that in fact, and, if you were to compare it to theHunter classic, this game is a bargain. If you wanted to do any of the stuff in this game in classic youd be paying for a membership and paying real money like $5 per weapon. The game has plenty of content for $30 with more to come in dlcs.
-This game however, does not have a lot of the features that classic has in terms of competitions and leaderboards and community. I think this is intentional and likely to stay that way. Both games serve a purpose, and the purpose of this game is not to be exactly like the last one, but a more standalone experience not tied down to microtransactions and a separate launcher with community stuff and accounts and all that jazz. This may turn some of the more hardcore hunters off, and if it does, then i dont think this game is for you.
- Does not have free look to detach look direction from walk direction. That would be a veryyy nice thing to have and i dont know why it isnt in already.
- Uses a progression tree in terms of weapon perks and various skills. This is a highly subjective way of doing it but i think it is a fine way to do it. I dont think its anything special and is highly debatable but i dont think it should be a turn off. It just allows for progression of the game and your character, which by the way, theres just about no character choice options... this easily seems like one of the most underdeveloped things. but eh.
- Sound is very immersive and well realized. Ive seen some people complain about the sound being bad somehow but this is crazy talk if you ask me. Maybe im just not hardcore enough of a hunter to really understand but i think some people are just babies.
Edit: while i still think sound is very good, some things ive noticed after more time are music cutting out randomly, bear calls being cut short, and sounds of russling and animal calls being a bit too loud.
- A quick graphics review: The game is gorgeous. Hands down the best nature ive ever seen in a game. If i had to gripe about graphics at all as a hardcore graphics enthusiast, shadows are pretty blocky, but they can get away with this because there is a ton of foliage to break up the shadows so that you wont notice unless you reeallyyy look at them. Still a higher res shadow option could be nice, but i think they used resources freed by using lower quality shadows for more impactful features elsewhere. The clouds if you look at them too hard are obviously just moving textures in the sky but whatever really the game is about nature not clouds and they look pretty good when not viewed under scrutiny. Water reflections are a bit low res.. i know reflections can be intense but at least an option for some higher quality reflections would be nice. Also about reflections, and this can be an issue with water effects in a lot of games, around edges of objects where water is in the background there is a weird halo around them, not a super big deal but very noticable. No option for anti aliasing??? this is a weird one but i guess there is AA applied somewhere at least, maybe tied to quality setting, but not cool at any rate. That being said, i havent really had any issues with aliasing, its not a jag fest like some games are. And you would think this would be too with all the foliage. And don't even get me started on the foliage, its so dense and detailed and even reacts to animals and players to the point where animals leave paths through the grass as they walk, easily the best foliage ive ever seen in a game. Overall, Beautiful game.
I think that covers most things.
Conclusion:
The game is pretty good for the price. A must have if you like walking simulation and hunting experiences.
Perhaps hold off for a month or two until some of the more glaring bugs and finicky-ness is sorted out if that kind of thing bothers you.

theHunter: Call of the Wild,
I'd give her 5 stars. Not entirely sure what all the hate and absolute disgust is all about, I have found nothing but greatness in the product.
Yes, sure there are a few issues here and there, but nothing that patches won't be able to iron out.
Right, just a brief reason why I rate COTW so highly with a pro's and con's list below.
Call of the Wild has some of the most beautiful, calming and pleasuring forests, plains, rivers and mountains to explore, the ambiance the game creates in that regard is utter beauty.
The animals themselves are really great to look at and stalk. Sure the Buck do not have the hugest varity of Antlers out there, but i am curious to see what the future holds in that regard.
Thus far each hunt has been majestic in its own way. Each hunt has brought about its own challenges and adventure with it. From hunting Red Fox to Various types of Deers, some animals are in a herd which force me to choose wisely and play my tactics carefully if i wish to leave with the best scoring animal, those that travel alone are often very sneaky and sometimes downright genius, though with enough patience and technique, the hunt will reward you with the sight of beauty and the pleasure of the one shot kill. (To which I have noticed a lot of people complaining about 3 shots to bring down a buck.... I have yet to have such an issue. 12 shots fired. 12 hits, 12 kills.
Anyhow onto the Pro's and Con's list.
Con's:
1) Small game and Big game create the same noise while passing through foilage/bushes which is hugely missleading or should i say somewhat confusing, I have caught myself doing 360s with the rifle aimed, looking for that deer that made that racket while passing through the bushes, to see only later that it was merely a rabbit. Very odd for a Rabbit to make such a loud crash through the bushes.
2) A couple of glitches while in Map mode, You have to constantly zoom in and out to see the borders of various places on the map, which isnt very helpful while trying to complete missions, but by no means a game breaker.
3) A few animals are still getting glitched/stuck on various rocks and or tree trunks, Thus far has only happend twice out of the 12 animals i have had the opportunity of taking down.
That is really it thus far.
Pros:
1) The beautifully designed Forests, Plains, Rivers, Mountains etc etc are a sight for sore eyes. I have no issues getting lost in them and just strolling through watching gazing Buck stroll through the wild.
2) The ambiance in the wild is fantastic, it really makes you feel as if you are in the wild, from the birds chirping, to the foxes howling (Squeeking?) to the birds flying out of the bushes while you hastly run past. The wind that blows over the plains and the odd time Thunder strikes the silent evening sky behind you. Its brilliantly done.
3) The Animals are very goodlooking, From the Rabbit through to the various Deers (I have yet to find myself a Bear or any other larger Game, thus i have to hold that comment). They act very well, and I have yet to have issues with them spooking just to stop a few meters later. When they spook, my god do they run, and stop very very far away. Have had some fantastic 2 hour marches following those Tracks.
4) The whole feeling to the game is great, It is not elite hardcore, but is by no means like a Call of Duty Hunter. I see tons of complaints that the game is far too arcade like, but I cannot seem to grasp what that means. The hunts are by no means easy, You can spend a very long time tracking down your prey, very easily spook him off and very easily miss your shot. (Unless ofcourse you are using your rifle like its a machine gun and shooting every animal in sight... well then you have no idea what hunting is about).
Thats about it for now, I will ofcourse update the review at a later stage.
All in all,
I will be spending tons of hours on this beaut of a game.

The game I never knew i'd like.
Among all the terrible simulator games out there, this one shines out like a diamond, and yet its such a simple idea.
Your a truck driver who starts out with nothing but your drivers license and your own rundown-shack of a home garage, so to start earning money you work as a driver for hire with the employer supplying the truck, but soon enough you have the money to buy your own truck, unlock the free roam mode and start makeing your own deliveries. Later on you can improve your own delivere company and hire other drivers to work for you.
The more you drive the more you level up and unlock more challengeing deliveries, like long distance, fragile, and urgent deliveries or be given more hazardous cargo to transfer like dynamite or diesel.
Also, if your getting bored on the road the game has a built-in radio which plays live broadcasts from an available list of radio channels or you can add your own favorite radio channel from the internet. Theirs also an mp3 player so you can listen to your own tracks or your favorite podcasts.
Mention must also go to the world map, which isnt to actual scale (because that would be quite a pain to drive through) but still is quite amazing in size and includes quite a few beutiful vistas.
Sadly, the game also has a few problems. The AI of other vehicles tends to misbehave every now and then, causeing an unescapable road block at an exit from the highway or hitting my truck at an intersection when they werent supposed to be moveing, landing me a fine, ruining my perfect delivere and just plain frustraiting me. But i seem to have only met with these situations once up to now so there probably pretty rare.
A few nit picks i have are the fact that you barely see any people on the street as you drive through the citys, you do see a few individuals on the street, but i doubt Paris is populated by about 5 people unless everyone else is either driving or at home watching TV.
Also the option to control the camera while the game is paused would be nice, it would make it a lot easier to take screenshots.
All things considered Euro Truck Simulator 2 is definetly a fun game and very much worth the asking price. d(^_^)b

Gameplay wise, Spec Ops: The Line is a standard third person cover shooter. The graphics and sound are all outstanding. Even though Bulletstorm sorta did it first, the environments are still interesting. The real star here is the story. Again, credit where credit is due, this is essentially Heart of Darkness (or Apocalypse Now if you prefer) the game. If you've never read it, this will almost certainly be one of the most intense gaming experiences you've ever had ("the feels"). If you have? It's a slight twist on one of the most thought provoking stories ever written. While the story can be cynically boiled down to "you followed orders...you monster!", it's the journey, not the destination. Much like Dear Esther, Shadow of the Colossus or Journey, this is a prime example of the power and importance of story telling in a video game. Naturally, I have to recommend the source material over the game, but you owe it to yourself to play Spec Ops: The Line.

I'll admit that I was somewhat skeptical when I heard that Ashly Burch would not be reprising her role as Chloe Price but you know what?  After playing the game I have to admit that Rhianna DeVries did a pretty good job of capturing the essence of the character and recreating some of the magic from the original game.  Is this the same Chloe that we know and love?  Yes and no, but that's okay because this is a different game which takes place during a different point in the character's life.  Either way I still adore my rage-filled angsty darling.  The game also managed to get me emotionally invested in Rachel Amber despite knowing her ultimate fate.
All that said, this game is not without its issues.  I have to launch it via Steam Big Picture to get my Logitech F710 controller to work properly.  I also had to switch over to using a mouse when selecting Chloe's new wardrobe in order to access the bonus outfits that I got for pre-ordering.   But aside from that?  I love "Life is Strange: Before the Storm" just as much as the game which came before it.

The hopes I had for this game were almost non-existent, to be honest. When the prequel to one of my favourite games, Life is Strange, was announced, something just felt wrong. The original development team has been hard at work with a new title, so Life is Strange: Before the Storm, has been developed by another company entirely. This sure raises a lot of questions…
Read full review at
The most obvious flaw with this new episodic title is the lack of time Deck Nine, the development team behind it, had to create it. The constant recycling of environments seems to be a homage at first, but it soon becomes tiresome. Writing is also all over the place, and what used to be subtle and interesting in Life is Strange, has been turned into obvious. Nothing is up for interpretation; every single thing is spoon-fed to the player by being written in big bold letters.
Upon inspecting a motorcycle, Chloe says:
Really? Was that the best way to convey she is going through some lonely times? The same thing happens with every theme featured, but probably the one I liked least was the main character’s sexuality. Don’t get me wrong, I think it’s great that we have a lesbian protagonist, but the way this topic is handled is way too bold and uninspired, which is a huge lost opportunity.
Gameplay is much duller than in the original title, too… As Chloe, unlike Max, has no crazy superpowers, everything the players do is walk around and talk to people. This could be good enough if environments were rich and conversations were properly written, but as already stated, none of those can be found anywhere is Before the Storm. The path developers took to turn these features more “gamey” is what they’ve named Backtalk, a “risk/reward conversation mode that allows Chloe to use her barbed tongue to provoke or get her way”. Let’s translate that into actual mechanics: a character says a line, and the player must pick the appropriate answer of the three possibilities shown on-screen in order to get closer to winning the argument. The correct answer is whichever includes a word that the other character has previously said. It’s THAT dumb. No creative answers, no trying to foresee replies, no nothing.
Before the Storm is extremely similar to Life is Strange, and that sometimes plays in favor of the prequel. The graphics, for instance, look as vibrant and breath-taking as they did in the first game. Hand-drawn textures and beautiful lighting effects create a stunning visual experience, indeed. It does have many technical issues, though. I’ve been lucky enough not to experience any crashes nor game-breaking bugs, but terrible controller support and resolution issues have definitely made the experience poorer, I’m, afraid.
Right now, it's an ok game for the fans. It does the service. It's functional. But it's NOWHERE near the brilliant masterpiece that was Life is Strange, unfortunatelly. Can't really recommend it, I'm afraid... And I wanted to love the hell out of this one.

Why is Max so mad? Oh that's right, for a moment I forgot, his wife and kid did done got run over by somebody with the word toe in their name.
Ok, that's enough of that, what did I think of the game? Read on my finely-feathered friends.
Graphics: Utterly superb. Beautiful vistas in what should otherwise be a bone-dry ocean bed. The art direction, texture work, and level design all have George Miller's blood, sweat, and tears strewn about them. The engine, which I've been too lazy to look up whilst I write this, is elegent and silky. The lighting, particles, physics, and texturing are all superbly rendered and calculated, bam! Moving on.
Sound: A huge part of the Miller universe is about sound design. The grinding metal, the pound of the vehicle as it smashes to earth, the crackle and boom of a huge petroleum-based explosion--all this jazz is spectacularly created. Avalanche studio knows their shiznit. It's a known fact. Next!
Gameplay: It's like butta. We've all, well most of us, come to form a love/hate relationship with the mechanics of this new-ish breed of play. Mostly love I'd say. You just...feel like a badass with these new mechanics. The counter/parry into  brutal pounding, into disarming, into chaining some rad beat down onto some serious foeage makes you feel like the biggest badass. OK, I'll not do that again, I promise. But it's true. One of the first in my mind to do this was the early Assassins Creed, and then Batman got a hold of it and did it better, and then Shadow of Mordor did it even better, and now pretty much everyone comes to expect a smooth continues flow of chaining awesome actions together. That's all fine and well, the fighting portion, but where this game shines is the driving. The vehicular entertainment factor brings me back to the first time I played Twisted Metal, and feeling the smash of metal on metal, the chaos, the spectacle gives me nerd chills. And Mad Max the game takes that spectical and injects it with 200ccs of pure nitro, just after chroming and screaming WITNESS ME! OK, I'll admit, there is no chroming in this game. Or huge cirque du soleil poles bounding back and forth, but it hits the mood with a laser sight...OK, I've digressed again. The driving is freakin incredible. So much fun, so much perfect mix of physics, simulation, and arcade.
Story: Just like the movie, you'll not need a deep story line to fully enjoy the action and rush this game kicks out. There is a decent narrative within the main quests, and some very memorable characters with great design. The standout obviously being Chumbucket, the Wasteland black-thumb stray you find wondering the barren open world. Chumbucket, who I'm pretty sure is voiced by the same guy that nailed Trevor in GTA V, kills it with his portrayal of this bumbling hunchback who's only drive (e'hem) in life is to create Max's ultimate driving machine, the Magnum Opus. Chum's desire to work on cars is literally spiritual, and keeps you wanting to upgrade your car as much as possible.
Verdict: Mixed reviews haunt this game, as well as having the brass to release the same day as Metal Gear Solid: Phantom of Pain, which is enjoying a wealth of glowing reviews. Max was definitely held underwater by the throat like a trouble step brother. But positive reviews are still there for MM, and I sure as hell enjoyed it enough to wrire my first review in years. Buy it.

theHunter: Call of the Wild,
I'd give her 5 stars. Not entirely sure what all the hate and absolute disgust is all about, I have found nothing but greatness in the product.
Yes, sure there are a few issues here and there, but nothing that patches won't be able to iron out.
Right, just a brief reason why I rate COTW so highly with a pro's and con's list below.
Call of the Wild has some of the most beautiful, calming and pleasuring forests, plains, rivers and mountains to explore, the ambiance the game creates in that regard is utter beauty.
The animals themselves are really great to look at and stalk. Sure the Buck do not have the hugest varity of Antlers out there, but i am curious to see what the future holds in that regard.
Thus far each hunt has been majestic in its own way. Each hunt has brought about its own challenges and adventure with it. From hunting Red Fox to Various types of Deers, some animals are in a herd which force me to choose wisely and play my tactics carefully if i wish to leave with the best scoring animal, those that travel alone are often very sneaky and sometimes downright genius, though with enough patience and technique, the hunt will reward you with the sight of beauty and the pleasure of the one shot kill. (To which I have noticed a lot of people complaining about 3 shots to bring down a buck.... I have yet to have such an issue. 12 shots fired. 12 hits, 12 kills.
Anyhow onto the Pro's and Con's list.
Con's:
1) Small game and Big game create the same noise while passing through foilage/bushes which is hugely missleading or should i say somewhat confusing, I have caught myself doing 360s with the rifle aimed, looking for that deer that made that racket while passing through the bushes, to see only later that it was merely a rabbit. Very odd for a Rabbit to make such a loud crash through the bushes.
2) A couple of glitches while in Map mode, You have to constantly zoom in and out to see the borders of various places on the map, which isnt very helpful while trying to complete missions, but by no means a game breaker.
3) A few animals are still getting glitched/stuck on various rocks and or tree trunks, Thus far has only happend twice out of the 12 animals i have had the opportunity of taking down.
That is really it thus far.
Pros:
1) The beautifully designed Forests, Plains, Rivers, Mountains etc etc are a sight for sore eyes. I have no issues getting lost in them and just strolling through watching gazing Buck stroll through the wild.
2) The ambiance in the wild is fantastic, it really makes you feel as if you are in the wild, from the birds chirping, to the foxes howling (Squeeking?) to the birds flying out of the bushes while you hastly run past. The wind that blows over the plains and the odd time Thunder strikes the silent evening sky behind you. Its brilliantly done.
3) The Animals are very goodlooking, From the Rabbit through to the various Deers (I have yet to find myself a Bear or any other larger Game, thus i have to hold that comment). They act very well, and I have yet to have issues with them spooking just to stop a few meters later. When they spook, my god do they run, and stop very very far away. Have had some fantastic 2 hour marches following those Tracks.
4) The whole feeling to the game is great, It is not elite hardcore, but is by no means like a Call of Duty Hunter. I see tons of complaints that the game is far too arcade like, but I cannot seem to grasp what that means. The hunts are by no means easy, You can spend a very long time tracking down your prey, very easily spook him off and very easily miss your shot. (Unless ofcourse you are using your rifle like its a machine gun and shooting every animal in sight... well then you have no idea what hunting is about).
Thats about it for now, I will ofcourse update the review at a later stage.
All in all,
I will be spending tons of hours on this beaut of a game.

As someone who has almost 300 hours in Thehunter: Classic this game is pretty much an upgrade to that game. The graphics and atmosphere are fantastic. Night hunting is a lot more tense than anything in Classic ever were. Took me first hour to get used to the keys and set my mouse and stuff but after that I was fully immersed in the game. Stalk hunted some roe deer and fallow deer and even a very hard red deer! So atmosphere, graphics and general feel are good.
Animals are pretty realistic. Tracking is a lot nicer than in Classic and it feels more natural. You can find animal in every corner if you get lucky but for my first hour I didn't even see more than one so it can vary. Each animal give you score, experience and money. Score is based on the animals size and antlers, how quickly you killed the animal, did you use the right weapon and bonus from previous animal harvests. Each animal also has a rank from very easy to mythical. The harder the animal is, the better reward it gives when harvested.
New equipment and weapons are bought with money earned in game from kills and missions. Most of the stuff are locked behind a level or a score so you need to play the game to unlock them. I don't know if I like this or not yet. Need to play more to see how fast can level up and gain money and score to determine if it's a grind to get them all.
Haven't done many missions yet but so far they seem to be reasonably well designed. You can activate multiple and do them while you explore and hunt. Gives extra cash and experience and shows you around the maps, which is pretty great.
So far the best thing about the game has been exploring. Maps are beautiful and full of stuff to discover. I was taking screenshots left and right all the time. It's a really, really beautiful game and sound design just enhances that feeling.
the UI is pretty horrible to be honest. Inventory is a mess and pretty unclear. Huge icons on the screen for tracks and calls. You can't see your own waypoint in the huntermate until you are 100 meters away from it. Makes the navigating a bit challenging when you need to open a map to see where you are going. Luckily you can turn most of those things off so that's a plus.
Most bugs that I ran into were sound or animation bugs. Background music in outposts is very loud. Animals can get pretty easily stuck on rocks when fleeing. Jumping and walking uphill is a drag. Somehow I lost almost all my health by jumping. The game ran smoothly on high/ultra with my machine (i7-2600, 16gm ram, gtx 970).
TL;DR If you liked TheHunter: Classic but don't want to pay montly fees and you own modern gaming PC, this is the game for you. If you have never played a hunting game then I'd say this is a pretty good game to start with. I didn't find it that hard until I was chasing a mythical fox in the night which was impossible! The game will be updated and bugs will be fixed so if you are concerned about those then keep an eye and wait for bugs to be ironed out. If you want the best and most beautiful hunting experience available right now, get this game. It's fantastic at what it does.

Okay. TheHunter: Call of the Wild™...is it any good?
ehm...yes, it is...BUT, and this is the BUTTEST of BUTS, it could be great and it isnt right now.
It is buggy. The controls and the menu's are doing weird things all over the place.
The challenge is okay. Sneaking up on deer has not become TOO easy. Landing a good shot is still something that takes practice. However, there are a reasonable amount of animals around and they are not as easily startled as in the TheHunter classic. This is an understandable choice, given the different game mechanics, but it takes some getting used to.
All in all, the gameplay could use some finetuning, the bugs definitely need to be FIXED as quickly as possible (it is a disgrace that the product is so buggy), but the game is generally fine.
And this brings us to the best feature of the game. IT IS GORGEOUS. absolutely gorgeous. If you are like me and you spent many hours into TheHunter classic, you are probably okay with how the old game looks. Not great, but it works and it stills conveys the idea of a realistic hunt. But this is a new level of looks. the foliage and the grass bending away when you walk through out, the light breaking through the trees. It is so beautiful and gives a whole different esthetic to the game.
Just yes. In this case, I would say, trust that the developers will fix the things that need fixing. They are a very community oriented bunch and they do listen to what the community says. If that happens, if the bugs get fixed and the gameplay finetuned, we have a mighty fine hunting game on our hands. Buy it. It works.

This review is written on 4.5 hours of playtime:
To start, I love this game. Everyone's biggest issue with theHunter classic was that you had to pay (real money) for weapons and items. In CotW, you earn money to buy them by completing missions and harvesting animals. I love using the camera to take photos of an absolutely stunning visual experience.
However, there are a lot of bugs, almost too many to mention and probably some that have not even been noticed yet. This is not acceptable for a full release game, if there is such a term anymore. It's 2017, developers dish out patches left and right to make thier games better, and I have a hard time believing Expansive Worlds will just up and give up on this game that they have been so passionate about.
Verdict: If you want a hunting game, and hate microtransactions, this is the game for you. Otherwise, stick to the 'free' theHunter : Classic version for now.
P.S. EW has voiced that both versions of theHunter will be living on, and that they are to go hand-in-hand.

Charming and self-aware, Rogue Legacy is a refreshing take on the platformer hack and slash genre. The advancement system, however, requires significant repetitive grinding and the balance of the game feels a little off. Expect to grind for a few hours to get to the point where you can one shot the starting enemies, only to find yourself tediously having to run through the easy rooms every round to get to the next 'level' of grinding.
Much is made over the procedural aspects of this game, and honestly the fun of the game is primarily in playing different characters with different traits, which make some parts harder, open different parts of the levels, and apply different play styles. However, despite being strung together randomly the rooms tend to blur together after a while, as the enemy variety is somewhat lacking. You can always expect to see the same set of enemies in each iteration, and the set isn't all that large given the intention of constant replay.
Still this game is worth the few bucks you'll spend on it and I encourage you to play it, even if you don't complete it.

As I died screaming between a wolf’s jaws, collapsing in the snow that dusts the top of the mountains while listening to it gnaw through virtual flesh, I had a realization: survival games are fun as long as they are about the threat of death.
Death itself is underwhelming: a gateway to an ever-increasing set of chores and tasks that you must repeat in order to recover your lost progress. Inevitably, the process eventually repeats, and the to-do list gets longer and less fulfilling, which sounds a little bit like hell and a little bit like a parable about the human condition. Rust [official site], the multiplayer survival game from Facepunch Studios, seems comfortable with both analogies.
If you’re not familiar with Rust, or if you only know it as the Survival Game with Lots of♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ it’s actually a weirder and more interesting game than it first appears to be. You wake up in a strange landscape, cold and naked with nothing but a torch and a rock to your name. Then, after a few minutes of trial-and-error exploration of Rust’s wilderness, you can start building crude tools out of loose materials, then using those tools to harvest more material to build better tools, etc. The tech tree runs from Stone Age materials all the way to automatic weapons and heavy body armor. Survival in Rust can become a fairly comfortable survivalist’s fantasy if you stay alive long enough… but death comes swiftly and with little warning.

My favourite thing about this game is it’s captivating story. With a lot of humour, this game pulls off an action shooter with RPG aspects and a storyline you should follow. There are lots of sidequests that will take hours to complete, but the benefits of completing this game are well worth the time. With millions of different guns, a lot of different character skins and a unique experience with all the various classes, this game has hours of fun built straight in.
The game will be fun no matter which class you play, but that’s not entirely due to the class. I found that most of the classes really lack something to keep you interested in, and throughout the whole game it feels like more attention was given to certain classes over others. Story-wise, the siren is pretty much the only class that gets any attention and backstory, as an individual with a history and as a class with abilities. All of the classes have a slight amount of backstory that becomes obvious throughout the game, but Siren has significantly more, and even then it’s very little.
Beyond that, the entertainment value of playing as certain classes over others was very noticeable to me. I played as all the classes, including the 2 DLC classes, and some of the abilities and skill trees and other class-specific aspects were lacking for a bunch of the classes. Some things that were common for all of the classes were that there are certain skill trees that seem obviously better than other ones and significantly simpler to think about, making them seem more attractive, and all of the classes lack enough in-game backstory to really get a feel for them. With all these classes, it comes down to a matter of opinion, what sort of playstyle you like and other such things, but I’ve found that there are some that are distinctly more enjoyable than others.
I think if there were more random Echo Recorders placed around the maps with a bunch of stories about the characters, with more information on them the game could be a lot more interesting. Throughout my playing of the game, I found a couple about Maya (the siren), one about Zer0 (the assassin/ghost) and nothing about any other character. That’s always been something that annoyed me. The stories of the characters may exist somewhere, but if they do, they are probably too hard to find.
In terms of story, I loved this game. There was a hint of humour in just about every interaction you had with the other characters, and the story overall was very captivating and kept me playing. I think the end-game was a bit lacking and didn’t completely match up with the story, but it was still interesting and I don’t regret playing this game through at all. The side quests in this game were very extensive, and easily one of my favourite aspects of the game. Some sidequests are very tedious and boring, but others are absolutely a blast, like those given to you by Tiny Tina (pun intended ;) ).
The replayability of this game isn’t infinite, it does get boring to play through the same parts over and over again in this game, but that doesn’t mean you can’t play it more than once at all. Replaying the game in True Vault Hunter Mode, a difficulty increase that allows you to replay the game using your already powerful character, can still be quite fun. The difficulty of the game overall becomes harder while maintaining the same story with no new additions aside from more powerful guns.
The playstyle in this game is very different from that of most other shooters. In Borderlands, you don’t really need to conserve any ammo and you can run around, jump and do a bunch of other crazy things while still attacking enemies. This makes the game more casual and relaxed, which I found to be pretty enjoyable. You very rarely run out of ammo, with all the excessive boxes with tons of different types of ammunition and the cheap price at which you can buy ammo in shops.
That brings me to my next point, which is the excess of money in this game. There is very rarely an opportunity where spending money makes much sense or is beneficial, with ammo being really cheap and not really affecting your money and most of the items in shops being pretty bad compared to the ones you can get outside from drops. I know a lot of people enjoy using the slot machines at Moxxi’s bar, but I never found it that entertaining when it for the most part doesn’t get me anything decent. Pretty much the only point of collecting money is to get the badass ranks.
The whole badass system is something I really like in Borderlands. Being able to slightly upgrade your character in about every way imaginable pretty awesome. Slowly, you’ll amass badass ranks by completing these missions, the more difficult missions resulting in more badass ranks, and for every 25 badass ranks you’ll get 1 badass token which can be used to upgrade one of the 5 stats presented. I really like the additional content that this adds to the game.
Personally, I far prefer playing this game with other people. I don’t like playing very many games alone, and even if I’m playing a singleplayer game, I like to be talking to other people at the same time. I find it a lot more enjoyable, and the same thing applies to this game. I’ve never played this game without other people simply because every moment allows for a lot more laughing and interaction when you’re doing it with other people. If I had played through this game alone, I might have noticed some interesting bits of humour, but I never would have started laughing hysterically at some glitchy motion or funny joke. The enjoyment is multiplied by a lot when playing this game with other people.
Something I noticed is that everyone plays this game differently. Personally, I like to play it patiently, doing all the sidequests, and being sure I’m making the right decisions with my skill points and gun choices. When I play Borderlands, I also like to play for as long of a period as possible. Of course I know nothing is that big of a deal, but I like being patient with this game and spending time on everything because I like feeling that I’m making the right decisions. Some of the people I have played with like to speed through the game and skip any extra content and make the easiest decisions possible. I think it’s important to play with people that have at least a similar mindset to you so that you aren’t being forced to play in a way that you aren’t entirely comfortable with.
Warning: Slight spoilers in following paragraph. Reader discretion is advised.
The final boss of the game really irked me. There was a whole obsession with how it was summoned using a siren and the key, both of which are very eridium oriented. The final boss used a lot of fiery attacks and swam in the pools of lava that surrounded the boss fight. I think it would have made a lot more sense if they were pools of molten eridium or something, with the boss spewing out eridium, or at least something purple, rather than fire.
This game also has some really amazing individual lines. They are scared all throughout the game, but easily my favourite is the line that Scooter says when you meet him in Sanctuary. I’ve probably ruined the rewatching of that line several times when replaying the game with friends, through my inability to repeat the line properly and because I keep on trying.
Overall, this game can easily be worth $20 depending on how much you play it and how much you enjoy it. I’d recommend getting it on sale simply because I’ve seen it go on sale reasonably often, for at least 66% off, but the game is also getting older and the Pre-Sequel (another game in this series, taking place between the first and second games) did come out recently. Quite simply, I love the amount of humour in this game, it’s a fun game to sink plenty of time into, and probably one of my top 10 all time games because of how much of a blast I had with it.

Not good at reviews so here is a gluten free bagel recipe
Gluten-Free Bagels
Makes 8
4 tbsp. active dry yeast
3 tbsp. sugar, divided
⅔ cup warm (110° F) water
1 cup gluten-free flour blend (recipe below)
1 cup potato starch
½ cup nonfat dry milk powder or Better Than Milk soy powder
2 tsp. salt
2 tsp. xanthan gum
1 tsp. guar gum
2 tbsp. canola oil, divided
1 large egg
1 tsp. cider vinegar
Brown rice flour, for dusting
1 tbsp. baking soda
Poppy seeds, for garnish (optional)
1. Dissolve the yeast and 1 tsp. sugar in the warm water and set aside, letting the yeast foam for about 5 minutes. Grease a 9×13-inch rimmed baking sheet or line with parchment paper.
2. In the bowl of a heavy-duty stand mixer, combine the yeast mixture, 1 tbsp. plus 2 tsp. of the remaining sugar, flour blend, potato starch, dry milk powder, salt, xanthan gum, guar gum, 1 tbsp. oil, egg and vinegar. Beat on low speed (using a regular beater, not the dough hook) just until blended. Increase the speed to medium-low and beat for 2 minutes, scraping down the sides of the bowl with a spatula if necessary. The dough will be stiff.
3. Divide the dough into eight equal portions. Generously dust each portion with rice flour; then shape into a ball. Flatten to a 3-inch circle, dust again with rice flour, and punch a hole in the center. Pull the dough gently away from the hole to form a 3-inch-diameter bagel with a 1-inch hole in the center. Place the shaped bagel on the baking sheet.
4. Place a rack in the lower third of the oven. Place the bagels in the cold oven. Set the temperature to 325 degrees and bake for 10 minutes. Remove the bagels from the oven, but leave them on the stovetop and increase the oven temperature to 350 degrees.
5. Meanwhile, bring 3 inches of water, the remaining 1 tbsp. sugar, the baking soda, and the remaining 1 tbsp. oil to boil in a Dutch oven. Boil the bagels in batches for 30 seconds, drain them on paper towels, and return them to the baking sheet. Sprinkle with the poppy seeds, if using.
6. Return the baking sheet of bagels to the oven. Bake until the bagels are nicely browned, 25-30 minutes. Cool the bagels on the baking sheet on a wire rack for 15 minutes. Transfer the bagels to the wire rack to cool for another 10 minutes. Serve slightly warm.
Gluten-Free Flour Blend
1½ cups sorghum flour or brown rice flour
1½ cups potato starch or cornstarch
1 cup tapioca flour
Whisk together until thoroughly blended and store, tightly covered, in a dark, dry place.

Seriously though, this is a fantastic game. There's nothing more relaxing than just spacing out while driving across the enormous map listening to some decent music. I'd definately recommend going into the settings and turning off the speed limiter and the fatigue simulation as the game is much more enjoyable without these. I also found it helpful to set the quicksave button to tab so I can easily back up the game before my reckless driving gets me into an accident.
The only downside I can think of is the sense of sameness in the places you visit. I mean a lot of them are really memorable, driving through the swiss alps is very scenic and it's very enjoyable driving along the atlantic coast, but most towns just feel like the same industrial park arranged in slightly different ways. I have now played this game for 951 hours, I've driven 592779 km in game and I'm still playing it!
Believe me when I tell you that I've tried to understand what keeps me playing this game and when I bought this game several years ago I didn't really think I'd like it.
The scenery is beautiful as you drive around in a compressed version of Europe with landscapes reflecting reality and with distinctive landmarks. Just seeing them in game knowing they exist in real life is very nice! SCS have added everything from aircrafts landing and taking off to riverboats and pedestrians to make the game feel alive. SCS also added AI-cars and trucks which you will love to hate! This leads me to the less good things with this game.
ETS2 isn't really a simulator, you drive a truck which seem realistic enough to drive but there are too many things which ETS2 lacks to be called a simulator. Like proper damage, brake wear etc. For anyone playing other simulators, I guess ETS2 feels a bit arcadish. The AI or "Annoying Idiots" as I call them tend to drive very badly at times, for example in roundabouts. The company you own and run is made so simple it would've been better if SCS left it out.
There are as of today three major map addition DLC and a fourth coming soon. ETS2 has numerous other DLC too, everything from cosmetic such as national flags to different kind of cargoes. The map DLC adds new achievements and so does some of the other DLC. I see a danger with SCS releasing too many DLC as the total cost of the game constantly increase. However, you have to consider what SCS gives you for free, such as new cars for the AI to drive around in and other updates. I haven't seen a released game being updated this frequently ever so buying the DLC makes SCS constantly updating ETS2.
If this doesn't convince you, download the demo, buy the game on a sale but you should treat you to this game.

If you get this game its not for the gameplay. The mechanics shown here have been done before, and done better. This does not mean the gameplay is terrible, just bland and familiar.
The REAL reason you get this game is the story. Unlike most "realistic" modern military shooters, The Line shows the true horrors of war.
You will make decisions in this game, all with the cost of life and with no right answer. The enemies are actually characterized as REAL people, and nothing you can do will save everyone.
Inspired by "Heart of Darkness" and "Apocalypse Now" this game has NO black and white. NO right and wrong. NO right choices. It’s a grim exploration of the trauma soldiers experience, and the pain they suffer as their faculties break down, and you eventually start to distrust the main character just as his squad mates do.
The main character's story arc is brutal, uncompromising, three dimensional, and downright terrifying at times when his actions catch up with him, and he tries to rationalize it all away while dealing with the blows to his sanity.
This game will make you lose yourself in the gameplay, enjoying the hero fantasy, then yank on the choke chain and force you to take responsibility for your actions as they wreak havoc that isn't always apparent at first glance.
At the same time it is a brutal, and not always subtle, satire of the modern military genre, and the role the players themselves have on the events in the game.
This story will make you feel guilt, it will make you feel remorse, and it will show the true hell that is war.
Highly recommended.

As I died screaming between a wolf’s jaws, collapsing in the snow that dusts the top of the mountains while listening to it gnaw through virtual flesh, I had a realization: survival games are fun as long as they are about the threat of death.
Death itself is underwhelming: a gateway to an ever-increasing set of chores and tasks that you must repeat in order to recover your lost progress. Inevitably, the process eventually repeats, and the to-do list gets longer and less fulfilling, which sounds a little bit like hell and a little bit like a parable about the human condition. Rust [official site], the multiplayer survival game from Facepunch Studios, seems comfortable with both analogies.
If you’re not familiar with Rust, or if you only know it as the Survival Game with Lots of♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ it’s actually a weirder and more interesting game than it first appears to be. You wake up in a strange landscape, cold and naked with nothing but a torch and a rock to your name. Then, after a few minutes of trial-and-error exploration of Rust’s wilderness, you can start building crude tools out of loose materials, then using those tools to harvest more material to build better tools, etc. The tech tree runs from Stone Age materials all the way to automatic weapons and heavy body armor. Survival in Rust can become a fairly comfortable survivalist’s fantasy if you stay alive long enough… but death comes swiftly and with little warning.

Hands down the best local multiplayer game on steam. It's very different from other local multiplayer games on steam largely because everything is based on manipulation of the physics engine. Other games require memorising different weapon and action combinations (e.g. Duck Game: knowing about the chain saw slide or the sniper shooting through windows). In Gang Beasts you can manipulate the body of your beast, and you use that to get the other players out of the map, or into the fire, or something similar.  That's it. You just learn the ways that your character moves - you learn, for instance, that you can jump and flop at the same time (A to jump, X/B to flop forward/backwards) and that allows you to dropkick people. It's not a combo of random buttons that does a prefab animation, it's entirely the manipulation of your character. That means that there's basically no skill cap - you just keep learning more stuff about how to do things. It's absurdly fun.
Things that need to be done:
* General bugfixing (like the ability to survive underwater sometimes, or the massive glitching out of the character mesh sometimes).
* Campaign mode - this is off to a good start already.
* More optionality over settings - we need to be able to select different map cycles, for instance.

His every move and action are tracked by speed cameras allowing the government to know immediately the instant he ever breaks the slightest traffic law.
Seriously though, this is a fantastic game. There's nothing more relaxing than just spacing out while driving across the enormous map listening to some decent music. I'd definately recommend going into the settings and turning off the speed limiter and the fatigue simulation as the game is much more enjoyable without these. I also found it helpful to set the quicksave button to tab so I can easily back up the game before my reckless driving gets me into an accident.
The only downside I can think of is the sense of sameness in the places you visit. I mean a lot of them are really memorable, driving through the swiss alps is very scenic and it's very enjoyable driving along the atlantic coast, but most towns just feel like the same industrial park arranged in slightly different ways. Sure there are some landmarks in the background but you don't really get to get anywhere near them. I don't so much mind this though as it's truck simulator not a tourism simulator.
This is a game I've played for ages and will continue to play for ages, something I can say about fewer and fewer releases these days

I have now played this game for 951 hours, I've driven 592779 km in game and I'm still playing it!
Believe me when I tell you that I've tried to understand what keeps me playing this game and when I bought this game several years ago I didn't really think I'd like it.
The scenery is beautiful as you drive around in a compressed version of Europe with landscapes reflecting reality and with distinctive landmarks. Just seeing them in game knowing they exist in real life is very nice! SCS have added everything from aircrafts landing and taking off to riverboats and pedestrians to make the game feel alive. SCS also added AI-cars and trucks which you will love to hate! This leads me to the less good things with this game.
ETS2 isn't really a simulator, you drive a truck which seem realistic enough to drive but there are too many things which ETS2 lacks to be called a simulator. Like proper damage, brake wear etc. For anyone playing other simulators, I guess ETS2 feels a bit arcadish. The AI or "Annoying Idiots" as I call them tend to drive very badly at times, for example in roundabouts. The company you own and run is made so simple it would've been better if SCS left it out.
There are as of today three major map addition DLC and a fourth coming soon. ETS2 has numerous other DLC too, everything from cosmetic such as national flags to different kind of cargoes. The map DLC adds new achievements and so does some of the other DLC. I see a danger with SCS releasing too many DLC as the total cost of the game constantly increase. However, you have to consider what SCS gives you for free, such as new cars for the AI to drive around in and other updates. I haven't seen a released game being updated this frequently ever so buying the DLC makes SCS constantly updating ETS2.
If this doesn't convince you, download the demo, buy the game on a sale but you should treat you to this game.
