First off, I'd like to say WB did an overall great job on the game. I spent 31 hours playing this, and I normally just go straight through the main story, but this game I did otherwise. I loved running around a desert wasteland, surprisingly. It seems boring and bland from afar, but they did a great job making it as exciting and immersive as possible.
Pros:
-Amazing combat mechanics, although WB has never done a bad job on that.
-Graphics were great, other than the fact he was in a barren wasteland, it's hard to do much with that.
-Not buggy, least from my experience. A solid game.
-Reminded me of Far Cry a little, which is one of my favorite game series.
-Added not only great fighting mechanics, but good racing mechanics as well.
-I greatly enjoy open world, and this one gave you a ton to do.
-Followed the original movie more, not the new one, which I prefer.
Cons:
-Didn't dive into Max's character, had little to none character developement. Was eager to find out more of how the wasteland came to be, and of Max's past and family.
-Boss fight left me wanting more, didn't get to smash his head like I did with other Top Dog's.
-(SPOILER) Felt horrible for little Chumbucket, Max treated him like crap and I guess it stuck to his character, again, no developement. I guess it isn't necessary but I'd like to have personally seen it.
-When racing, if you even slightly hit a wall you'd bounce off then take 10 seconds to get back to normal speed. Very frusterating.
-No decision making whatsoever, although I'm spoiled with new games that have that option, this one sadly did not.
Overall, I loved the game. I never played the Batman games, but I've come to understand Warner Bros always tends to release a solid game. It didn't completely stand out, and it wasn't my favorite game, but I did enjoy playing it. I highly recommend doing all Wasteland Missions possible, and taking down bases, as it at least gets you into it more. Certainly worth the buy if any of you were wondering, just expect some anger out of races. I'd give it a 7/10.

I've been playing this game for a while now (granted having played since little more than a year is nothing compared some others, as well as 250+ hours of play time). It started as a game I bought just to have something to play with my friends (who were having the wildest adventures to listen to in TeamSpeak). I had no idea what I was up to, not even knowing what DayZ was all about other then it beeing a Survival-Type of game (with Zombies). "If you die, you lose everything" I've been told (It's true). After a rough start, many encounters with other players (most of them tried and managed to kill me), many many many deaths through various reasons and said 250+ hours of staying in Chernarus I've decided to give my opinion about this game (current Patch 0.62).
Pro:
+ Huge world with (almost) no boundaries.
+ Though it seems to be simple the System itself is very complex (Health, Hunger, Thirst, Bone-Stats, Shock, Loot-System, Shooting) [I recommend to check out WOBO's Youtube-Channel*, he helped me a lot to understand how DayZ works].
+ Fairly good view distance (though details drop off very quick).
+ The Immersion is great despite those Zombies (Light- and Soundeffects, Wind and its effects on trees and smoke for example [Since 0.62]).
(+ If there's any value to it: Sometimes it's so calming and peaceful just wandering around)
Con:
- Slow development Cycle (It's true, a good wine needs time to age well, but this doesn't apply to games while still beeing alpha).
- KOS (Kill on Sight) is still prevalent, even though I feel like more and more people tend to be friendlier (what doesn't mean they won't kill you, but rather they talk to you and then kill you if they think you've got something of interest - C'est la vie).
- Still full of glitches, buggs and lag-spikes (It keeps improving and YES it's just normal in an alpha but still ...[I hate this damn apple glitch, it makes survival way easier if you don't need to worry about finding food and water - as apples give both - and just run up to the next appletree])
- Beginners will have a hard time getting the hang of it (If it hadn't been with my friends, my first hours of the game would've consisted of me starving, dieing of thirst, and generaly have no idea what to loot and how to shoot [No seriously, only thanks to DayZ I practised shooting in videogames in general]).
In all honesty now that I'm writing this review, I understand, why many are drawn away from DayZ. Promisses not keepen, tiny evolution steps compared to a slow development, KOS, glitches, buggs and yes sometimes just running around looting or sitting and waiting for something to happen (for someone to come around so you can shoot them for example) can and will be boring. This game needs a lot of work until it's finished.
And still I have to say, the most boring moments in gaming to me happend in DayZ, but also the most exciting ones as well (alone and together with friends). It's undescribable, how thrilling it is to have a gunfight with other players, or to be curing your illness (in my case: Cholera) sitting within a forest just to hear a car driving by followed by gunshots.
Why i still recommend this game?
Not only for its potential, but for what it has become in the (granted short) time that I've been playing it. I look at ArmA3 Mods, at other (Zombie-)Survival-Games, but to me DayZ (despite its flaws) makes so much right, that I'm willing to stick through another wave of KOSers, glitches, running around for hours and uncounted deaths, so that I can once more feel the thrill and joy of surviving all this and I wish for others to have the same amount of fun like I do, too.
Give DayZ a try, you won't regret it, I surely didn't.

I hate that Steam forces me to boil down the review to binary Yay or Nay, but given only these choices I am afraid I have to say Nay.
The fact is there nothing wrong with the game, I can’t mention any bugs, design flaws, balance problems… it is just but for 2 exceptions (see detailed review) everything the game has to offer you can find somewhere else, often done better and not unimportantly at half price.
And this isn’t a case where you can find similar feature in one game and another feature in another… there are games out there that a so similar I was certain Mad Max was made by the same developer.
*** Detailed Review (long and might have spoilers) ***
Know that Mad Max is a good, fun game. I’ve put 18 hour into it already and have no intention of stopping however it is not worth $60 price tag considering you can get similar or better experience for a half price.
First of all things Mad Max is worth paying for:
1.       Settings.  If you are a fan of Mad Max Universe or at least post-apocalyptic settings in general the game should be worth few extra bucks
2.       Vehicle Combat.  There are number of the games that offer vehicle combat, but there is no denying that Mad Max’ combat which focuses on ramming rather than firepower and often goes off-road feels unique.
The rest:
1.       Things to do.  Professional reviews of Max seem to like to say “open world with lots of things to do”.  Well it’s NOT, it’s more accurate to say that there are about a dozen of things to do (if you want to be kind and count say fighting minions and fighting bosses as separate activities) BUT you can repeat those thing over and over in over a 100 locations.  This isn’t as bad as might seem, the gameplay is fun enough that feeling of grind won’t set in for some time, but you’ll get there.
2.       Melee Combat.  Unless you are new to this whole gaming thing there is nothing there you have not seen before.  Parry-counter system that you know from Batman, Assassin Creed, Shadow of Mordor, Sleeping Dogs, and so on.  Whether Mad Max melee is better or worse is a matter of personal preference, it certainly has a standard compliment of finishers, perfect parries, dodges, escapes, rage, and more.  Personally though I think Mad Max while fluid and brutal is rather simple and blunt… No swashbuckling flourish of Assassin, Over the Top feel of Batman or Kung-Fu sophistication of Sleeping Dogs.
3.       Open World.  There is beauty in the Great White with its wide dune seas, hulks of derelict ships and occasional unique feature such as crashed airplane or gigantic stature.  In the end though it’s a desert - nothing but nothing with rubble in it.  It fits the settings but it also feels empty and blunt.  This isn’t Assassin with busy towns  and lush wild environments; this isn’t Sleeping Dogs with bustling fictional Hong Kong; this isn’t Mordor teaming with Ork activity… there are event sand random encounters here but not nearly enough.  There are also over a hundred of locations, unfortunately 90% of these look the same, feel the same and boil down to the same “kill everyone and look for scraps” functionality.
4.       Character Advancement.  You can improve Max, his car and even Strongholds he uses… and there are plenty of such improvements, but not more than in other similar games and linear advancement (this isn’t about choices or right tools for the job, just level, get improved ability, level, improve ability further) feels dumbed down comparing to others.
5.       Immersion.  You know what you need to do in Sleeping Dogs to learn new martial arts move?  You need to do a favor for Sifu - recover items that were stolen from the school, bring it back, and complete an actual training session.  You know what you need to do in Mad Max to learn new melee maneuver?  Get enough metal scraps and… well in the middle of nowhere sacrifice it to the thin air - and boom you now know new fighting technique.  The problem is this is just an example; the game is full of suspension of disbelief and symbolic actions.
6.       Missing Features.  And then there are things that you would expect from an open world action adventure but for some reason are missing here most noticeably Stealth and Mobility.  Max can barely jump – forget the climbing and parkour mobility of Assassin, Batman, Ranger, Officer Shen…  as for Stealth Max’s idea of Stealth is occasionally rushing an opponent who has his back to him (there is simply no stealth in the game)

From nearly start to finish I enjoyed my time in the Wastelands with Max.  Yes, the missions and tasks were repetitive and, yes, the combat was more of the same from Batman or Shadow of Mordor but the world was immersive enough, attractive enough (in its own wasteland way) and just plain fun enough to keep me returning.
Nearly every "repetitive" aspect managed to find a way to stay interesting.  Melee combat felt heavy and brutal and slamming a guy's head into a wall or suplexing him never got old for me.  There's a hundred or so locations where you can seek scrap metal or water but they varied from tents to old subway cars to cliffside villages to abandoned restaurants to deep caves.  You're tasked with tearing down giant metal "scarecrows" but, to the last, I enjoyed flying past (or through) them, launching a harpoon and collapsing them behind my racing vehicle.  You'll do a LOT of driving but the landscape is wonderfully created as you progress from dried ocean bottom to ravaged desert towns and upland desert to the mountains of waste and scrap surrounding Gastown.
Vehicular combat is a special joy and from early on you are armed with a harpoon that can tear off armor, tires or doors or pull a War Boy out of his car or a sniper out of his tower.  Further car enhancements allow you to attach grinders to your wheels Ben-Hur style or launch explosive spears to quickly end a fight.
The game certainly isn't perfect.  Boss fights are almost all copies of each other, clearing mine fields is tedious busy work and there is a major plot-required race that deviates from all the other driving you'll do in game.  The plot is nothing special and this game is definitely more about the journey than the destination.  But Mad Max and the Wastelands kept me coming back for more days on end managed to never feel "old".

Spec Ops:The line is one of those games where the promotional materials betray it's true nature.
It's true that the gameplay, while generally boring Gears of War-esque whack-a-mole fest,is still serviceable,but the gameplay being like it is helps convey the storyline, as it's one of the best military shooter stories ever told in gaming....not spoilering, but the game is littered with little details that help fill in on the thought-provoking storyline with other neat details being left to the player to infer.

This is easily my favorite shooter of 2012 and one of the most memorable gaming experiences I have had in a long time! That being said, the gameplay is generic and repetetive and the multiplayer is useless. The visuals, on the other hand, are above average and at times very impressive. However, what really makes this game stand out from all other modern military shooters is the story.
In a genre where narrative sits unnoticed on the backburner Spec Ops: The Line is a breathe of fresh air. I don't want to give any of the story away, and the less you know about the story heading in the better. Trudge your way through the slightly slow build up at the beginning of the game and you will soon find yourself eagerly anticipating returning to the game; not because it's the most fun game you've played, but because you will be interested in the narrative and where it will take you next.
If you are looking for the next Call of Duty or Gears of War then look elsewhere. However, if the idea of a military shooter with a very good story that takes interesting and unique risks with it's story telling to create an experience that you've doubtfully had with any game prior then definitely consider picking this game up.

Pros: Combat system

Now the reason I listed the combat and story as both pros and cons is due to the fact that the combat system can be fun for the first few hours but will eventually become boring since you don't have much in the way of weapons beside your shotgun, Fists and the occasional spiked baseball bat to use until it breaks (for whatever reason) and you will more often than not have close to no ammo. Now the story is listed as both because it can be engaging and interesting at times but then be more monotonous than you might like a few times through, however I did find the majority of the characters to be interesting like Chumbucket your car mechanic who has probably done sexual things with the Magnum Opus a few times and will help out with combat.
Overall I would say in my oppinion that Mad Max is an easy 8.5 out of ten.

Do you like free roaming? Like to do a lot of sidequesting, collecting? Like to drive vehicles? Do you like the Mad Max franchise/movies? Then this game is for you. People who are not that much into the previous mentioned topics can still enjoy the game and get enough satisfaction out of it. The story isn't that great, comes down to go to person x to achieve vehicle unlock x etc. I think I'm halfway through the story but I don't think it will change any time soon. That's not to say that it is boring, the prerequisites that you need to complete can be simple or challenging depending on where you are in the game.
Exploration is also done very well. You have these Ubisoft-ish points you have to go to, to scout the area around it but even if you don't you can still explore the various sites by driving around. If you do want to use the balloon sites (to scout the area) you have to secure the site, then go in the air with the balloon and manually detect everything in your vicinity with your binoculars. So it's not something passive as just climbing up somewhere and then 'syncronishing' the area. Don't forget to enjoy the view when you're up there! ;)
Combat system could be better but doesn't really offer any real challenge. The only challenge you'll experience is when you face a large group of enemies where you'll have to press the block/parry button a lot of times on the correct moment. That's not to say the combat system on foot is bad, but it's not my favourite.
All in all this game doesn't offer anything new, but that doesn't mean it ain't good. I'm really enjoying it and can only recommend this. If you like the previous mentioned topics, buy it straight away, if not then wait till the price drops. This game is definately something you're going to be enjoying if you make the purchase for what you deem the right price!

This isn't a game that holds your hand. SO, if you're expecting that, turn right around. Nothing is easy the first time through, and even when you've become used to the patterns it can still be punishing. A metroidvania style game, it blends the dark atmosphere and story telling of castlevania with a light humor; You'll find yourself intrigued by the epic backstory, but later chuckle when your character has IBS and you fart every other other time you jump. The story isn't in your face either, it doesn't require a lot of explanation. You can discover it on your own if you want, or just go around killing every enemy you see and ignore the history lying about. The game doesn't punish you for neglecting the expository, but it does punish you for mistakes. Essentially, everytime you die: you are given a set of three new characters of varying clases, spells, and traits. The characters are randomly generated so it never seems to stale as far as choosing a new class. I often found myself favoring certain spells and traits, but I was more comfortable with them. Some traits can be bad, and add challenge to the game. And others are just an interesting, and refreshing, diversion to the game. It can be a bit grindy at times, but when you manage to accomplish something: the feeling is immensely gratifying. The satisfaction of overcoming that hurdle let's you forget that you still have another milestone to accomplish. Especially when you start accumulating a horde of gold to spend on your next death. That's right, everytime you die: you get to upgrade your character. On top of death letting you start fresh and make yourself stronger for the next fight, it randomizes the entire castle. The general layout is the same but the individual rooms are changed. This, in my personal opinion, really helps the game keep it's replay value. Overall, it's a massive time killer. You'll find yourself frustrated at times, but once you get the hang of it: it can become crazy fun. For 15 dollars, this game is great. Better than some games that are charging 60. However, if you're not into 2D side-scrolling, dungeon crawling, role playing, grindy games: stay away. This game is not for you.

Bought it because it was kinda cheap and I must say that Euro Truck simulator 2 is one of the most addictive and immersive games I've ever played.
Not too realistic, no damage visible on car, no explosions when you're carring some petrol or acid.
It's not spectacular at all, it's slow.
The most important (to me) factor who contributes on fun and enjoyement is exploration, and Euro truck with or without map mods is one of the biggest open world, with nice variety very good landscapes and a sense of detail on environment, road works, trains, farms, small villages, forests, mountain trails it takes about 1 hour and a half, maybe more to cross the map from one point in Europe to the opposite. the driving model is very solid, not as complex as car sims like Asseto corsa or GTR2 but it's there, sometimes it's slipperly, your truck may collapse, you have to be aware check your rear view mirrors, incoming cars trucks, reckless cars, speed limits and so on..

A good game with a lot of similarities to the first. Suffice it to say: if you enjoyed the original, you'll find a good deal to like here as well. That said, the sequel doesn't deviate in any major ways to draw in the audience which avoided the first game.
Graphically, the game hasn't changed much. It holds up well after the last few years, but poly count is a little low and some textures could use a little help. Either way, it has a respectable style which keeps it hanging on as time goes by. Performance is mostly good, but enabling nVidia PhysX will crush frame rates (I play on a GTX 760 which is roughly mid-range at the time of this review). Disabling PhysX settings (which is too bad, because they're somewhat impressive) brings the frame rate back up to a smooth 60.
As for gameplay, it's more of the same. Expect the same sort of absurd, irreverant humor as the first. The story line benefits from a notable new writer (of internet fame), and goes to a noticeably deeper place (and somewhat darker). Ultimately, the game is a "loot and shoot" in the extreme. Unfortunately, the loot isn't quite as I remember. A quick Google search shows that the method for determining loot value was changed between the two games, and the ability to discern quality items based solely on item grade is no longer a true option. In fact, some very high-rarity items are utter rubbish. Get ready to brush up on stats, because you'll need to know your numbers to really pick quality gear. That said, you can always make it through the game with whatever you find - it's difficult at times, but only a moderate difficulty overall. If worse comes to worst, the RPG aspect allows you to grind a few levels if you need to out-level a boss or quest area at any point.
The long-short is that it's a fun game with a decent story and a good art style which runs well on most PCs of today. If you enjoy the endless grind and quest for loot, you could spend some real time here - multiplayer being included. If, on the other hand, you prefer a shorter, tighter experience, you may find yourself frustrated.

From what I hear this game got a poor showing from critics however through my experience I found it much more enjoyable than they implied -
Pro's - The game looks fantastic, really feels like you are immersed in the Mad Max world. If you are a fan of the films and you are looking for that authentic experience then look no further. It plays very similarly to Shadow of Mordor as far as combat, movement is a little more limited but it doesn't take away from the game. The story line is good also, giving us the classic Mad Max type villan.
Con's - A lot of the game is based around car upgrades, which worked well but not as great as I was expecting. You need scrap (which is found all over the wasteland) to upgrade most of the vehicle parts (most of which don't come until you do repetative missions to reduce threat level in each region of the map). Once you do these missions you then need upwards of 1-2k scrap to fit your new gear. Most scrap piles offer 5-30 but you can get perks to upgrade this. This made me stop playing the game once I completed it however it doesn't take away from the main campain. If you are at all into gathering collectables and scavenging, this is defenitely the game for you.
Overall the game is what Mad Max fans have been looking for. It is very immersive, its has nice subtle references to the films and as the strory progresses you meet individual and memorable characeters.
Final Verdict - I would say the game is a solid 8/10. Combat and story is great, car customisation could do with a bit of work and the repetativeness toned down a little.

The community is cancer. People will gun you down even if you are a fresh spawn or with♥♥♥♥♥♥tons of loot. This game can be so tense and fun sometimes. I remember I was playing with a friend and we were at the top of a light house. He looked down and thought he saw someone. I didn't believe him. I wanted to go down but he told me not to. Now the good stuff:
This game is so much fun.

Progressing is one of best thing I've experienced.

I played this game for over 2000 hours now, Steam Online/Offline and Console combined, so it's time for a short review.
This game is worth every cent and second you can put in it.
The main game is action packed, different and alway fun, at some points a bit repeating and often you can think of what'll happen next, tho. The story is pretty solid and good, especially if you know the first Borderlands and you find the little easter eggs. There are many places you can go to and you will always find something new.
The DLCs are as good as the main game, especially the Tiny Tina-DLC is even better, in my opinion. They have much content and you can see, that Gearbox put a lot of love into this game, even the DLCs (nothing that everybody does).
The Skins are what they are: Skins! They make the game funnier and you can find them all. Except the DLC-Skins but who cares? You can find so many heads and skins in this game that you don't need to buy the extra ones (except the Skins for the Siren, you need to have those!). And even if you buy them, they are only 99ct (Europe), so you lose nearly nothing.
Now to the negative site. There are many bugs and glitches, as you would already suppose. Non of them is really annoying (except if your weapon doesn't stop talking to you QwQ), mostly they are funny, but still something that could be fixed. I found about 5 or 6 gamebreaker / soft-locks. I know, that sounds kinda a lot, but it's my job to do so, so I find them, even thought I need to really try. And this is excatly what my point in this section is: The gamebreaker / soft-locks in this game are preeeeetty hard to get. Sure, you can get them by accident as well, but that's in like every other game as well.
Overall, I really can recommend this game, especially if you have 2 or 3 friends, 'cause the Multiplayer is really fun and works as smooth as Michael Jackson as a criminal. I recommend to buy the GOTY, 'cause then you have fun for hundreds of hours. But as I already said, there are many bugs and glitches, so if you are the kind of "gamer" that doesn't like games with bugs, don't buy it. The bugs are nothing big in particullar, and they could get fixed easily, but you know what they say: "You fix 1 bug, you get 2 new ones".
(P.S.: If you ever up for some Borderlands 2, just tell me, I'm always ready and will always go for another run! :D)

review:
Gang Beasts is an arcade beat-em-up game which is largely based around physics and not exactly meant to be taken seriously. You play as a jelly man/jelly baby, fighting other jellies in a bunch of different scenarios such as on trucks on a highway, or even on a giant bong. The default controls were quite ‘meh’, so I advise them to be changed. There’s a ton of different levels, such as Gondola most of which have their own unique ways of dying/other actions, such as Gondola allows you to knock your opponents off their elevator by you yourself using your head to bash their connector wires, and make them, yourself and their gondola fall to a miserable death. You can change largely how your character looks, be a bear, a blue bear, a red bear, other creatures. The main menu is empty, it only has ‘settings’ and ‘play’ options in the main menu. Not really that great. It could go whit a level editor, full on character customisation (maybe saving presets?).
Fun, addictive, intriguing, button mash to win. You can just simply bash your head against your opponent and win 8/10 times. Then kick their KO’d body into a river of their own blood. It’s hilarious what you can do, pick up a literal giant of a jelly (2.5x the size of your jelly) and just throw them out of the ring. Sadly enough, there’s no level editor as of now, so you can’t make a death circus, however, you can still laugh at the AI or your friends. Spawn mega-AI jellies, or bring your friends along to play a LAN match or few. Sadly it’s only LAN multiplayer, no servers, so again, a downside (but who needs friends anyway right?).

Spec Ops: The Line breaks away from the conventions of modern military shooters by focusing on a small cast of characters rather than a massive war.  The character arcs and storytelling are more coherent and interesting than most other shooters on the market. Cpt. Walker and his crew's mental well being only degrade as they unravel the mystery behind the 33rd Infantry's presence in Dubai.
Where the game falls short is in its average gunplay and enemy AI. The unique sand mechanic is entirely contextual, with enemies standing under or beside shootable windows that drown them under sand.
Despite its faults I strongly recommend this game to anyone interested in a horroresque exploration of a soldier on a downward sprial into madness.

I had my share of problems with this game.. at first.
Most of those problems were related to the repetitive sidemissions, since I'm a story-focused completionist. Thankfully, since I watched Fury Road before starting this game, the car, those little activities and the world really grew on me. And boy is this world lovely crafted, don't be fooled by the wast emptiness of the wasteland. Crearly a lot of heart and effort went into this game. A lot of movie-licensed games have a problem of capturing the atmosphere of the movie. And as a person that has played games for over 20 years now, I think this by far one of the best license-adaptations ever made.
From a technical standpoint, there is really not much to complain. On my medium-priced PC it runs buttersmooth and looks incredibly well. Some things (like explosions and environments) more, some things (like facial- and body animations on other people than Max and Chumbucket) less so. But I can forgive those minor complaints.
Overall, it really comes down to if you can live with the bare bones of a story and the side-activities. If you can, then this is a game that I can absolutely recommend.
By the way: I think it's a mandatory tip to not pillage the camps that have ONLY scrap in them. Believe me, they're not worth it.

I really, really enjoyed this game, and if the following words mean anything to you, I think you will as well:
Arcade platformer metroidvania roguelike.
Still with me?
It took me 102 deaths and 16.5 hours to beat this thing. Unlike other roguelikes, it's very probable that you will beat this game after investing enough time into it, thanks to a life-to-life upgrade progression system that other roguelikes don't possess. As Rogue Legacy is super fun to play, that won't be hard to consider doing.
Like most roguelikes the game's dungeon is different every time you play, but you can sacrifice a bug chunk of your money of your money (used for upgrades between lives) to keep the dungeon the same, keeping access to all the warp points you've uncovered, etc. This feature is theoretically good for fighting the game's bosses until you win, as they are very difficult and will take multiple tries to beat. But as bosses always drop a ton of cash, I never bothered with that. In fact, I effectively never used the feature -- not because I'm super hardcore, but it's just in my best interests. The more money I get, the faster I upgrade, the faster I will eventually beat the boss in its due time.
Even if you have played other roguelikes and didn't enjoy them, I recommend you download the demo to Rogue Legacy and give it a shot. As death is your chance to spend your money and upgrade your lineage; like it's the only way to Level Up and if you're an RPG fan, you know Leveling Up is fun.  This is a rare example of a game that actually makes it fun to fail.
If you like action platforming, the game is an incredible value with fun mechanics and charming aesthetics.

I started to play the game expecting it to be good (after reading review's and listening to my friend's opinion's i thought i would enjoy it) but wasent ready for it to be the game i eventually came to really have a love hate relationship with (but in a good way).
Rogue Legacy Launch Trailer - YouTube
You start of at the entrance to the castle and you are the first descendant and you walk in thinking "COME ON I CAN TAKE ON ANYTHING" 10 descendant's later your like "OMG THIS GAME ISNT THAT EASY".
But as you wade through and lose more character's you eventually come to realise that this is the aim of the game and that death is'nt a stumbling block but a means of progression as every time you die you leave the castle and then spend the coins you have ammased,therefore your character gets better on every new life and the game gets that little bit easier.
Eventually you will beat the game and go "I BEAT YOU",but then here it comes NG+ and then the game really start's.
The enemies are tougher the boss'es are harder (sometime's to the point of frustration) and its basically like you have started the game from the beginning again.
The sound's and music in game are great and do a fantastic job of making this feel like an old 8-bit game which in fact it is'nt (OF COURSE DUH),but the score for the game is so well put together that you would be forgiven for thinking that it is.
Rogue Legacy OST - Complete Soundtrack - YouTube
The 8-bit style they have gone for with the graphic's really does suit the game and compliment's it in fact and overall the gameplay is fair and balanced to the point that you realise that every mistake you make is your's and not the game cheating you at all (might feel that way but trust me all death's are your fault and the game is not laughing at how its tricked you yet again-SO JUST DEAL WITH IT).
Anyway in closing if you dont own this game "WHY NOT" its been cheap enough in the sale's to make it a definate purchase and even at full price is still one of the best GEM'S on STEAM full stop.

As you progress through the game, you will notice that the castle changes with each generation, and every time you die, you leave and inheritance to your descendents which they can purchase manor upgrades that increase abilities and stats of your character or purchase equipment and/or spell runes from blueprints and runes (respectively) that you have found in the castle. After spending some time with this game, it has grown on me. It does a decent job of filling the void from having a lack of Castlevania on the PC (the 3D games are dead to me), and with its own charm, has made me a fan.

tl;dr -
is an imperfect game, but it's amazing despite its imperfections and it's completely unlike anything else available on the market. It's also cheap. BUY IT.
:
As of a few days ago, the complete season of
is out... so what's the deal?
Dude...
:
Uneven but ultimately gorgeous. Low-rez textures abound, and some things look just plain ugly on close inspection. Luckily, these technical issues are often mitigated by clever depth of field trickery, top-notch lighting, and atmospheric cinematography, so the game is quite beautiful overall. Character animations--particularly facial animations and lip syncing--have also received massive improvements this time around, so the game often delights in long, lingering shots of characters' expressive faces and subtle eye movements.
:
Due to the SAG-AFTRA voice actor strike directly coinciding with the production of this game, none of the original's voice actors could reprise their roles. So new, non-union VAs for everyone, with (mostly) positive results. As in many video games with massive amounts of dialogue, the voice acting can be all over the place, particularly for minor characters. The performances for Chloe and Rachel, however, are phenomenal and should be commended. This is definitely a case of making the best of a bad situation.
:
People familiar with narrative adventure games know what to expect. Lots of reading, lots of cutscenes with branching dialogue trees, investigating detailed environments, minor puzzle solving. But narrative games have to walk a fine line concerning gameplay. Too much gameplay distracts from the story, but too little makes you wonder why you're even holding that controller. That said,
does a great job of finding ways to incorportate its gameplay cleverly into character development and plot progression. As such, it rarely feels tacked on or extraneous.
A good example is the backtalk system. Backtalk is a new addition to the series, and it's essentially argument turned into gameplay. You listen to what your "opponent" says and quickly select the best response. If you're clever or persuasive enough, some situations are more likely to work in your favor. If you fail... well, you may have just ruined a relationship for nothing. It adds exciting variety to otherwise standard dialogue tree conversations.
:
Amazing. Indie-folk band Daughter (one of my favorites, so I'm definitely biased) composed an ambitious album-length OST appropriately titled
which ranges from atmospheric post-rock instrumentals to tear-jerker ballads drenched in electric guitars and heavy reverb. Some key tracks include "All I Wanted", "Improve", and "A Hole In The Earth".
The game also makes excellent use of licensed songs that range from wistful folk music ("I Don't" by Koda) to loud, driving rock ("Don't Mess With Me" by Brody Dalle). My personal favorite is "Through The Cellar Door" by Lanterns on the Lake.
:
has an incredibly rich and complex cast. The two leads--Chloe and Rachel--are some of the most fully realized and complex characters in gaming today, and this is a franchise which is proudly leading the charge of strong, complex female characters in modern gaming. The whole cast, however,--even its minor characters--will manage to surprise you, for good or for bad.
I'll leave this vague, though, because discovering who these characters are is a big part of what makes
so good.
:
made a name for itself by taking topics that most games don't dare go near and rushing headlong into them with complete earnesty.
continues that trend by carefully discussing topics like grief, sexuality, friendship, family, abandonment, drug abuse, mental health, and violence (both physical and more subtle forms). I don't think it needs to be said that it's refreshing as hell to see any of these topics discussed in a video game, but let me say it anyway: it's refreshing as hell.
:
This is another area where
really shines. I can't say much without spoiling anything, but the story is lean, exciting, refreshingly realistic, thematically coherent, and--much like the original game--heartbreaking. Have tissues ready. After each episode, you might find yourself in a deeply nostalgic, existential funk that I can only think to call the
-blues. That is, it's a story that will live with you for a long time after it's over, and if that's not a sign of successful storytelling, I'm sure I don't know what is.
It's also worth noting that this is prequel that's done absolutely right. If you've already played
,
will give you new and valuable insights into characters and setting, all while telling a story that's both impressively meaningful and completely self-contained.
:
Despite my gushing,
is not perfect. Some of the writing and dialogue can be stilted, unsubtle, or cringy. The production value can be uneven, and it's obvious which scenes got more love and which got less. Some minor characters suffer from the age-old bad voice actor syndrome. There are some plotholes and there are several important scenes that aren't fully explained, leaving the player to sort of fill in the gaps in a way that isn't ideal. And as with many narrative adventure games, your decisions don't impact the overall arc of the story so much as how you find your way through it. You will always start in the same place and end in the same place, but specifics of the story's interior will change depending on your choices. Basically, the reality of video game production means there are some casualties. Things are sometimes messy, corners are cut, or story threads are mishandled, but I'll argue that these facts don't detract enough from the entire package to worry too much about them.
:
I never thought Deck Nine's work would manage to live up to the quality of original by DONTNOD. It was a long shot from the start, but they hella delivered.
is a worthy addition to the story of Arcadia Bay and the people who live there. The game is imperfect, but it's still completely unique among video games and it thrives despite its imperfections. It's earnest, realistic, emotional, and poignant. If you played and enjoyed
, go buy
now. If you're new and looking to get into the series, this game is an easy recommendation.

The first episode was fun and interesting however some problems that were apparent in the first game still exist.
Problem 1
The game still has weird jerky movements with some of the characters and I think most of it is negligible since the subtitles and dialogue do a good job of distracting your focus from it.
Problem 2
Cringey dialogue has always been a problem in Life is Strange and Before the Storm is no exception.Especially in the first few scenes of the episode, also I will say that most of the cringey stuff comes directly from Chloe herself, specifically during the David scenes she tends to make these exaggerated snarky comments about her step father almost to the extent that even the Voice Actor, who did a great job, could not make it sound congruent because of how unrealistic it seemed. Nonetheless, the latter part of the episode was great, I enjoyed the DnD scenes and the interactions between Chloe and Rachel was captivating.
Problem 3
The introduction of Nathan and Drew was by far the most risible cutscenes in the game. During the scene, the jerky movements in addition to the somewhat forced dialogue felt lackluster in depth. This is the scene where the aforementioned Problem 1 stood out the most.
Problem 3
Personally, I feel the game can be stretched to five episodes because the character development seems too fast to be relatable and the extremely intense moments near the end of the episode felt forced. Almost as if the game is urging the player to feel empathic towards the characters when it is not earned. I could not see how a player who didn't play the first game can relate to such moments that were quick, polarizing, and evanescent.
Overall I would give it 7/10

Absolutely fantastic, one of the best indies I've played in a very long time. Rogue Legacy takes influence from the good ol' days of Super Nintendo and 2D Castlevania, then injects a fresh new taste of "Roguelight" gameplay. Every time you start the game, the world is randomised, yet successive runs (and deaths!) allow you to progress through an impressive skill-tree which boosts the next hero's stats/class. It's a fantastic mesh of old and new, and one I'd reccomend to anyone who enjoys a good 2D Hack 'n' Slash.
Pros
- Charming visuals
- Consistently funny
- Tight controls
- Rewarding sense of progression
- Fantastic level design
Cons
- Not all classes are equal
- Can feel like a grind at times
- The "Just one more run" mentality this game evokes will leave you tired after forgetting that it is 3AM and you should probably be asleep by now.

If you can press on though, a wealth of adventure and content await. Once some of the enemy's attack and movement patterns are learned progression comes quickly. I found my runs increasing in time from a couple of minutes to ten, to over half an hour.
Combine that with an interesting character customization system and some good old fashioned looting and you have a great game.
Be warned though, the music will get annoying after about twenty hours.

Remember when you watched "Apocalypse Now!" the first time and suddenly realized this wasn't your basic war movie, but something that goes deeper and stays with you long after you close the TV? Yeah, "Spec Ops: The Line" does that same for the shooter genre.
The gaming mechanics and intensity in Spec Ops are good; fluid movement with a good cover system, nice bobbing camera and the immersion in the intense and lethal battles is very present. But were it for these alone, "Spec Ops" would be a mediocre shooter at best. What makes the game stand out is the fact that this is the first shooter, if not game that makes you question your morality at every turn and every squeeze of the trigger.
Based heavily on Joseph Conrad's "Heart of Darkness", this is a journey into the dark and twisted psyche. The beautiful post-apocalyptic Dubai stands merely as a setting for a battle that goes on within the minds of the player, not just the sandy dunes. This is a shooter that leaves you feeling nothing like a hero or even a good guy. And that is exactly why you should try it out.

As a choice based game, there's not a lot of freedom in what you can do, and limited choices that might affect the game. But the choices you make as the player paint the story of Walker..., whether or not if it actually changes the in-game story itself.

The good: Interesting set pieces and visually engaging scenes. The story is done relatively well.
The bad: Pretty generic third person cover shooter gameplay.
I would recommend it to people who like third person cover shooters or people who can atleast withstand playing them. Your in for a ride either way.

You would think, after reading so many great reviews and reflections that this game provoked, that there wouldn't be much point in playing it, but you'd be wrong. I knew what I was getting into when I started the Line, and it still hurt. I don't even like Military shooters, probably for the same reason The Line doesn't, and I still felt implicated in its vicious takedown of casual, jingoistic murder simulators. And that touches on the real reason every gamer should play this, because it's not really about how horrible shooters can be, it's about you. It's about what point in the game the violence becomes too much, and you have to decide whether to keep going. It's the gaming equivalent of smoking in a locked car, and getting to the point where you will break the windows open to get fresh air.
I thought I knew where this was going. and I still wasn't ready for it. This game isn't your classic rogue like, as the title might suggest. Yes, you die and your character is lost and you have to start from the beginning, but the gold you collected on that previous character allows you to purchase stat upgrades, weapons, armor, and more. If that's not enough, you get a feature fairly early on that lets you replay the last map you died on, with all the rooms still explored on your map and everything, but you lose out on a small portion of the gold you collect that run.
With your character being able to withstand more hits and do more damage coupled with you as a player improving with each death, you feel a sense getting stronger really fast, but it still takes some time before you're able to effortlessly plow through everything, keeping the game interesting.
I only have 2 gripes with the game:
1. Near the end of the game, most of your runs involve killing everything for as much gold as possible. It becomes noticable when you're grinding to help defeat the final boss, and you realize the progression gets slower and slower with each upgrade purchased (As buying 1 upgrade increases the prices of every other upgrade) The problem is, this is needed. Even if you're able to beat the final boss at an underleveled state, the New Game+ will tear you apart.
2. The New Game+. As far as I know, there's no way to go back to the regular game after beating the last boss. So this means you're forced into NG+ with much stronger enemies, and if you aren't strong enough you're going to have a really hard time getting the money that you need.
The main issues come in more toward the metagame, but even so should not keep you from the overall game experience, which is definitely worth it.

tl;dr -
is an imperfect game, but it's amazing despite its imperfections and it's completely unlike anything else available on the market. It's also cheap. BUY IT.
:
As of a few days ago, the complete season of
is out... so what's the deal?
Dude...
:
Uneven but ultimately gorgeous. Low-rez textures abound, and some things look just plain ugly on close inspection. Luckily, these technical issues are often mitigated by clever depth of field trickery, top-notch lighting, and atmospheric cinematography, so the game is quite beautiful overall. Character animations--particularly facial animations and lip syncing--have also received massive improvements this time around, so the game often delights in long, lingering shots of characters' expressive faces and subtle eye movements.
:
Due to the SAG-AFTRA voice actor strike directly coinciding with the production of this game, none of the original's voice actors could reprise their roles. So new, non-union VAs for everyone, with (mostly) positive results. As in many video games with massive amounts of dialogue, the voice acting can be all over the place, particularly for minor characters. The performances for Chloe and Rachel, however, are phenomenal and should be commended. This is definitely a case of making the best of a bad situation.
:
People familiar with narrative adventure games know what to expect. Lots of reading, lots of cutscenes with branching dialogue trees, investigating detailed environments, minor puzzle solving. But narrative games have to walk a fine line concerning gameplay. Too much gameplay distracts from the story, but too little makes you wonder why you're even holding that controller. That said,
does a great job of finding ways to incorportate its gameplay cleverly into character development and plot progression. As such, it rarely feels tacked on or extraneous.
A good example is the backtalk system. Backtalk is a new addition to the series, and it's essentially argument turned into gameplay. You listen to what your "opponent" says and quickly select the best response. If you're clever or persuasive enough, some situations are more likely to work in your favor. If you fail... well, you may have just ruined a relationship for nothing. It adds exciting variety to otherwise standard dialogue tree conversations.
:
Amazing. Indie-folk band Daughter (one of my favorites, so I'm definitely biased) composed an ambitious album-length OST appropriately titled
which ranges from atmospheric post-rock instrumentals to tear-jerker ballads drenched in electric guitars and heavy reverb. Some key tracks include "All I Wanted", "Improve", and "A Hole In The Earth".
The game also makes excellent use of licensed songs that range from wistful folk music ("I Don't" by Koda) to loud, driving rock ("Don't Mess With Me" by Brody Dalle). My personal favorite is "Through The Cellar Door" by Lanterns on the Lake.
:
has an incredibly rich and complex cast. The two leads--Chloe and Rachel--are some of the most fully realized and complex characters in gaming today, and this is a franchise which is proudly leading the charge of strong, complex female characters in modern gaming. The whole cast, however,--even its minor characters--will manage to surprise you, for good or for bad.
I'll leave this vague, though, because discovering who these characters are is a big part of what makes
so good.
:
made a name for itself by taking topics that most games don't dare go near and rushing headlong into them with complete earnesty.
continues that trend by carefully discussing topics like grief, sexuality, friendship, family, abandonment, drug abuse, mental health, and violence (both physical and more subtle forms). I don't think it needs to be said that it's refreshing as hell to see any of these topics discussed in a video game, but let me say it anyway: it's refreshing as hell.
:
This is another area where
really shines. I can't say much without spoiling anything, but the story is lean, exciting, refreshingly realistic, thematically coherent, and--much like the original game--heartbreaking. Have tissues ready. After each episode, you might find yourself in a deeply nostalgic, existential funk that I can only think to call the
-blues. That is, it's a story that will live with you for a long time after it's over, and if that's not a sign of successful storytelling, I'm sure I don't know what is.
It's also worth noting that this is prequel that's done absolutely right. If you've already played
,
will give you new and valuable insights into characters and setting, all while telling a story that's both impressively meaningful and completely self-contained.
:
Despite my gushing,
is not perfect. Some of the writing and dialogue can be stilted, unsubtle, or cringy. The production value can be uneven, and it's obvious which scenes got more love and which got less. Some minor characters suffer from the age-old bad voice actor syndrome. There are some plotholes and there are several important scenes that aren't fully explained, leaving the player to sort of fill in the gaps in a way that isn't ideal. And as with many narrative adventure games, your decisions don't impact the overall arc of the story so much as how you find your way through it. You will always start in the same place and end in the same place, but specifics of the story's interior will change depending on your choices. Basically, the reality of video game production means there are some casualties. Things are sometimes messy, corners are cut, or story threads are mishandled, but I'll argue that these facts don't detract enough from the entire package to worry too much about them.
:
I never thought Deck Nine's work would manage to live up to the quality of original by DONTNOD. It was a long shot from the start, but they hella delivered.
is a worthy addition to the story of Arcadia Bay and the people who live there. The game is imperfect, but it's still completely unique among video games and it thrives despite its imperfections. It's earnest, realistic, emotional, and poignant. If you played and enjoyed
, go buy
now. If you're new and looking to get into the series, this game is an easy recommendation.

The first episode was fun and interesting however some problems that were apparent in the first game still exist.
Problem 1
The game still has weird jerky movements with some of the characters and I think most of it is negligible since the subtitles and dialogue do a good job of distracting your focus from it.
Problem 2
Cringey dialogue has always been a problem in Life is Strange and Before the Storm is no exception.Especially in the first few scenes of the episode, also I will say that most of the cringey stuff comes directly from Chloe herself, specifically during the David scenes she tends to make these exaggerated snarky comments about her step father almost to the extent that even the Voice Actor, who did a great job, could not make it sound congruent because of how unrealistic it seemed. Nonetheless, the latter part of the episode was great, I enjoyed the DnD scenes and the interactions between Chloe and Rachel was captivating.
Problem 3
The introduction of Nathan and Drew was by far the most risible cutscenes in the game. During the scene, the jerky movements in addition to the somewhat forced dialogue felt lackluster in depth. This is the scene where the aforementioned Problem 1 stood out the most.
Problem 3
Personally, I feel the game can be stretched to five episodes because the character development seems too fast to be relatable and the extremely intense moments near the end of the episode felt forced. Almost as if the game is urging the player to feel empathic towards the characters when it is not earned. I could not see how a player who didn't play the first game can relate to such moments that were quick, polarizing, and evanescent.
Overall I would give it 7/10

Overall, even if you don't enjoy these types of games, it's a game which might change the gaming industry.

I played this game for over 2000 hours now, Steam Online/Offline and Console combined, so it's time for a short review.
This game is worth every cent and second you can put in it.
The main game is action packed, different and alway fun, at some points a bit repeating and often you can think of what'll happen next, tho. The story is pretty solid and good, especially if you know the first Borderlands and you find the little easter eggs. There are many places you can go to and you will always find something new.
The DLCs are as good as the main game, especially the Tiny Tina-DLC is even better, in my opinion. They have much content and you can see, that Gearbox put a lot of love into this game, even the DLCs (nothing that everybody does).
The Skins are what they are: Skins! They make the game funnier and you can find them all. Except the DLC-Skins but who cares? You can find so many heads and skins in this game that you don't need to buy the extra ones (except the Skins for the Siren, you need to have those!). And even if you buy them, they are only 99ct (Europe), so you lose nearly nothing.
Now to the negative site. There are many bugs and glitches, as you would already suppose. Non of them is really annoying (except if your weapon doesn't stop talking to you QwQ), mostly they are funny, but still something that could be fixed. I found about 5 or 6 gamebreaker / soft-locks. I know, that sounds kinda a lot, but it's my job to do so, so I find them, even thought I need to really try. And this is excatly what my point in this section is: The gamebreaker / soft-locks in this game are preeeeetty hard to get. Sure, you can get them by accident as well, but that's in like every other game as well.
Overall, I really can recommend this game, especially if you have 2 or 3 friends, 'cause the Multiplayer is really fun and works as smooth as Michael Jackson as a criminal. I recommend to buy the GOTY, 'cause then you have fun for hundreds of hours. But as I already said, there are many bugs and glitches, so if you are the kind of "gamer" that doesn't like games with bugs, don't buy it. The bugs are nothing big in particullar, and they could get fixed easily, but you know what they say: "You fix 1 bug, you get 2 new ones".
(P.S.: If you ever up for some Borderlands 2, just tell me, I'm always ready and will always go for another run! :D)

After seeing Mad Max: Fury Road, I was left with a deep craving to know more about the Wasteland. I wanted to explore the  different cultures, see what has become of our world. I feel that was the movie's main attraction. Not the characters, but more the world that allowed those characters to exist. It has been said that Max is not necessarily a protagonist, but more of a passive character with things happening TO him.
I feel the game draws from the movies in that respect. The undeniable star of the game is the Wasteland as a whole. The melee and car fighting are meh, the missions are meh and not extremely varied, but the reason I found myself coming back to the game over and over was the feeling I got as I rode into the world, seeking my next adventure. Reviewers have said that the game feels less than the sum of its parts, but I disagree. Take each individual component of the game, it's mediocre, maybe alright. Put them all together, and you get something special. Not GOTY material, I agree, but something that has managed to satisfy the craving Fury Road has implanted in me.
Another big thing I feel this game is not getting a lot of credit for is the technical aspect. I have a mediocre gaming PC. The best thing in it is an ATI Radeon R9 270x, which is okay, certainly not up there with 290x's and GTX 970-980's. The game runs like a dream. I didn't have to tweak a single thing in the graphics menu. Smooth FPS, incredible view distance. The way they stream content between the far-view of the whole wasteland and the regular view is spectacular. Hands down one of the best technical performances in a year marked by a series of catastrophic technical failures (Assassin's Creed, Arkham Knight to name a few).
All in all, I feel this game could have been more. I'm not sure how it could achieve more than it has, but from time to time there's that sinking feeling that in a parallel universe there's a better rendition of this game. But I also feel that a lot of this game's faults arise from the open world zeitgeist. Take the Assassin's Creeds, take the Far Crys. You have a map full of stuff to do, now go do it. That's the modern open world game, and I feel that Mad Max was built around that principle, in order to satisfy the current open world public. Maybe that's where they could have put more effort to make this game great. Maybe they were too wary to go all-out and create a crazy experience in fear of it being outcast from the open world elite. That would have been something special. Embracing the very essence of the Wasteland in order to recreate it.

Mad Max:
~~~~~~~~

In a post-apocalyptic world when sand dunes have replaced pretty much everything, this world is brutal and vast! Only a skilled and fearless warrior with a knack for driving can survive this ordeal. His name is Max, Mad Max!
You will be playing Mad Max (no kidding), a tough guy on a mission to rebuild a new and slightly modified motor vehicle called the “Magnum Opus!” You will be assisted by "Chumbucket", a brilliant but strange mechanic who wears an unusual jewellery piece, a spark plug necklace!
This game really reminds me of a mixture of a few games:  Shadow of Mordor for how the map is laid out, and instead of climbing towers to view an area, you take a trip on a small hot air balloon to pin point locations on the map; and the Batman series for the combat system. Great story line with well-designed missions but if you are like me you will go through the entire area to pick up collectibles, scrap metal and project parts, or you could even go racing - MARVELLOUS!!
Make sure to collect all the scraps you can find so you will be able to add on features to your “Magnum Opus” but also equip your favourite warrior with well needed upgrades. Upon achieving missions and challenges, you will be rewarded with tokens which you can use by having a friendly one-on-one chat with Griffa. He will use his magic to put you to sleep and then you will be able to increase Mad Max abilities.
In some locations, you will find project parts. These parts can be used to upgrade strongholds so when you stop there, it will regenerate your health, fuel and ammunitions.
Let’s be  honest, Mad Max is absolutely magic in regards to graphics and the game runs beautifully well. Great voice over, the controls are smooth and easy to master. Just a stunner of a game!
Positives:
~~~~~~~
-	Big open world and lots to do
-	Splendid graphics
-	Great voice over
-	Plenty of upgrades
-	Achievements
-	Trading cards
Negatives:
~~~~~~~~
-	Are you for real?

Mad Max is an example of what tie-in games can achieve if they have more than a token effort put into them. The barren wasteland world is beautifully realised with the landscapes reaching out from horizon to horizon. The core game mechanics are mostly well realised, often getting close to their more mature brethren from which they draw inspiration. For fans of the open world genre there’s more than enough activities to keep you going for numerous hours on end. For people like me though who aren’t so interested in the distractions the game is still readily playable if you do pretty much campaign missions only, you’ll just have to use your skill rather than your scrap to win fights. Suffice to say I was surprised by just how playable Mad Max was, especially given its tie in origins. If you’re one of the many raving fans of Fury Road then Mad Max is probably worth a look in.

Let me get this straight, I ve played many games, all kinds, some with hardcore gameplay, realistic at it's best with a learning curve who spans for years. from Tribes to Quake Team fortress, and old RPGs from Daggerfall to Witcher 2.
Bought it because it was kinda cheap and I must say that Euro Truck simulator 2 is one of the most addictive and immersive games I've ever played.
Not too realistic, no damage visible on car, no explosions when you're carring some petrol or acid.
It's not spectacular at all, it's slow.
The most important (to me) factor who contributes on fun and enjoyement is exploration, and Euro truck with or without map mods is one of the biggest open world, with nice variety very good landscapes and a sense of detail on environment, road works, trains, farms, small villages, forests, mountain trails it takes about 1 hour and a half, maybe more to cross the map from one point in Europe to the opposite. the driving model is very solid, not as complex as car sims like Asseto corsa or GTR2 but it's there, sometimes it's slipperly, your truck may collapse, you have to be aware check your rear view mirrors, incoming cars trucks, reckless cars, speed limits and so on..
Everything is there, almost - turn indicators, windshield wipers, gas, repairs, day night cycle, weather effects, fatigue you can buy trucks, upgrade them. you have different jobs, with precious trailers, fast deliveries, long hauls you can also make your own company, hire drivers and you travel across many countries in Europe. and that's it.
You can grab some graphic mods to enhance the experience, many mods are avaliable from traffic, to econmy mods and many maps.
Exploration and real enjoyement are there, it's a different kind, the gameplay on the pad is great to with vibrations who emulates the force feed back who is usually on wheels.
And to add, SCS is a great company, generous upgrades graphics maps, trucks, close information to the community I really didn't excepted such a gem, it's a refreshing change, relaxing and interesting gameplay with almost no flaws at all.
Try it.

(Ik that i'm like almost 2 years late to undertale, but i'll explain why)
The game is ok, it's funny at times, and the music is pretty good at times too. but what really killed my interest for undertale when it first came out was the fanbase. i haven't played the full game so my opinion might change in the future if i do play further. but was it overhyped? totally. i remember when it first came out EVERYONE was praising the game like it was made from the heavens by god himself. and that killed my interest for undertale for a while. but because i was really naive back then, and stupid, i would talk♥♥♥♥♥♥to almost ANYONE who liked undertale even a little bit. i would even complain about very LITTLE things that undertale had. and would hate on it without even playing it. why did i do this you may ask?
Well. when i was 13. when FNAF first came out, and when my friend introduced me to it, i fell in love with the series. i would go around deviantart for fnaf art, would look at fnaf theories. etc. and i remember when fnaf 2's trailer came out, i was very hyped. eventually fnaf 2 got released, and i liked the series even more. however, when fnaf 3 was released, i did like it, but things start to change. whenever it came to videos, i would reference fnaf almost ALL the time. and it got to the point where i even had a CRUSH on one of the animatronics in the games, (i'm not telling you who it is, so you find that out yourself) but anyways, what does this have to do with undertale you may ask? well while fnaf 4 was being made n stuff, a guy called "Roberate" started making videos about trashing FNAF. and because it was something not done much before. people liked his content, and tried to be like him. same with another channel similar to him. "I ARE TECH". and after all of that, the FNAF hate bandwagon was created. because of this, roberate quitted youtube because he didn't want to escalate this bandwagon since people on the bandwagon would harass fnaf fans for no absolute reason. the worst part for me is. i was part of the bandwagon for a little while. then undertale came out. at first i didn't really know what it was. but then when i saw it was being overhyped. i did the same thing to undertale fans along with other stuff.
but times changed, my hate for the game started to decline. i played the demo, it was ok. and today i finally played the actual game. and still. it was ok.
I don't hate the game, but neither do i like it. (atleast of rn)
if you are gonna buy this game and you are reading this review, go for it. but if you don't like too much exploring n stuff, then i don't really recommend it.
For now, i give this game a 7/10. the game is good, but it's not something life changing like a lot of people said when it first came out
EDIT: I've played the full game... and my god...
my opinions didn't change.
Again, it is good at times. however, don't really have much to say.
The gameplay itself is... ok. the battle scene gameplay is actually a great and original idea. it's like a mix between touhou and earthbound. however, it can be tedious at times too.
The music is also ok. (my favorite is the "Another Medium" soundtrack.)
In my opinion, depending on the series, it's kinda annoying whenever you're playing or watching something that can't decide if it's gonna be a lore based rpg game that is meant to be taken seriously, or a comedy/funny rpg that isn't meant to be taken seriously.
i'm totally fine with adding some jokes here and there to a game that is mainly meant to be taken seriously to make it more entertaining when you're not fighting bad guys (or sparing bad guys in this case, depending on the route :p ). but when you keep making funny 4th wall breaks and jokes on a game that is meant to be taken seriously, that's when it gets kinda irritating. i mean, you want your game to be taken seriously or not?
and because of the number of jokes/funnies, it's the reason why sans is popular. yeah, he's funny sometimes, but people should realize that undertale has other characters. other than funny skeletons.
I've also noticed that, undertale also can't decide whenever it should make itself look retro and pixelated like a late 80s to mid 90s type game, or if it should make itself look high quality like a present time game. (Nothing really major about this. it's just a nitpick)
And we get to the routes.
You know, i never got why the game makes you look like a heartless monster for killing some mobs. i mean yeah, you don't have to kill them n stuff, and you can spare them, but come on. can't we have other major things happen while we're on the genocide route? other than being punished for it? even if the enemy i've encountered is trying to kill me, the game still punishes me for "being a heartless killer"
and we get to the genocide ending. beating sans, killing asgore and flowey (asriel) and then meeting chara, after she explains some stuff, you decide to either erase the universe (which is really ♥♥♥♥ing extreme for a game about peace and love) and then getting killed (by chara supposedly)  or not choosing to erase the world. getting you killed by chara anyways and the universe supposedly being wiped out.
so whenever it comes to the decisions in the genocide ending, they don't really matter. (to me, it feels like it's trying to replicate the original half life ending. except it doesn't really do that much of a good job)
The pacifist ending feels forced in my opinion. to most people, it's all emotional. but to me, all of the fight scenes n stuff feels so forced.
The neutral ending/omega flowey ending is the only ending i truly like. (since the 4th wall breaking stuff actually works here)
i could go on and on about why i don't think undertale deserves to be called a masterpiece. however, i wanna keep this review short.
In a nutshell, you don't need a great or (atleast) original storyline/character to please the tumblr/LGBT community.
To people who want to play a good game with a bunch of humor and 4th wall breaks here and there and an ok storyline, this game is for you.
yet to people actually wants to play a game that fills you with emotion with these characters. yet knows games/stories very well, then undertale isn't for you. however,
i'm not forcing you to do anything. it's your choice whenever you want to buy this game or not. this is just my review.
if there was an option where you could give the game a "Meh" rating, then i would give this game a "Meh" rating.
However, the only reason why i made this vote a "Recommended game" rating review, is that more people would probably see it.

INGREDIENTS
½ cup flour
1 cup sugar
½ cup salted butter, melted
2 eggs
1/3 cup cocoa powder
Prepare the ingredients: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Grease a 9-by-9-inch baking pan.
Make the brownies: In a medium bowl, combine the flour, sugar and cocoa powder. In another small bowl, whisk together the butter and eggs. Add the egg mixture into the flour mixture, stirring until just combined.
Bake the brownies for 25 to 35 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. Remove from the oven and let cool for 5 minutes. Cut into 16 squares and serve. Enjoy!

(Ik that i'm like almost 2 years late to undertale, but i'll explain why)
The game is ok, it's funny at times, and the music is pretty good at times too. but what really killed my interest for undertale when it first came out was the fanbase. i haven't played the full game so my opinion might change in the future if i do play further. but was it overhyped? totally. i remember when it first came out EVERYONE was praising the game like it was made from the heavens by god himself. and that killed my interest for undertale for a while. but because i was really naive back then, and stupid, i would talk♥♥♥♥♥♥to almost ANYONE who liked undertale even a little bit. i would even complain about very LITTLE things that undertale had. and would hate on it without even playing it. why did i do this you may ask?
Well. when i was 13. when FNAF first came out, and when my friend introduced me to it, i fell in love with the series. i would go around deviantart for fnaf art, would look at fnaf theories. etc. and i remember when fnaf 2's trailer came out, i was very hyped. eventually fnaf 2 got released, and i liked the series even more. however, when fnaf 3 was released, i did like it, but things start to change. whenever it came to videos, i would reference fnaf almost ALL the time. and it got to the point where i even had a CRUSH on one of the animatronics in the games, (i'm not telling you who it is, so you find that out yourself) but anyways, what does this have to do with undertale you may ask? well while fnaf 4 was being made n stuff, a guy called "Roberate" started making videos about trashing FNAF. and because it was something not done much before. people liked his content, and tried to be like him. same with another channel similar to him. "I ARE TECH". and after all of that, the FNAF hate bandwagon was created. because of this, roberate quitted youtube because he didn't want to escalate this bandwagon since people on the bandwagon would harass fnaf fans for no absolute reason. the worst part for me is. i was part of the bandwagon for a little while. then undertale came out. at first i didn't really know what it was. but then when i saw it was being overhyped. i did the same thing to undertale fans along with other stuff.
but times changed, my hate for the game started to decline. i played the demo, it was ok. and today i finally played the actual game. and still. it was ok.
I don't hate the game, but neither do i like it. (atleast of rn)
if you are gonna buy this game and you are reading this review, go for it. but if you don't like too much exploring n stuff, then i don't really recommend it.
For now, i give this game a 7/10. the game is good, but it's not something life changing like a lot of people said when it first came out
EDIT: I've played the full game... and my god...
my opinions didn't change.
Again, it is good at times. however, don't really have much to say.
The gameplay itself is... ok. the battle scene gameplay is actually a great and original idea. it's like a mix between touhou and earthbound. however, it can be tedious at times too.
The music is also ok. (my favorite is the "Another Medium" soundtrack.)
In my opinion, depending on the series, it's kinda annoying whenever you're playing or watching something that can't decide if it's gonna be a lore based rpg game that is meant to be taken seriously, or a comedy/funny rpg that isn't meant to be taken seriously.
i'm totally fine with adding some jokes here and there to a game that is mainly meant to be taken seriously to make it more entertaining when you're not fighting bad guys (or sparing bad guys in this case, depending on the route :p ). but when you keep making funny 4th wall breaks and jokes on a game that is meant to be taken seriously, that's when it gets kinda irritating. i mean, you want your game to be taken seriously or not?
and because of the number of jokes/funnies, it's the reason why sans is popular. yeah, he's funny sometimes, but people should realize that undertale has other characters. other than funny skeletons.
I've also noticed that, undertale also can't decide whenever it should make itself look retro and pixelated like a late 80s to mid 90s type game, or if it should make itself look high quality like a present time game. (Nothing really major about this. it's just a nitpick)
And we get to the routes.
You know, i never got why the game makes you look like a heartless monster for killing some mobs. i mean yeah, you don't have to kill them n stuff, and you can spare them, but come on. can't we have other major things happen while we're on the genocide route? other than being punished for it? even if the enemy i've encountered is trying to kill me, the game still punishes me for "being a heartless killer"
and we get to the genocide ending. beating sans, killing asgore and flowey (asriel) and then meeting chara, after she explains some stuff, you decide to either erase the universe (which is really ♥♥♥♥ing extreme for a game about peace and love) and then getting killed (by chara supposedly)  or not choosing to erase the world. getting you killed by chara anyways and the universe supposedly being wiped out.
so whenever it comes to the decisions in the genocide ending, they don't really matter. (to me, it feels like it's trying to replicate the original half life ending. except it doesn't really do that much of a good job)
The pacifist ending feels forced in my opinion. to most people, it's all emotional. but to me, all of the fight scenes n stuff feels so forced.
The neutral ending/omega flowey ending is the only ending i truly like. (since the 4th wall breaking stuff actually works here)
i could go on and on about why i don't think undertale deserves to be called a masterpiece. however, i wanna keep this review short.
In a nutshell, you don't need a great or (atleast) original storyline/character to please the tumblr/LGBT community.
To people who want to play a good game with a bunch of humor and 4th wall breaks here and there and an ok storyline, this game is for you.
yet to people actually wants to play a game that fills you with emotion with these characters. yet knows games/stories very well, then undertale isn't for you. however,
i'm not forcing you to do anything. it's your choice whenever you want to buy this game or not. this is just my review.
if there was an option where you could give the game a "Meh" rating, then i would give this game a "Meh" rating.
However, the only reason why i made this vote a "Recommended game" rating review, is that more people would probably see it.

Running off the reservation never meant so much, nor has it held such high consequence!  (whichever higher power you believe) help us... help me.. I have sinned while pursuing absolution and purity.  I have never felt so good, yet, felt so disgusted in myself... over a game.  If you are paying attention to the story, and not just the enemy, you will be left stunned, if not in utter disgust, and shock.... in yourself.

Refreshing, and Disturbing in one, final, blood drenched breathe.  Finally I have found a Shooter that challenges your Dexterity, Aptitude AND Mind!
Don't be a brain-dead nitwit - find the mental challenge, and face your Demons!
