Now, I was a massive fan of the first game. And if you enjoyed it, you will probably enjoy Before the Storm. Though the dialogue is a bit clunky in the beginning, BtS makes up for any occasional misteps in the complex characterization, beautiful design, thoughtful descsions, and some interesting new mechanics.
Pros:
-"Back talk" is a new mechanic, meant to replace rewind, adding intense mini dialogue sections to navigate, and it actually works well.
-Cloe's new voice actress has excellent range, even if it takes a bit to adjust ot the new sound.
-The story isn't interested in just showing what we already know about Rachael and Cloe, or simply filling in backstory. It goes in a different direction.
-The writing, for the most part, is clever, and on point.
-Whoever designed the visuals of the game is brilliant, with plenty of fantastic and breathtaking moments.
-The new characters that have been introduced seem interesting and complex.
-And yes, Rachael Amber is awesome, but not perfect, which is important.
-There are also some nice mechanical touches, such as using WSAD to select actions rather than the awkward drag to select in the original
Cons:
Again, sometimes Cloe is a bit awkward in her angst, and the attempt to make her sound "cool" fails.
On occasion, the inclusion of characters from the main game seems forced, as if they are trying to do a role call. However, generally it feels more like a reference than a forced inclusion.
Obviously, it's hard to tell at first blush, and there are still two episodes to go, but at the moment it seems that BtS does a good job actually adding to the fiction of LiS and retaining it's themes while having it's own distinct atmosphere and additions to the gameplay.

So this review is coming from someone originallywho used to think this game was overrated and just a meme, I can say that I was absolutely wrong.
TL ; DR // UnderTale is an rpg-ish game that is VERY rich in story, OST, gameplay mechanics, and an amazing overall theme/message. Do I recommend this? Absolutely. I've spent about almost 5 hours on my first run, and plan on doing two more for the alternate endings.
Now to the actual review.
You're a human who, one day, wakes up in an "underground" world full of monsters. After being attacked by a ♥♥♥♥ing flower, you are taken in by a mother-figure who states that as cruel as this world may seem, you must always be kind to one another. On your journey back home, you meet friends / enemies / friends-turned-enemies and vice versa (honestly, this depends on how you play). The farther you go, the deeper the story becomes. You start to learn more about the underground: how it's come to be, interactions and relations with humans, its inhabitants, and much much more.
UnderTale adds a little spin to the typical turn-based RPG game style that we know and love. On your turns, you can choose to FIGHT (This consists of dealing damage obviously. This is where you gain XP.) / ACT (This consists of talking, joking, cleaning, etc) / ITEM (Healing, Equipping, Etc.) / MERCY (This consists of giving "mercy" or fleeing the fight. Neither option gives XP while fleeing gives no currency). During the enemy's turn, your little heart (representing your soul) is bombarded with different attacks unique to each type of character. Ex: a frog's attacks will be very much easier compared to a certain skeleton
Most fights can be avoided/resolved through both fighting and sparing/fleeing; however, certain enemies need to be interacted with in a certain way before sparing them.
Aside from that, there are multiple puzzles that are used to A) progress B) add some humour C) reward you granted you complete the puzzle.
Another mechanic that I just loved, was the fact that your choices do affect how the story goes. Ex: if you bring a certain item(s) with you til the end, a conversation might have a few more lines of text / if you kill or spare certain characters, others will remember that.
Correct me if i'm wrong, but I'm pretty sure the OST was written by (the game dev) Toby Fox himself. That aside, I feel like every song fits perfectly with the situation, as I can't see any other song matching. In a nutshell, the soundtrack is a lot of acoustics, piano, and 8-bit-like sounds. None of the soungs are longer than 7 minutes, (frankly, most of them are less than 3) but this isn't even an issue (as I think they're replayed until the certain scene/fight is completed).
Firstly, themes of a story can be interpereted in a multitude of ways. So let me state that this is opinionated and up for debate.
For the overall story, I'd have to say the theme was that hope and love
. At the beginning, you wake up in a world and there's two figures telling you two separate ideals. That the world before you is a dog-eat-dog world, or that everyone deserves love and bringing mercy to the world will make it a better place. These parallels can be used to compare the "underground" to the world we live in today. There will always be people set out to ruin the day or people who aren't afraid to stomp on someone to reach their goals
. However, there is also the fact that if you "turn the other cheek" and meet insult/pain without revenge/hate

As for the characters themselves, there is a plethora of personalities represented in each unique/main character.

The story is an adaptation of Joseph Conrad's "Heart of Darkness" which was the basis for the movie "Apocalypse Now" only against a Middle East backdrop rather than a Vietnam one. The Col Kurtz character is renamed Col Konrad, a wink and nod. The gameplay is decent and reasonably fun. The multi-player is nothing to write home about. The music is well done and exciting. This game is an absolute mind♥♥♥♥. I cannot for the life of me think of any game that goes and explores the dark corners that this game does. It isn't trying to soapbox about the horrors of warfare or the culture of the military person (things I expect some bored bloggers to get a hard-on about and overanalyze everything), it's simply a game that took the CoD-clones, lined them up against a wall, executed them, gave you ridiculously limited ammo for an actual challenge, regenerating health that's -slower- than the norm for actually intense combat, a decent (though sometimes annoying) cover system, and a final plot twist that will leave you reeling.
What I like most about it? You get opportunities throughout the game to do the popular "moral decisions" thing games like to toss in these days, but it isn't "Hug puppies!" versus "KILL ORPHANS". These are, all of them, morally grey areas, and just like the real world, the road to hell is paved with good intentions. Buy this game.

Allow me to tell you the story of Sir Lee: the first member of an aspiring Player's legacy.
Sir Lee was the pawn of the Player. He was a perfectly all-rounded Knight, but plagued with a severe problem; horrible game optimisation. After many minutes exploring forums, mashing buttons and trying to open the options menu, they were disappointed to find very little information that could help them defeat the terrible lag. The Player then sacrificed the resolution of Sir Lee's vision to attempt and remove the lag, with varying degrees of success.
With the lag defeated, the Player and Sir Lee were free to explore the castle. After paying all their money to some♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥blocking the door, they entered the first hallway. There, spoils lay strewn across the landscape, ripe for the picking. After greedily cultivating his compensation and looking at some book, they found themselves deeper in the halls of the Castle.
Suddenly, a fork in the road fell before them. They could continue forwards, go up, or down. Feeling curious, the Player ordered Sir Lee to go down: a decision both of them would soon regret. Sir Lee fell from a great height onto a pit of spikes, surrounded by fire-shooting ghosts that deal contact damage. With the newly increased speed after the lag-ridden tutorial, his combat training was worthless to the super-speed ghosts and projectiles reminiscent of Ten Desires' Extra stage. He took his final stand on a dumb puzzle of temporary platforms in an attempt to get out when he was launched by an eyeball into the pit below.
That day, the mysterious forces behind Rogue Legacy cursed Sir Lee and his family. For generations to come, all of them would attempt to conquer more than three rooms of the castle, and all failed horrendously. Dwarves, giants, homosexuals and lunatics alike fell to the numerous spikey-floored monster cesspools filling the castle. And on that final day, the day of the death of Sir Lee II, the Player quit and wrote this review.
As such, the tale of Sir Lee and his master, the Player, ends. This world, the world of a ridiculous legacy, will lie dormant for untold ages until the Player forgets the story of Sir Lee. Surely, something great must be hidden in this castle, this game. I, the Player, simply cannot get past all the bull crap to find it.

Mad Max is ultimately a quite solid sandbox game, with some flaws. The driving controls, at least on keyboard seem a tad bit off, I tended to just spin out on the most innocuous terrain. Also enemies tend to cheap shot you during execution moves which just feels cheap. There's a lot of collectibles to find and while I think they could have upped their value exploration is still worthwhile because they don't repeat layouts for camps and scavenger locations, Elder Scrolls this is not. The atmosphere is really good as well. Writing is pretty cliche and not good though, but Chumbucket, your hunchback mechanic is nicely written. It also lays the grimdark on a little bit thick, which is rather glaring considering that the movies aren't. Mad Max is one of those games that never truly achieves greatness though, it could have really been enhanced by stuff like Shadow of Mordor’s Nemesis System. (I have no idea why they didn’t seeing is that WB published both.) Regardless if you’re looking for a good sandbox game, Mad Max will definitely deliver and while it’s not PERFECT IN EVERY WAY, it’s not MEDIOCRE as the reviewers are saying.

A whole buttload of fun for Steam local co-op.
It is not online multiplayer and that is not a problem. Though devs have said they're planning it
Pros:
The whacky physics, controls, and general gameplay give endless fun for friends to sit around with controllers and beat the snot out of each other with giggly limp-arm jelly kid characters. A lot of sweaty controllers and intense button-mashing sounds with frequent roaring laughter and "Oh my god, WHAAAATT!?"
The art style stays a nice minimalistic and cartoony style to match the silly characters and the music isn't too bad either, though nothing really amazing. The game is really satisfyingly simple in all aspects.
The developers have also posted some really cool plans for the game and info on its development.
Cons:
-Updates seem to be highly infrequent. Maybe I'm spoiled from other Early Access games that update every week but 1-3 months for an update seems excessive. The updates seem to come with some good content though.
-Current 0.3 alpha build is pretty unstable for a lot of people (crashing, Waves gamemode not working, settings not saving)
-Camera system needs work. Even with 4 people in a game, there's only one screen which zooms in out and like other local co-op fighting games, usually from one direction. It causes problems because people can sometimes fall behind objects and not really know where they are and sometimes people can be cut completely off the screen. I'd think outlining people on screen behind objects and pointing an arrow to people off screen would help the problem, but no such thing currently exists.
Despite it's current unfortunate 'quirks', slow development, and minimal content, if you're the kind of jerk that hooks up 360 controllers and large screen TVs to your PC for friends to come over and get rekt, Gang Beasts is pretty essential to a local multiplayer collection.

Not too sure what to write here so heres a recipe for Pancakes instead
Ingredients:
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
3 tablespoons sugar
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon freshly ground nutmeg
2 large eggs, at room temperature
1 1/4 cups milk, at room temperature
1/2 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more as needed
Now to make it
1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg.
2. In another bowl, beat the eggs and then whisk in the milk and vanilla.
3. Melt the butter in a large cast iron skillet or griddle over medium heat.
4. Whisk the butter into the milk mixture. Add the wet ingredients to the flour mixture, and whisk until a thick batter is just formed
5. Keeping the skillet at medium heat, ladle about 1/4 cup of the batter onto the skillet, to make a pancake. Make 1 or 2 more pancakes, taking care to keep them evenly spaced apart. Cook, until bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, and the undersides are golden brown, about 2 minutes. Flip with a spatula and cook about 1 minute more on the second side. Serve immediately or transfer to a platter and cover loosely with foil to keep warm. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding more butter to the skillet as needed.
6. Procedure for adding fruit to pancakes: Once the bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, scatter the surface with sliced or diced fruit, or chocolate chips, nuts, etc. Flip with a spatula and cook for 1 minute more, being careful not to burn toppings.

Well after almost 30 hours of playing this game, I thought it was time to write a resume about my endeavours. It's the first time that I use my steering wheel+pedals (Ferrari F430 FFB) not for a racing game and the experience has been a combination of relaxation, concentration and just joy of playing a game with a serious note.
Although many features of this game remain to be explored for me, I can highly recommend this game for people who are looking for a relaxing yet long-term game investment. Doesn't mean you can't have fun when you start out, but when you get the hang of this game you'll want to progress.
It never feels like a grind, and is excellent at spending a few hours just driving around, doing your job.
Graphics are more than allright, although not superrealistic. However certain landmarks or road features like the "Soleil de Langres" on the A31 from Metz to Dijon are available for bigger immersion.
As trucking life is limited to 90kph I don't believe this game is recommended for people who love fast action-fast pace games. Can very well appeal to an older generation of gamers like me though.
It appears this game also has excellent mod capability for any kind of feature and features internet radio if you put it in your gamefolder. Personally I enjoy the yellow headlights mod quite a lot as it makes me feel like driving my own day-to-day car as well.
9/10 would buy again.

Fantastic idea.  I really, really wanted to like this, but as seems to be the norm with platformers these days, the physics are horrid.  Who in god's name wants to float around slowly, at a confusingly low framerate, watching things happen 1/3 of a second after the buttons are pressed?  For a game that really wants to take its cues from Castlevania (Castleroid generation), it's puzling that the physics feel so painfully archaic.
Jumps feel awful the entire game long.  Requiring me to hold down (and only down - which, thanks to every PC gamepad on the market, is completely impossible) to trip the platforms is asinine and doesn't work at all in practice.  The enemy damage scaling is hilariously abrupt - everything kills in one hit as soon as you change areas.  The checks and balances in equipment are too abrupt.  You never earn equipment badges from chests.
Ultimately, despite a fantastic idea - it turns into every other roguelike. An utter crapshoot, completely devoid of skill.  The fact that the game performs so poorly can only be blamed on the developer not properly optimizing it, as a low-res 2d game with nothing but light scaling and transparencies should fly at 60fps on an etch a sketch... Yet my surface 1 can't run it to save it's life on "max settings" (if such a thing can so be called for 2d gaming.)
Great concept, embarassing execution.  Uninstalling now - wish I had my 15 dollars back.

So, i have this game for like, umm, 2 hours and i have like one hour played? Yeah, sounds about right. Well, i was interested in this game since it's announcement, however, i didn't back it back then. And with this purchase, i realized how stupid it was not to back it / preorder it back then. 'Cause this game is absolutely stunning. For a comparison, it's more complex Sim City, but prison themed. When you start the game for the first time, you'll be welcomed with a 10 minute introduction which will show you how does the game system work. However, it doesn't show you everything, but this is compensated with the ingame wiki, but still, you will have to search for some guides on the internet. But that's just a minor problem as the game is still in the alpha stage. And that's what surprises me at most. I've never seen a game in the alpha stage that is polished like this one. Everything seems to work so far and there aren't any major bugs or glitches. The graphic style of the game is also awesome - it's little bit cartoonish and cellshaded - and i like that. The detail of every single prisoner is absolutely outstanding, too. You can view prisoner's bio, which is impressively detailed and so on. Every prisoner also has a name and traits, so the game gets really personal in this branch. Also with the new update, the riots have been added to the game, so if you won't keep your prisoners happy, there is a chance that your prison will change into a warzone. I also like the building system. Remember how in the games like Sim City, Prison Tycoon, Zoo Tycoon and many other games was the building only a matter of the single click and no waiting? Well in this one, you can forget it. First, you have to wait for the material to arrive, second, you have to wait for the workers to obtain it and unpack it and actually BUILD IT. This improvement adds that realism feeling to the game, and that's how i like it. Well, to end this review - it's hard to judge the game now, in the alpha stage, as the developers can ♥♥♥♥ it up or make it even better that it is right now, but in this state, the game is ABSOLUTELY AWESOME AND YOU SHOULD GET IT! YOU WON'T REGRET, I PROMISE!

There are many things in this game that make you think of the jail system in general. The game ideas of the jail system do not affect the game play. Worth a try even in its current state, don’t miss it on sale if you love this type of games. The theme is good, can be gory if you let it, and the way it presented its choices is very fresh, and makes it stand out.
I recommend Prison Architect if sandbox building/survival games entertain you.

I would say it is great open-world game, involving copious amounts of automotive carnage, brutal melee encounters and just about as much dust as one could reasonably expect.  Some may find the repetitive nature of the various camps and such to be boring, however we're not to "FarCry 4" levels of collect-shiny with this game.  A surprising number of upgrades can be ignored in completing the storyline.
While there are some deviations from the standard trope of open-world games regarding the storyline, it fits with Mad Max's image fairly perfectly, and adds to the continuing theme of Mad Max in a greater sense.  He is almost a quintessential anti-hero.
The only real negative which I encountered is in the EULA, "f.	You may not exploit the Game, or any portion thereof, for any commercial purpose;"  In laymans terms, this means that the quality and quantity of cool videos on Youtube involving huge explosions, epic crashes and the like will be severly hampered and the community disparaged as a result.  The best folks for this job are the ones who work for pay through monitization, and they will likely steer clear of this title given Warner Brother's track record with IP claims.
Effectively this will likely result in this game lacking staying power when compared with other titles of the open-world genre.

It's been a long time since I wrote a review, but I feel like this game really warranted me writing one.
The games takes place in a post-apocalyptic Antarctica, where a little robot named Suzie Crabgrass has taken controll of the minds of all 5 people that live there. The player choses and controls one of those 5 people, and has frequent visions of an angel named "Angelica Pickles". The mysterious Angelica is later revealed to be the spoiled rotten cousin of Tommy and Dil Pickles, the main paganists of the series. Angelica uses her powers of sorcery to summon a devilish minion that she refers to as Cynthia, and uses her powers to ravage villages throughout the land of Antarctica. Tommy and his band of misfits get fed up with her oppressive rule, and decide to whip up a resistance group called Third Eschelon. The open roads of western Europe and the UK scaled to 1:15 of the real size is the setting for the base game of ETS2. Kitted out with real trucks from such manufacturers as Scania, DAF, Iveco and Magestic, you are presented as a truck driver dreaming of one day owning his/her own logistics company complete with a fleet of vehicles and drivers to drive them.
In the begining your role is to freelance, driving other people's trucks moving cargo from city to city. From the position of the driver seat, above, behind or side views, you need to ensure you obey all the road rules and avoid any crashing. Thats right this is a simulator after all so you need to ensure that you stay in your lane, indicate to turn or change lanes, stop at red lights, keep under the speed limit, don't exceed your maximum driving hours and keep your truck fueled. Luckily there are ample stops and gas/petrol/refueling stations available along the way so that shouldn't be too hard. Just watch out for those 550  euro speed cameras in the UK, Ouch!
If you are unimpressed with GTA's driving realism and want something a bit more non-fiction, then ETS2 is for you. Driving a truck is more addictive than at first glance. Sure you are hauling cargo on roads, but its more than that. You are trying to kickstart your own trucking company, so you need moolah to get there.
If in doubt wait for a sale, but honestly even at the full price its worth it. Especially with the mod support.

Not too sure what to write here so heres a recipe for Pancakes instead
Ingredients:
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
3 tablespoons sugar
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon freshly ground nutmeg
2 large eggs, at room temperature
1 1/4 cups milk, at room temperature
1/2 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more as needed
Now to make it
1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg.
2. In another bowl, beat the eggs and then whisk in the milk and vanilla.
3. Melt the butter in a large cast iron skillet or griddle over medium heat.
4. Whisk the butter into the milk mixture. Add the wet ingredients to the flour mixture, and whisk until a thick batter is just formed
5. Keeping the skillet at medium heat, ladle about 1/4 cup of the batter onto the skillet, to make a pancake. Make 1 or 2 more pancakes, taking care to keep them evenly spaced apart. Cook, until bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, and the undersides are golden brown, about 2 minutes. Flip with a spatula and cook about 1 minute more on the second side. Serve immediately or transfer to a platter and cover loosely with foil to keep warm. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding more butter to the skillet as needed.
6. Procedure for adding fruit to pancakes: Once the bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, scatter the surface with sliced or diced fruit, or chocolate chips, nuts, etc. Flip with a spatula and cook for 1 minute more, being careful not to burn toppings.

Rogue Legacy has an interesting premise that sounds good on paper - and seems somewhat fresh at first - but doesn't translate well due to poor, dated platforming that is exacerbated by a flawed implementation of randomness.
The randomized nature of the characters, maps, and enemy layout more often than not ends up detracting from the platforming and combat. In fact, the maps are routinely laid out in ways meant to deliberately frustrate. The platforming elements demand a lot of the player in regards to precision and timing, and yet the controls themselves are floaty and imprecise. It leads to very short lives ended by frustrating deaths which couldn't be avoided.
Characters inherit or develop new traits, from benign cosmetic features to physics-altering gimmicks. While some are sources of mild amusement, such as flatulence, most do nothing but add an extra and artificial dimension of difficulty. For example, you may have "gigantism" which makes your character huge - it's difficult to impossible to avoid enemy attacks or navigate traps. So you chuckle, "oh hey I'm big that's funny", then immediately die and get no progression out of it. Ditto for "vertigo", which inverts the world and all controls. It's all just pointless and poorly thought out.
The short lives combined with a scarcity of enemy and platforming variety inherintly leads to repetition. It snowballs into full-on grinding before you're even thirty minutes into the game. To make matters worse, even the grinding itself is throttled by progressively more expensive unlocks and a mechanism that removes all excess gold from your new characters prior to re-entering the dungeon. So if you didn't do very well your previous life thanks to the poor controls or some gimmicky trait that hamstrung your character, you can't progress at all.
In short Rogue Legacy is a poor game, from general design to gameplay, and I'm shocked it is rated so highly. It's really nothing like the genre it claims to pay homage to. I only spent $5 USD on it, so there's that, but even five bucks seems steep for this game - I'd rather the developers had paid me to play it.

I have played every "Grand Theft Auto" game, every "Saints Row" game, most of the "Batman Arkham" series, "Mafia" 1 & 2, "The Godfather", every "Dead Rising" game, every "Elder Scrolls" game, "Just Cause" 1 & 2, every "Fallout" game... and I have to say that, although I enjoyed the HUGE open world experience, this game has a lot of problems as well as a lot of repetativeness.
Before I begin, I want to point out that I did say that this was a recommended game, but sadly after playing for 90 hours, I see that my over excited attitude was a bit misplaced and I need to change my review. For those who read this previously and agreed to it, I am very sorry, but for those who have not bought the game, please read what I have to say about this game.
PROs
====
1.) The game has a HUGE world for you to work with
2.) Lots of missions to accomplish
3.) Lots of side quests to keep you busy
4.) Lots of locations to go to
5.) Lots of vehicles to collect
6.) Lots of upgrades to find and equip
7.) Lots of great places to restore supplies (water, gas, etc...)
8.) Lots of hand to hand combat fighting
9.) Plenty of things to do outside the main missions
CONs
====
1.) Missions and side quests are more about fetching and returning
2.) The things you do are more repeated than seperate
3.) A lot of the required accomplishments are pretty easy (Although I played similar games)
4.) Combat is more hand to hand since you can only hold about 6 ammo for your shotgun
5.) Hand to hand combat is just 1 button while defense has 2 buttons
6.) Chumbucket will ONLY join you in the Magnum Opus
7.) Dinki-Di will ONLY join you in the buggy (Required for mine locations)
8.) Other vehicles don't really serve a purpose except possibly for the races
9.) The only real missions I enjoyed doing were the ones where you help build the bases up
10.) You can win the vehicles in races, but it's more satisfying to find them and steal them
11.) You can't have Dinki-Di and Chumbucket at the same time
12.) A lot of the locations which require destroying are not as challenging
13.) Overall, nothing unique about this game, a lot of elements are taken from other games
14.) You have to get pretty close to use the harpoon and gun when in vehicle combat
SOME THINGS TO CONSIDER ABOUT THIS GAME!!!
========================================
Many aspects of this game don't give the ideal concept of realism. On top of that, a lot of the missions, quests and other accomplishments don't give any real sense of accomplishment. The whole point to most of the quests are to lower the threat level of each region you enter so you don't get attacked as often, as well as to collect scrap, which is the games form of money to help build up your character, car, and outposts. Although this is actually fine, there's other things going on that don't show a sense of realism. For example, the fuel tanker routes don't really lead to ANY location on the map. To top it off, it doesn't serve any REAL purpose other than to gain a trophy and to lower the threat level. Why would a fuel tanker be a "threat"? Most cases, it's more of a threat to anyone who would be near it when it explodes. I even managed to steal a tanker, only to find out you can't have a fuel tanker for any reason. I find this to be a bit odd as you can get other vehicles, but not a tanker. I would think that if you designed a "route" that a vehicle is taking, it would do more than just lower a threat level. How about making it so that the tanker actually enters a building, and either steal it to gain fuel, or maybe destroy it so that the base it's coming from loses say electricity or the vehicles stop working after a while. (This is just one example) Clearly they didn't take into a more psychological point of view when making this game. These days, missions or quests should have a sense of accomplishment as well as have different ways to make you feel good in that it served an "in-game" purpose throughout the whole game.
Also, I noticed that "stealth" wasn't in the developers list of "Things to add in the game". Most games I have played offer some kind of way to "sneak" or "stealth" your way into a camp, base, even on someone who is walking away and can't see you. In this game, no matter where you are, you are noticed coming a mile away, even if you walked all the way there, you are still noticed. It's as if you can be seen and heard coming a mile away, especially in areas where it is almost void of life. I would have thought that this would be ideal for locations that have alternate ways of entering the base so you wouldn't "set off alarms". Oddly, the only purpose the "alternate" routes of entering a base serves is to simply avoid wasting resources to open the "front door".
Plus, the jump button is almost useless, as you only jump a few "inches" off the ground instead of say 3-4 feet off the ground. The jump may as well be left out of the game as the locations you reach have plenty of ways to climb up a high platform.
And hey, wouldn't it be cool if you could ride, say, a bike? Nope, no bikes at all in this game, even though it was clearly in all the movies. I guess they thought that since the enemy would only be using vehicles with 4 wheels, it would be a super disadvantage to make bikes.
My biggest one is why you need 2 different vehicles to transport 2 different passengers. For some reason there is no way to transport Dinki-Di and Chumbucket in the same vehicle, even  though it's clearly big enough for Dinki-Di to fit in the back seat of the car. I guess it was to create a challenge for the game itself.
The hand to hand combat is okay, it's pretty cool to be able to bash their brains in while knowing when you block and counter attack the next guy that wants to do the same to you. The attack and counter attack is a neat idea and works well for this game.
The extra DLC has absolutely no outcome of the game nor does it serve a real function other than to have another car frame. The DLC doesn't even give you improvements over the other car frames you collect.
About the only real enjoyment I had was simply collecting the cars 1 by 1. I have only been stealing them as well as finding them from certain locations which have special vehicles parked at the landmarks. Although I have not particpated in the races, I think I would have enjoyed finding and stealing them more as they offer a certain satisfaction after stealing them. From what I could tell, the only purpose the races offered, outside gaining vehicles, was to open additional "fast travel" as well as offered refueling locations for you to go to when you are running low on fuel.
This game starts out strong and enjoying, but you later see that all you are doing is playing "fetch the stick". So much repeated missions as well as so much repeated boss fights that this game loses challenge because you see the truth that you just repeat and repeat, over and over to accomplish all your missions and quests. My suggestion, wait til it's $20 or less.
OVERALL
=======
The main thing to remember is that this game is a lot of fun. Regardless of my rants, there's plenty to do, lots of things going on while you accomplish your missions, and more than enough to keep you busy. The only thing to consider is that you will be doing constantly the same thing over and over. The map is insanely huge so there is that. Lots of vehicles to collect and make. Plenty of places to go and side quests to accomplish.
HIGHS
=====
Huge map, tons of locations, lots of vehicles to find, plenty of things to keep you busy, and enough of a challenge to allow you to come back for more...
LOWS
=====
Tedious meaningless mindless tasks that, although help you get more scrap as well as lower threat levels, takes way too much time to accomplish while you are trying to finish the main game itself.

Players often express anger at DayZ by claiming that the developers don't care about the game or are taking too long to finish development.
However, they don't quite understand that DayZ's development as a standalone game essentially began when it originally released in 2013. While it may not seem to the average player that the game has developed much since, you'd have to realize that the build you see right now is only to keep players occupied while the primary development continues on a entirely different renderer and custom engine. In retrospect, the game has been in development for about 3 and a half years, which really is a relatively normal development time for most games.
This December, we'll most likely finally have the chance to be able to enjoy a quite different game from what we may experience now. Players will see what the bulk of development has accomplished over the past few years and I think everyone will be suprised to see the results.

Wow.. such an experience! The best 2d indie game i have played in a long time.
[The Game] One of the best stories that have ever been. It can be up to 5-7 hours of playtime before you finish the story but you probably have missed something in the past so 15 hours minimum. I wish it was more to the game,  maybe they will release a similar game in the future.
[The Story] For one of my favorite games i did not expect this game to be such an amazing story. Adventure with lots of bossfights, outstanding soundtracks, lots of cool items and just filled with love and hope.
[The Soundtracks] The soundtracks in this game is just legendary. When you first listen to it it warms your heart, you feel like you love the earth and yourself. I recommend the soundtracks highly.
[The Characters] I absolutely love the characters in the game. And its very fascinating too look at them.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The Human, officially named “Frisk”, is a lone child who accidentally entered the underground world while climbing Mt. Ebott, being the only human in the underground and acting as a surrogate for the player; always retaining a neutral expression but possessing immovable determation, willing to face every challenge on an adventure to reach the barrier. If the player decides to kill every enemy in the game, the human is revealed to be the reincarnation of Chara, the first human to fall into Mt. Ebott.
Flowey is the first character to appear and the game’s mascot. He starts off as friendly towards the player by starting the tutorial of the game, but gets interrupted by Toriel after he starts explaining that the philosophy of the underground world is to “kill or be killed.”
Toriel (also nicknamed “Goatmom”) is an anthropomorphic goat monster that gives the rest of the tutorial to the player. She is warm and caring, but over-protective towards the player; walking them through their initial puzzles and first battle. She is adored by some fans for her motherly nature.
Sans is a sociable but lazy skeleton that would rather tell jokes and pull pranks than do his job as a sentry. He shows a friendly disposition towards the player and may warn them as well. As is indicated by his name, Sans is based off the infamous comic sans typeface; his dialogue is written in this typeface.
Papyrus is a very determined but incompetent puzzle designer and guard. He’s set on capturing the player but only motivated by the glory he’ll earn. He has a confident nature and can also be persuaded to go on a date with the player. Likewise to Sans, Papyrus is based on the papyrus typeface in which his dialogue is written.
Alphys is a shy and reclusive royal scientist who watches the player’s progress through security cameras. Her personality is based on the infamous Otaku stereotype; she’s completely withdrawn to her lab and has an obsessive interest with anime and comic books.
Undyne is the captain of the royal guard and a zealous warrior on a mission to capture the player. Her personality is reminiscent to tropes from anime, as during her fight she: monologues a heroic speech about her motivations to fight the player, surplex a giant boulders because she can, and refuse to surrender.
Asgore is the ruler of the Underground. He acts as the game’s main antagonist; plotting to break the barrier and destory humanity as retribution for the war. He is however, while depicted as a kind, loving, and chivalrous family man; actually very depressed as a consequence of prior events. Although not directly a major character like the others, Asgore’s role becomes more clear as the plot develops.
Mettaton is an entertainment robot created by Alphys who acts as a flamboyant TV host with a love for performing. The player meets him after discovering that while Alphys won’t directly fight the player, she has instead added anti-human defenses to Mettaton, who will try to kill the player through television-stages in the underground. Later during the game, Mettaton reveals a new humanoid form with neck-length hair.

I'm sure you know the basic idea behind the gameplay by now.  You're a knight who is entering into your father's castle to do battle with the creatures that live there. Every time you die new children are spawned. Each child has their own traits. Traits range from helpful to making the game almost difficult. You are granted the money the previous generation earned to upgrade your character and purchase equipment to help you on your way. The castle itself is extremely challenging, and dying is ensured.
I personally enjoyed the gameplay very much. It's very challenging and you're going to die many, many times.
The good part is that you can purchase the upgrades to make the game easier to even those of us who aren't great at platformers can eventually progress. The upgrade system is awesome. The system the game uses to price these is right on, it allows you to advance but makes it difficult when you start looking to max things out or purchase the more expensive upgrades. This is helpful because every round your money is reset. The system usually has something you can purchase so your money doesn't go to waste.
Every time you die a new generation of characters is born for you to take your pick from. They each have their own traits and classes and it's up to you to decide which ones you want to play. So you favorite class might not always be availible, and you might be left with poor choices in terms of the traits they have. The one thing that would have made this better would have been if they would have taken into account more of the genealogy. It doesn't appear that breeding effects the future choices and they appear mostly random.
The castle interior is a great mix of jumping puzzles and combat. The room order is randomized each time you go in so figuring out where to go can be a challenge as well. It's broken down into distinct zones that each have their own enemies and challenges, as well as their own bosses. The controls are tight and responsive, making each death seem "fair" instead of due to game issues. The amount of the castle you can reach greatly increases as your character gains power.
The graphics and sound are awesome, giving you a bit of a retro feel with some modern twists. The characters are highly varied; ranging in height, width, and design each with their own benefits.
If you're looking for a game to sink some serious time in, but that can also offer you a quick ten-minute play session this is the game. It's a great combination of the long-term and casual gameplay blended into one.

I have played every "Grand Theft Auto" game, every "Saints Row" game, most of the "Batman Arkham" series, "Mafia" 1 & 2, "The Godfather", every "Dead Rising" game, every "Elder Scrolls" game, "Just Cause" 1 & 2, every "Fallout" game... and I have to say that, although I enjoyed the HUGE open world experience, this game has a lot of problems as well as a lot of repetativeness.
Before I begin, I want to point out that I did say that this was a recommended game, but sadly after playing for 90 hours, I see that my over excited attitude was a bit misplaced and I need to change my review. For those who read this previously and agreed to it, I am very sorry, but for those who have not bought the game, please read what I have to say about this game.
PROs
====
1.) The game has a HUGE world for you to work with
2.) Lots of missions to accomplish
3.) Lots of side quests to keep you busy
4.) Lots of locations to go to
5.) Lots of vehicles to collect
6.) Lots of upgrades to find and equip
7.) Lots of great places to restore supplies (water, gas, etc...)
8.) Lots of hand to hand combat fighting
9.) Plenty of things to do outside the main missions
CONs
====
1.) Missions and side quests are more about fetching and returning
2.) The things you do are more repeated than seperate
3.) A lot of the required accomplishments are pretty easy (Although I played similar games)
4.) Combat is more hand to hand since you can only hold about 6 ammo for your shotgun
5.) Hand to hand combat is just 1 button while defense has 2 buttons
6.) Chumbucket will ONLY join you in the Magnum Opus
7.) Dinki-Di will ONLY join you in the buggy (Required for mine locations)
8.) Other vehicles don't really serve a purpose except possibly for the races
9.) The only real missions I enjoyed doing were the ones where you help build the bases up
10.) You can win the vehicles in races, but it's more satisfying to find them and steal them
11.) You can't have Dinki-Di and Chumbucket at the same time
12.) A lot of the locations which require destroying are not as challenging
13.) Overall, nothing unique about this game, a lot of elements are taken from other games
14.) You have to get pretty close to use the harpoon and gun when in vehicle combat
SOME THINGS TO CONSIDER ABOUT THIS GAME!!!
========================================
Many aspects of this game don't give the ideal concept of realism. On top of that, a lot of the missions, quests and other accomplishments don't give any real sense of accomplishment. The whole point to most of the quests are to lower the threat level of each region you enter so you don't get attacked as often, as well as to collect scrap, which is the games form of money to help build up your character, car, and outposts. Although this is actually fine, there's other things going on that don't show a sense of realism. For example, the fuel tanker routes don't really lead to ANY location on the map. To top it off, it doesn't serve any REAL purpose other than to gain a trophy and to lower the threat level. Why would a fuel tanker be a "threat"? Most cases, it's more of a threat to anyone who would be near it when it explodes. I even managed to steal a tanker, only to find out you can't have a fuel tanker for any reason. I find this to be a bit odd as you can get other vehicles, but not a tanker. I would think that if you designed a "route" that a vehicle is taking, it would do more than just lower a threat level. How about making it so that the tanker actually enters a building, and either steal it to gain fuel, or maybe destroy it so that the base it's coming from loses say electricity or the vehicles stop working after a while. (This is just one example) Clearly they didn't take into a more psychological point of view when making this game. These days, missions or quests should have a sense of accomplishment as well as have different ways to make you feel good in that it served an "in-game" purpose throughout the whole game.
Also, I noticed that "stealth" wasn't in the developers list of "Things to add in the game". Most games I have played offer some kind of way to "sneak" or "stealth" your way into a camp, base, even on someone who is walking away and can't see you. In this game, no matter where you are, you are noticed coming a mile away, even if you walked all the way there, you are still noticed. It's as if you can be seen and heard coming a mile away, especially in areas where it is almost void of life. I would have thought that this would be ideal for locations that have alternate ways of entering the base so you wouldn't "set off alarms". Oddly, the only purpose the "alternate" routes of entering a base serves is to simply avoid wasting resources to open the "front door".
Plus, the jump button is almost useless, as you only jump a few "inches" off the ground instead of say 3-4 feet off the ground. The jump may as well be left out of the game as the locations you reach have plenty of ways to climb up a high platform.
And hey, wouldn't it be cool if you could ride, say, a bike? Nope, no bikes at all in this game, even though it was clearly in all the movies. I guess they thought that since the enemy would only be using vehicles with 4 wheels, it would be a super disadvantage to make bikes.
My biggest one is why you need 2 different vehicles to transport 2 different passengers. For some reason there is no way to transport Dinki-Di and Chumbucket in the same vehicle, even  though it's clearly big enough for Dinki-Di to fit in the back seat of the car. I guess it was to create a challenge for the game itself.
The hand to hand combat is okay, it's pretty cool to be able to bash their brains in while knowing when you block and counter attack the next guy that wants to do the same to you. The attack and counter attack is a neat idea and works well for this game.
The extra DLC has absolutely no outcome of the game nor does it serve a real function other than to have another car frame. The DLC doesn't even give you improvements over the other car frames you collect.
About the only real enjoyment I had was simply collecting the cars 1 by 1. I have only been stealing them as well as finding them from certain locations which have special vehicles parked at the landmarks. Although I have not particpated in the races, I think I would have enjoyed finding and stealing them more as they offer a certain satisfaction after stealing them. From what I could tell, the only purpose the races offered, outside gaining vehicles, was to open additional "fast travel" as well as offered refueling locations for you to go to when you are running low on fuel.
This game starts out strong and enjoying, but you later see that all you are doing is playing "fetch the stick". So much repeated missions as well as so much repeated boss fights that this game loses challenge because you see the truth that you just repeat and repeat, over and over to accomplish all your missions and quests. My suggestion, wait til it's $20 or less.
OVERALL
=======
The main thing to remember is that this game is a lot of fun. Regardless of my rants, there's plenty to do, lots of things going on while you accomplish your missions, and more than enough to keep you busy. The only thing to consider is that you will be doing constantly the same thing over and over. The map is insanely huge so there is that. Lots of vehicles to collect and make. Plenty of places to go and side quests to accomplish.
HIGHS
=====
Huge map, tons of locations, lots of vehicles to find, plenty of things to keep you busy, and enough of a challenge to allow you to come back for more...
LOWS
=====
Tedious meaningless mindless tasks that, although help you get more scrap as well as lower threat levels, takes way too much time to accomplish while you are trying to finish the main game itself.
Good fun for the price.

Mixed bag compared to the original but so far definitely worth it.
There were sizable issues with the first one regarding lip syncing, choppy dialog and writing that was mostly brilliant but sometimes cringe worthy. All those issues remain but the dialog in Episode 1 particularly isn't all that great. However the story and character building remain as brilliant as ever. No spoilers here but the Chloe/Rachel dynamic felt completely natural and developes brilliantly. There is a character thrown in that just feels forced just so they can create a dramatic scene but other than that all the major and most minor characters have deep personality.
Lots of nods to the original, many of which are important and some of which are just nice to see. You spend about 50% of the game in new locations and 50% in old but modified locations. Even still it all feels fresh and not rehashed. There's one particular thing that happens in an old area that has me wanting very badly to go back to the original game to see if it's there. If so it would very much change the way a scene or two from the original feel emotionally.
Overall this is Life is Strange in every way that is important. It doesn't QUITE live up to the original but is still excellent. For comparison I would give the original 5 episodes a 10/10 and I just knew immidiately after 10 minutes of playing that it was special. I would give Before the Storm a 8.5/10 even with some very rough dialoge at times. The story and emotions more than make up for it. It's worth noting that the quality of the dialoge definitely improves with each new episode. I had no issues at all with episode 3s dialoge.
[EDIT] I just found out this game was not developed by DONTNOD but by another developer. They did a GREAT job but as always you can very definitely tell it was not made by the same people.

it's funny how this game is like the chloe to life is strange's "max".
original had it's faults but it added to the charm of it, and it was very innocent in nature with everything. the music was calm and relaxing most of the time, the menus and journals all looked very genuine and innocent, which perfectly describes max.
this game is rough around the edges. everything has a dont care attitude to it. it goes all out with the cringy lines and stereotypes and even acknowledges it's there (frank pointing out chloe's spike armband and saying she is trying too hard, for example) and doesn't care, unlike the first game where it subtly had lines such as "ready for the mosh pit, shaka brah" that were cringy but added to the game's charm and innocence. the music is amazing just as the first, but rather than calming and nice acoustic guitar, it is dark clean electric guitar sounding music that fits the life is strange series yet at the same time differentiates itself from the original. perfectly fits the mood for chloe. this game just screams "the world and everyone in it sucks", which perfectly fits chloe's style.
the game has issues. the originals only glaring issue was that the lip syncing was off earlier in the game, although in later episodes it was not as bad. this game though has had issues with crashing, a very "off" sensitivity feel (feels bad to control the camera, sometimes i will even move my mouse but the actual camera wont move until i drag the mouse completely across my desk, it's almost like it has some sort of broken smoothing or delay or something), and the new voice actors just dont seem to fit their characters as well as the previous ones did (the only one that i felt was recasted well was joyce). another problem is that
it depends on you playing the first game too much, to the point that it even breaks authenticity just to cut straight to the point. something more minor as well that i was personally not happy about was that there doesnt seem to be controller support in this game.
also i want to point out that the new mechanics to replace rewinding time are actually a really cool addition to set this apart. no longer can you make a choice and rewind to try something else (again, fits max much better than chloe who is just a "do it or die" kind of person), but every decision is
permanent. it just feels different to make a decision in this compared to the original, and for that, they managed to really set this apart from the original.
in my personal opinion, its not as good as the original, but it is amazing in its own way. you should definitely play the first if you havent already before you pick this one up.

I've played Rust since Legacy w/ Zombies.  I've been here through all the major changes and the Beta of 'Current Rust'.  I've seen BP system go away, Experience System go away, Component System changes, Explosive Ammo Raiding get nerfed, Raid Towering go away (and then brought back this patch), and I've stuck through it all.
However this last patch is a game killer.  My clan of 18 players, which normally has 9 people at a time (half Euro, Half US), has 0 people on right now.  This patch killed the game for not only us, but several of our allied clans that play on other servers.  The ability to thatch onto other people's bases without TC access allows anyone to bypass all security.  It has effectively gotten rid of "Big Raids".
Normally, our clan would raid 20-ish bases between Thur (wipe day) and Sat.  They were offline for the most part and "Economy raids", and then we would find the biggest group on the server to "Big Online Raid" on Sunday.  It was fun building massive compounds, towers, and walls and then going out in groups of 4-6 finding trouble or taking down Helis/chasing down Air Drops.  This new change however isn't fun anymore.
A group of 3 people can now effectively raid any base they see with very little effort.  All Helk did was change the way people build (instead of tall towers, it would become mathematical formulas for "width protection vs height protection".  You'll see double-stack AIDS bases that are 40 rockets to the core and 40 rockets from the ceiling, and it will take a group of 20+ to build it (and not be able to do much manuevering once inside of it...)
If Helk had made it so only ladders were placeable within TC range, it wouldn't have been a game killer.  It would have actually been a good change in some regards.  But to be able to place down Thatch to climb up and over any base, is ridiculous.
After 4,169 hours in Rust, through all the changes... I'm finally done with Rust.  Maybe this was Helk's intention.  The real money is in mobile games.  Perhaps he is forcing Rust to die out.  In any case, I got my money's worth and met some cool people over the years.  Time to find another game to occupy my time.
If Helk removes the thatch building and leaves the ladder placement, I would come back, but it doesn't appear to be his intentions now or ever.

Rogue Legacy is a hard as nails rogue-like harkening the 16-bit graphical age. Everytime your hero dies you get to choose from one of three kin to take his or her place. Each hero is of a different class and can have up to three unique traits. Classes can be upgraded and as you play more are unlocked. Classes included Barbarian, Assassin, Miner, Knight, Mage, etc...You can also unlock abilities for all classes such as mana and health upgrades at the Manor. There are three shops at the Manor, an armory, a perk selector, and an engineer who lets you repeat the same dungeon instead of it being random the next playthrough. In each dungeon there are four unique areas  and several possible bonus rooms which have mini games such as defeat all enemies, hit all the targets, and reach the end without taking damage to collect special prizes (these are much harder than they sound). As with any rogue-like: you will die.... a lot.
My main complaint with the game is the character Death. Everytime you enter the castle/dungeon you must give all your money over to Death never to see it again. Which means you can't save it up between levels for higher priced unlocks. Did I mention, unlocks costs scale as you buy more of them. There is an unlock to reduce the price of Death but it is unlocked mid-game and by then if you have been buying upgrades is out of your price range.
Recommended for those who want to get thier a$$ kicked a lot to 16 bit charm

The concept of this game is excellent, but once you get up to (and past) the first boss, it all feels kind of pointless:
1. Everytime you purchase an upgrade the other upgrades become 10 gold more expensive. So if you have a bad run, you spend your gold so its not wasted (the game takes your money when you re-enter the castle)-- and then the expensive upgrades that you DO want are just that much further out of your reach.
2. The randomly generated castle is an artificial thing meant to extend the game's lifespan. You can learn about the (small) handfull of enemies in each area, but you'll spend 90% of your time in the first two zones, over and over, just trying to progress. Progression is stunted even further by the game's general concept. You get just a LITTLE bit further each time, or the castle generates a room full of spikes and you take 75% of your health in damage before getting anywhere. Better get used to that first room, mate, because those four candlestick holders and that chair are always gonna be there for you to hit every. Single. Time.
3. Bosses are bullet-hell creatures. Given this game's "tough but fair" philosophy and how easy it is to die, this was completely out of left field. The sudden difficulty ramp when it comes to killing any of the bosses will be like crashing into a brick wall, and made even worse if you're using a keyboard. The game only has five bosses, and rightly so considering how it all works, but the sudden spike in difficulty is not only unwelcome but punishing to the unwary gamer. I like difficulty so it's not a cakewalk, but I don't apprieciate having almost no chance at all. This is a cartoonish platformer, not Dark Souls.
4. No difficulty adjustment.
5. You can't use a mouse on any of the menus, which just FEELS wierd.
=-=-=-=-=

Pros:

- More Breaking Bad Refrences
- I get to play Dungeons and Dragons, instant GOTY

- Dream sections
- Basically Footloose montage of beating the crap out of everything

- Its unique
Cons:
-Had to verify files in order to get it to work properly
Episode 1: 9.5/10
Episode 2:
So I decided to just put the episode underneath eachother. So far I have been loving the prequel, and made me stay up till half past 3 in the morning. I think the second episode was a massive improvement over the first episode. I have seen some reviewers complaining about the junkyard section but to be honest I loved it. Seeing how everything comes together and the differences between now and when Max is there three years later. Also as a huge Shakspeare fan and actor myself I loved the play section of the game. Also the twist ending did catch me off guard. Finally the subplot about stealing the money made me want to cry (especially as a similar topic was discussed in the latest episode of This is Us by coincidence and it made me really upset - also crossover one day, I wish -)
Pros:
- I love Rachel
- I honestly loved the Junkyard scene
- The Money subplot
- Franks dog as a puppy is adorable and shows how much he cares about it
- The Tempest was a highlight which I will remember for a long time
- THE KISS!!! (aka fan service but I don't care theres a lot of that in this game)
- Fleshing out Nathans character, and actually meeting his father)
- The music was excelent
Cons:
- Backtalk was close to useless in this episode
Episode 2: 9.7/10
Episode 3:
I'll have it noted this is the first time since the first episode of the original game that I did not play the episode within 48 hours of its release as I was away. Lets just say avoiding spoils for this was a lot easier than Star Wars, another franchies that I am in love with but sadly have to admit that the most recent Episode (funny how that worked out) had faults. This is by far the weakest episode of Before the Storm. While it's by no means bad, its issues are blinding and frustrating. I don't think the sudden shift from escaping Arcadia Bay to find Rachel's mother was smooth, I feel it rather needed a forth episode for this so the transition could be more smooth. Another issue was how most characters story arcs wrapped up, either it was to convenient or non-existant/forgotten about. While I believed the visuals in this episode were good and the connective tissue to the base game at the end was nice, story suffered big time in this episode, leaving the story to feel rushed for a conclussion. Again back talk is under uttilized and is only used (not counting the pouding war) with Elliot which I feel brings in its own issues. Elliot was forgettable before the episode and I believe when I look back at this game, I will have forggotten about him and if by chance I do remember it will be because he is a cheap Warrin clone.
Pros:
- Chloe is still lovable
- BLUE HAIR!!
- Connective tissue to Life is Strange and that cheeky post credit scene
- Visuals were nice
- David is still amazing
- That opening was quite nice with the viewfinder
- Back talk is still an amzing feature but...
Cons:
- Choices meant nothing, it always ends the same because it needs to connect to LIS with only difference being a secret ending with Sera.
- Shift in story was not as smooth as it could have been causing major issues with almost all of the side character's arcs and other issues
- Elliot as a character and his whole section was unnecassary. He is also a blatant clone of Warrin but at least showed his stalker aspects (at least this time I did not have to find a creepy locker)
- ...Back talk is under utilized and has only one main use in this whole episode unless you trying to get 100% (like myself)
Episode 3: 7.5/10 (still higher than what I rated the new Star Wars)
Game as a Whole:
*Have not played Farewell yet*
Life is Strange Before the Storm at its heart is about the young Chloe and Rachel (and fan service) while suffering in its final episode, I still believe this was an amazing and emotional story even if its best fetures were not always used to the best of their ability.
Final score: 9.0/10

I started playing Arma II DayZ Origins mod 4 years ago. It was an
, so the controls were a bit ♥♥♥♥ed up, there was no melee, the zombies had super powers basically so it was recommended just not to fight them in close combat, etc. When Bohemia announced a DayZ Standalone I was super happy about it. Finally DayZ will become the game that I always wanted, but after purchasing DayZ Standalone, I was hit by a dose of reality. That game was unplayable. Like literally, the game was
: bugs everywhere, impossible movement, high-end GPU struggling with medium graphics, only the most basic gameplay was implemented... I ended up playing 4 hours and going back to dayz origins. I just wished that by that time refunds existed on steam.
Last week I installed again DayZ Standalone and give it a try. First I was shocked to see that
Okay, games take 3-5 years to be developed, so lets just assume that DayZ Standalone was released the first day of development, and lets not count the 3-5 yeras that Arma2 and Dayz Mod took to develop. After 3 years i must say the game is playable. Some problems have been fixed (some good, some regular), for instance the now I can play with High/Very High graphics and the GPU can keep up with it most time, (although Arma 3 has way better graphics and runs in Ultra). The movement now feels more natural although it still bugs a bit on small areas (doors, shelters...). Now there's vehicles. So the gameplay has widen up, now there's a lot of playstiles, you can go bandit (as always), you can go full survival only relaying on handmade arrows and agriculture, you can roam the map with your car...
. Before it's just like BI just released the game so that we can become testers, but not in a way to be played and enjoyed.
The game still have some big issues. For example, the lack of permanent bases really holds back a lot of players. At the moment you can hide barrels on the woods, and pray for it to stay, but eventually someone ends up finding it and stealing all your stuff. So now there only exists
bases, just to store food/tools when you go out farming. Also, I understand that it's a survival game, and they want us to feel how hard it is, but they should put more attention on the spawns. Some items should be everywhere, for example pet bottles (I assume on the middle east humans need to drink water, and not just from the tap). Cooking tools are also very hard to find some times. Like how can it be easier to find a bus wheel than a PET bottle or a cooking POT...
You get the idea. If you forget the fact that it's been on the market 3 yeras, this game
it's okay for 20€. I recommend it to people who likes to be patient and to farm a lot. I used to hate the game, but now it's actually a good game
If they keep developing the game, the result might be something good in 2-3 more years. The problem that I see is that ArmA II was released 8 years ago, and DayZ is starting to feel a bit old, with all the other survival genre games that have been released, like PUB, Rust...
I recommend the game, but only assuming you get it for around 20€, and that you have the mentallity that this is a Alpha game. I may regret this on 3 years when beta is still going on, but atm I give it a 6/10.

Haven't hammered a recent release in a long time and I'm glad it was this game. Now, I may be biased because I loved the film (even though there's not much relating the two besides characters and the same name) but the post apocalyptic wasteland in Mad Max is my favourite of all time.
The game is massive, granted it should be because there's driving elements; but it's not empty. There's tons of small hidey-holes where enemies have stashed their loot and you go down these dank holes and find old ruined Churches, or the inside to a house that's been buried with sand and collect the tasty Scrap and Historical relics, which give you some insight into how the world got into the state it's in.
Storywise, it's a bit odd. But with the good colourful characters and a good pace, it's enjoyable. Combat is similar to other WB games (Batman, Shadow of Mordor) except it feels a little clunkier on this game, but that's not where the true action lies; it's the vehicle combat.
I can't praise this enough, it's fantastic. The ability to rip off wheels, or blow up cars while grinding into others never gets old. Same with the customisation, granted most people will stay in a similar setup but the wealth of options is endless.
How does it run? Like butter. My rig isn't the best (GTX 970, Intel i5 2790, 8GB RAM) and it runs maxed out at 60FPS and the detail in the game is incredible. It's obvious the team at Avalanche really cared about this game and the IP and they've done it wonders.
I wish I could scrub my mind and replay the game, it's just that good.
The only *bad* aspect to me is the game does turn into a collectathon, now I don't mind this, this game especially as every camp/hole/base is different and detailed. But for people who have say, 100%'d Assassin's Creed Black Flag and other open world/zoned games it could wear off quickly. But again, not an issue for me.

UPDATED SOLO REVIEW
Devblog 175:
The rust of today is not the Rust anyone remembers, and to be honest that’s a very good thing. Sense its initial launch, this game it has gone through many changes with the vast majority of changes good while the minority falling on their face.
The game itself is getting prettier and prettier all the time, the mechanics continue to improve and gameplay continues to get flushed out with memory leaks getting patched and new content continuing to make its way onto the game like the addition of the armored-personnel-carrier (APC)
Developers of Rust continue to focus on features for team play or clans play while ignoring the needs of solo players. Devs clam that what helps clans inevitably helps the solo player. As a solo only player I can tell you that this is a load of ****. If you’re a solo player and your new to the game you are going to get wrecked, eventual it’s going to happen.
I recommend moded or community servers with 0 to really low pop count are the servers for new solo players with no experience in games like rust, or moded/community servers that are dedicated to solo or PvE only for solo players.
However, if you have skill and you got ice for blood, then a vanilla server will get your heart pumping from the moment you wake on a cost line, until the day of the monthly wipe, when you start all over again and it can be fun.
Overall the game is solid and continues to improve. Content is good and getting better. At this point I can recommend this game with confidence for people who are solo players thanks to the improvements made by the devs and the support of moded and community servers.
Original Solo Revue Devblog 158:
What we have here is a game that has gone far, far away from its point of origin that made it a game to be excited about.
The devs continue to work on optimization while adding features and gameplay. However, if you’re expecting a game setup for solo survival, you’re going to greatly disappointed. With an emphasis on clan play (or zergs), the game-devs continue to create feature and tools for large clans that dominate a server or servers. in a game where a solo favoring person could once have played for the fun of it, now needs to be in a team to survive, host a server that they can enjoy the PvE game play, or find a solo only server with an admin that enforces solo play for a solo player to enjoy the game.
Clans, however, now face no problems as the dev team has recently add new game changing features that brake the rules as it has been for so long. Now, no structure or base is safe from anyone and the rule book has been shattered.
Where I once would have highly recommended this game, the game is no longer worth getting into.

One episode in, and I already think I'll enjoy Chloe's series more than the original.
In terms of gameplay, it's still the same storytelling mechanic from the original series, except with Chloe's own unique feature of being able to "backtalk" someone into getting what you want. There's also a cool minigame of sorts if you are into table-top games!
The Max's series had the drawback that the developers were still trying to iron out how to use Max's powers in a storytelling game, which led to some weird and sometimes annoying mechanics in the first two episodes. However, by the end, Max's mechanics had been fully fleshed out, and gave a great ending to the series.
I feel like Deck Nine had already known what went right with the first game, and built upon it. The soundtrack is amazing, the storyline is more involving, and the new backtalk feature feels more exciting than Max's ability did. Just like the original, each character has a unique look and langauge that makes them mean more to you than their cartoonish apperance shows. I'm sure I'm about as far away from the demogrpahic that the developer was targeting as you can get, yet Chloe's story still makes sense and is interesting. Really looking forward to the next episodes.

Knowing this is pretty much an overall enhanced version of the 18 Wheels of Steel game developed by the same company which I played, like, 10+ years ago, I've always been wanting to play this.
18 Wheels of Steel Across America was the first one I've played and also one of the oldest (if not the oldest) SCS truck games I believe, and that game with its sandbox styled gameplay and of course, trucks, has impressed me so much back in 2003. This game basically builds on top of that, just like many other installments by SCS, with better graphics and more realistic simulation, and it has brought back that feel - solitude, driving through nights, accompanied by sometimes a nice rainy mood, and getting frustrated over trying to drop your cargo precisely but gradually become better at it. Euro Truck Simulator 2 has superb graphics, best so far I would guess, and it has covered about everything you would expect from a truck game developed by SCS. So if you're a fan of these games... yeah.

This is a game that actually takes it's subject matter seriously, but you can also just go and do your own thing if you're not really interested in the minutia of establishing a successful trucking business. The game suits whatever playstyle you have.
You can go and drive your truck around all over the place, smashing into things and doing silly stuff. Or you can do a few missions here and there, and try to earn some real rep and eventually establish a proper business. Then there's mission progression towards even longer trips that can give you even more money. I can definitely see how longer drives might make this game feel really tedious if you play it too often, but it's your choice whether to do them or not. Though I have found that the realism adds a genuine charm to this game.
Mind you, I'm using the most basic controls for moving forward and backward with my xbox controller. Here's a list of what happened the first time I drove my truck for a job -
1. Couldn't figure out how to get out of the truck lot.
2. 5 minutes later - Figured out I had to turn round' a bend to exit said lot.
3. Almost had a sedan run into my side before I realized there was actual traffic in the world.
4. Almost had a van run into me coming the other way because apparently traffic runs on the left side of the road in London (which I already knew... shame on me).
5. Arrived at the entrance to the destination lot. Had trouble getting in, so I decided to back up a bit. Rear end of my truck smashed into the front end of a sedan waiting behind me.
6. Took 20 minutes trying to figure out how to back up my shipment successfully into the designated space on the lot.
2nd Job -
1. Went beast mode getting out of the lot because I knew exactly what turn to make this time.
2. Made a wrong turn onto a highway lane just to save time, and didn't check to see if cars would run into me in either direction, because I'm a badass trucker. Survived.
3. Went by another trucker thinking how much of a loser he must be while treating it as a race.
4. Flipped my truck on it's side at a turn because I didn't brake enough or enter it smoothly.
5. Had to call AAA to get my truck right side up. Turns out they conveniently took me the rest of the way to my destination town since I was already so close ^_^
6. Held up about 10 cars trying to back into this new destination lot with people' precious time-sensitive christmas presents in tow. Took me about 10 minutes to finally get into this space.
7. Got reminded that I was still a poor person by the game although I had just earned money from two jobs... specifically like this: "Don't see any trucks on your garbage♥♥♥♥♥parking lot? That's because you don't have any, you poor ♥♥♥♥♥♥."
I got this game in a humble bundle, but I honestly feel it's worth buying alone for some truckin' adventures every now and then, although at a discounted price. It's even better with a racing wheel.
If you ever thought about becoming a truck driver, just... no.
If you already are one, I bow down to your excellence; Thank you for your service.

First things first, which also seems to be the thing everyone is talking about, this game is one of the best optimized games I have ever played. This thing could probably run medium settings on an intel HD 4000. Either way, my 370 runs this thing at high at an almost constant 60 fps. It also has nearly every graphical adjustment setting you can imagine. So, from a techincal standpoint it is awesome.
The world is beautiful as well. It may be a desert, but it is a very pretty desert. Everything looks good in this game, characters, vehicles, explosions, vehicle explosions. Driving is a lot fun, and the vehicular combat is what keeps this game going. That and the entertaining modifications you can make to your car.
The problems with this game are mostly story related. I don't really know what exactly the plot of this game is. It just seems that your main companion decides to work with you because your the saint. And nothing more is really explained of that and you have your companion who by rights seems to be the smartest person in the wasteland. This game is also extremely repetitive. After about three hours of gameplay you have probably done every different task there is to do, and you will realize you are just going to repeat these tasks over and over till you acquire all your car parts. Now, there is something really charming and comforting about doing these repetitive tasks. It's kind of odd, really. Driving around the desert acquiring scrap and punching war boys to death just works.
Worth the money if you enjoyed Shadows of Mordor at all.   The upgrading your vehicle aspect, and overall dreary beauty of the wasteland is awesome.

Though it's quite buggy and a lot of menu navigation and basic UI are missing, I think the actual gameplay is quite fun, and is especially entertaining with friends. I see this being a great local multiplayer game in the future, and it has a lot of potential.
[EDIT] Gang Beasts, while still in early access, has gotten better with the last few updates. I haven't followed the development at all, but last time I played it was still a lot of fun to play with friends locally. I hope it continues to improve.
