Prision Architect has a tough task being both a Prision Simulation game and a Fun tycoon game.  It finds most of it's success on the construction aspect of the game.  Designating different rooms, prioritizing security vs expansion, and giving challenges at a pace that is focused yet enjoyable is a strong positive to what this game can offer.
On the other side, the prison managment, there is still very little to accomplish.   During my playtime with PA, they have added the abiltiy to have prisions finish their sentence and leave, I've had prisioners start riots and fires, I've had tunnels that lead to escapes.  Yet, once I'm done building (usually around 200 criminals) I find it hard to not start over.
Typically i stick with a design that has been working for me over the last few alpha builds, so It is a routine.  I get invested and find small ways to improve my design.  Then I get back to 200 and get bored.
In the future, I'm hoping for more interactions with the prisoners, or some end result of what life in my institution has done.  I'm hoping for more end game content.  I get that it's called Prison Architect, but what's left after I'm done building, what is my incentive to build a prison thats more cost effective, or has less riots, or can be run with fewer staff when in the end I'll just give up on it anyway?

Absolutely fantastic fun!
Honestly, I have been following this game ever since it was originally announced. I have watched it grow, watched Introversion quite hilarious break things almost every update. It is a truly brilliant game, very addictive and I feel like i get  alot out of it. Whilst I have only had 14 hours playtime, I have barely even scratched the surface - my first prison, like everyone elses - was terrible. Second prison, I was learning - the third prison, I truly feel like I am thinking like an architect, thinking of ways to stop my prisoners from escaping and keeping traffic flows at a reasonable pace.
This is the sort of game that can turn from a peaceful getaway, into absolute chaos within minutes. For example, I went to get a cup of tea and left the game running. Came back to find my Power Station had gone up in flames, thus causing my water supply to dry out. This really did hack my inmates off, as I was literally performing a shakedown (search of all prisoners and possible hiding spots) and had everyone banged up whilst I performed some outer-wall maintenance. The end of it? A riot started - and my prisoners stole the keys off of my guards and tried to make a quick getaway. However, I was quick on the ball and had some Riot Police ready to sort out that little disaster.
There is so much you can do within this game, and you can get lost for hours without even realizing. If you think you're going to like this game, I can assure you, you're going to love it.

Really clever, innovative creative game that I'm sure a lot of people will absolutely love.  I respect it immensely.  But I do not enjoy playing it- I love rpgs and action/adventure type games, but this doesn't capture my (admittedly short) attention span for the following reasons:
-random encounters- while it's possible to play as a 'pacifist', you play the same mini-game whether you attack or talk to 'enemies', and the mini-game decides if you take damage regardless of whether you are a pacifist.
-checkpoint saving- relatively frequent, but there are TONS OF PUZZLES- replaying puzzles if you die while dealing with the above random encounters really sucks;
-slow movement- with random encounters which are redundant and require minigames, and puzzles, moving slowly makes this a constant test of patience.
Again, brilliant, clever game- it makes you think and is very thoughtfully put together.  I just didn't have much actual fun playing it.

Prison Architect is just a fantastic game. At the beginning taking out grants and building a basic detention centre can be very easy, but you have to make sure that you think of all the factors that could affect your prisoners. One wrong move and you may go in the red.
You have to gradually expand your prison, instead of allowing tons of prisoners at once. For example, if you have maximum security prisoners, you cannot accept them all at once in the beginning, because of how the prisoners will react to the little you have in the prison at the beginning, and you have to make sure that you accept prisoners at the right time, or they will just riot.
The variety of the rooms and programs the game has is just phenomenal in this alpha stage, all the extra activities and programs the prisoners can do and you can expand on really makes the game never get boring.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 is one of those games that, at first glance, you wonder why you would ever get into it. And, like any simulation game, there are probably some people who will still be scratching their heads after they've tried it.
But for the rest of you, ETS2 will suck you in.
The core gameplay is straightforward: drive a truck and deliver various cargo from Point A to Point B — those points being located in a plethora of cities throughout western Europe and parts of eastern Europe. This gameplay is easy to get into quickly, with a minimal understanding of all of the game's simulation features. From there, the game grows in a variety of ways that keep things interesting for quite a while, including:
All in all, Euro Truck Simulator 2 gets the simulator formula right. Everything that exists in the game contributes logically to the gameplay; the realism is highly configurable so that the game can appeal to a diverse audience; and, while not strictly a sandbox game, ETS2 gives players a lot of flexibility to play and evolve their business the way they want.
Euro Truck Simulator 2 has definitely been a worthwhile investment for me.

Mad Max: The Video Game. I don't normally do reviews but on the occasion I play a game worthy of a review, I will.
First thing to say about this game, do not be afraid of the minimum requirements!
Straight after checking the graphical settings and finding them all to be set to high, I clicked the 'new game' button and began to worry as I thought my pc would struggle to play this game. Oh how I was wrong.
It runs superbly on my pc (athlon x4 750k, gtx 760) with what i think is 40-60fps no matter what you are doing in the game or how intense the cutscenes are. My rig barely heats up more than what it is at idle, or that of playing something like csgo, which is very reassuring.
The gameplay itself is very fun with war boys to kill and camps to destroy. the more you progress in the story and the more missions you complete, the more upgrades you can unlock and purchase with what I presume is the currency in Australia, scrap (joke!). Scrap is acquired from detroyed cars or found in camps or loot sites. The game itself is quite similar to Just Cause 2 (if you've played it) as allows you to carry on after you've finished the story and try to achieve 100%.
The combat for both vehicles and hand to hand is very satisfying with very pretty explosions from wrecked cars and a combo-like system similar to the arkham games where you can continue fighting everyone around you by blocking their counter attacks and then unleashing fury mode which allows you to give much harder hits (again, very satisfying!).
All in all, a very good game that respects the original films aswell as the new one. However, as a fan of the films, the abundance of 'guzzolene' in a land where i thought it was a rare occasion to find any at all, ruins the survivor aspect of the game. I assumed that finding fuel would be like christmas but there seems to be full jerry cans everywhere. Thats probably just me but overall a brilliant game with endless replay value.

Don't be fooled by my play time on Steam - I've played a lot more than it says (I owned the physical copy for ages before registering the key here) and I can say it's pretty addicting.
Like most simulators, the game is based on a mundane task, and obviously this is based on driving a truck. Not everyone's idea of a fun time, I know, but it really can become fun if you put your mind to it. Or rather, don't. The reason I love ETS2 so much is that it's so great to just load up on a lazy day that I'm not in college and drive around for a bit. It lets me forget the stress of the real world, and take up someone else's life and just relax. Put some tunes on the music player from your computer, or listen to a nifty in-game radio that covers a lot of stations, even the more obscure ones like Real XS, only available in Manchester if you're listening on FM.
Unlike a lot of other simulators, the presentation is absolutely spot on here. The graphics look excellent and there are plenty of options to fine-tune your experience (even my decent PC has frame issues on the highest settings) but even on lower settings the graphics are better than the majority of simulation games out there. The mechanics are great too, and the physics engine really makes you feel like you are driving a real-life truck.
I do have a couple of issues with the game. One is that the collisions aren't very good/realistic and there is no visible damage to the truck at all. However, if you intend to play the game at all seriously, (i.e. not purposefully crashing into everything all the time) this won't be an issue. The other is that every time there is an update (and that is a lot), my truck gets returned back to my main garage back in Manchester, which is annoying seen as I've already explored the roads around that area (Great Britain). I feel it would be better if your truck was moved to the nearest city, considering they're not too far away from each other.
Aside from those couple of very small problems, ETS2 delivers in every area. Graphics, sound, gameplay and general presentation are well above the rest when it comes to simulators.

I originally discovered this game through Giant Bomb, the same way I'm sure thousands of others did too. This was back in early 2014 and back then the game had a few sandbox levels, a small single player level with bots and the typical stages we all know such as ring and trucks. Then things went very quiet for a long time after the release of 0.0.3 in April 2014 until the game was reworked and released on Steam in Early Access. As it turned out, the release turned out to be quite disappointing for a long of people as it was missing a lot of content the game previously had such as the sandbox levels which to this day have yet to make a return.

It's difficult to review Gang Beasts for what it currently is and what it can and should be. There have been a ton of delays and the devs have been radio silent at times which hasn't helped matters either. What I can say is that the actual part of playing Gang Beasts is incredible. It's some of the most fun you can have. Should it have online multiplayer? Probably but only to satisfy those that keep complaining about it. Local multiplayer games have been seeing a resurgence as of late and Gang Beasts is a shining example among them. Sitting around and playing on a large TV with a group of friends and trash talking each other in a way that often reminds me of playing Smash Bros. Melee on the GameCube. By just playing the game online misses out a core piece of why the game is so fun. Being in a room of others really adds to the enjoyment. If the game does get online multiplayer, that's totally awesome too and would benefit 99% of how people play games nowadays but do yourself a favour and at least try to play it with others in person, it's a blast.

Much like the cars in it Mad Max looks good but is a bit creaky underneath. This review will probably contain SPOILERS, but only for like the first five minutes because the games a bit repetitive.
First, the good:
This game feels so much like the Batman games I originally thought it was the same developer. Which means the combat is pretty fluid and visceral, you feel like a total badass and it never feels far-fetched that Max is more than capable of taking down ten guys at once.
The driving is nice, takes a little getting used to and the cars feel doughy sometimes but flying down the dusty tracks in your hand-built monster is a fun experience.
The customisation is spot-on, I was eagerly anticipating having enough scrap for some of the personal or vehicle add-ons and they all make a noticeable difference.
Now for the bad:
Mad Max _feels_ like the Batman games but it doesn't look like the Batman games, mainly because the camera is so poor in close quarters that you can't see anything at all. This can lead to getting hit in fights you should be walking simply because the camera decided showing Max and the dude he's fighting is too much work so it points somewhere above their heads. Considering half the combat is in close confines this can get very annoying.
Also the enemy design is lacking inspiration. For general mobs there's weak dude, melee weapon dude, fast dude with a knife and shield dude. OK, so there's the occasional suicide bomber and some weird "ferals" who come at you like dogs but mainly you will have a mix of the first four. Bosses are even worse, there is only one type: big, muscley dudes with melee weapons. Oh, one is weak to knives, one is weak to fire, the usual, but you end up beating them all the same way.
The vehicle combat is ridiculous. Either you will get ganked super-fast by some dude rubbing up on you or you will be wasting the enemy in seconds. There is no in-between, no long, ongoing games of cat and mouse. If you are in front, no matter how fast your car is, you will be caught. But if your car catches on fire you can bail out and be as dangerous on foot as you were in your vehicle. It makes you wonder why Max needs a car in the first place.
The in-game races are very strange, the other racers show little amibition to reach the finish line first, they would rather pick a fight with you. Just you, not each other and certainly not with the other cars you might meet on the road which will be drawn to you like you have a magnet as a hood ornament.
There are a few more quibbles like Max using his shotgun to bust stuff when he has a crowbar right next to the holster but that's more of a logic flaw then an actual problem with the game itself. In short, the game is fun 80% of the time but the other 20% will have you throwing your gamepad at the wall.

Basically, this is a cross between a Metroidvania and a Roguelike. Randomly generated castles, genuinely fun platforming, and a more approachable version of permadeath than your typical Roguelike. The progression never really feels like grinding, the controls are spot-on, even with just a keyboard, and the randomly generated advantages and disadvantages of each new generation keep each playthrough interesting in its own way. If you dig the Metroidvania format, especially, you'll probably find a lot to like here. If you like your Roguelikes "pure," you probably won't care for the permanent upgrades, or the fact that you need to buy a lot of them to unlock new classes. I don't mind it at all, but it definitely makes the game a bit more forgiving than it would otherwise be. That said, it's also a hell of a lot of fun, either way.
The Mac version has one pretty glaring bug. As of the time I'm writing this review, you will usually find yourself having to force it to quit; otherwise, it'll just keep running after you exit, and stay in your taskbar. Not a dealbreaking bug, but a somewhat annoying one. Other than that, it works pretty much perfectly.

I hope you all find this review usefull. After playing this game for almost 40 hours, I think I can easily tell you what is good and what is bad about this game. First we will go with the good.
THE GOOD:
This game is beautiful. Even if you can't run it at MAX Settings, they did a fantastic job. The world is huge, and if you can see it, you can get there eventually. Combat is similar to Batman, but Max actually will brutally kill someone and that is pretty bad♥♥♥♥♥when you do some finishers. Car Combat is fun, happens often, and driving around in the Magmun Opus is always a good time. I love watching turn into a machine of destruction. That is about it, the rest of this review is going to be bad.
THE BAD:
So much bad in this game, it takes away from a good game. I can see why it didn't break out into the 80's on the Meta Critic. Lets begin with the combat. Feels like Batman, but the camera doesn't help and guys fly off the side of the screen and hit you causing you to drop combos, not knowing when to counter and so on. If you are in a cramped space, just keep hitting X as you are blind because the Camera is not helpful by any means.
The Counters are BROKEN. There are a million little things to unlock to help you level up. The counters are broken! Just try it! Do something and watch as the counters don't move. I have had counters also reset and go back to 0 when I was a few away from completing.
DEATHRACES! This is by far my biggest complaint about this game. There are races that give you Griffa Tokens needed to level up. They start out very easy and go to Extremely Difficult and frustration real quick! It is more a programming issue I feel. First off, the enemy AI won't try to take out each other, they only hit you. All cars are pretty slow to move and get going and they will hit you none stop making it almost impossible to get to the finish line in time to get the token. Something always happens that is unpredicable. For instance: One race you jump off a cliff right at the start. Sometimes it might do some damage, sometimes I land and loose half my health, sometimes I land and spin out, sometimes all the guys gang up on me and I lose almost all health or tons of time. Randomly I have spun out, hit a rock, I couldn't see it and there goes a perfect race. The AI knows different routes to take, and you could follow but then you will not get there in time. Try doing it yourself and something always happens. Go off the trail and your car slows down to a crawl. One race has you in a heavily armored car and no matter how many enemies you kill, there are always 5 racers chasing you, hitting you, cutting you off, or hitting you head on. It is damn near impossible to beat! This is so frustrating for the person who wants to complete everything!
TASKS: This game has way too much to do and not in a good way. By the time you clear the first territory, you have to do it all over again, and again, and AGAIN! It becomes so much of a bad routine you almost just want to skip everything and play the story missions. Bad pacing, not enough variety, and you just start getting bored. The only thing is I am one who likes to get everything, so this has kept me going, but I don't know if I can finish this game as it is getting very boring now.
RUNNING: Don't even waste your time and effort holding down the right trigger. YOU DON'T MOVE ANY FASTER RUNNING OR JUST PRESSING UP ON THE ANALOG STICK.
SUPPLIES: This is a bad thing too. You are in the Wasteland with little water, supplies, and everything else. It makes you feel this way in the early game. Once you level up, get strongholds, just use everything with out worry. You will have all the gas, water, ammo and more you need.
Overall this could have been a great game with better balancing, better AI, and better race mechanics. So many little things take away from a great game. I can only recommend if you like collecting tons of stuff, but if you want variety, this game isn't for you.

A charming, often funny, and always deliciously weird game that at first glance may appear to be a JRPG (as others have noted, most like Mother/EarthBound), but is really more of a free-form improvisation inspired by JRPGs, as well as other thought-provoking indie games of recent years (Braid and Fez come to mind).
It's longer and more varied than you might think, and well-worth playing to the end.
However, be aware that you cannot experience the whole game in the first playthrough. Some call this “replayability.” I call it “annoying.” However, I promise you that even if you can only commit to one playthrough, you will “get it," have fun, laugh, and be provoked to think more deeply about accountability, responsibility, and morality.
I would also like to thank the developer for supporting Linux.

Basically, this is a cross between a Metroidvania and a Roguelike. Randomly generated castles, genuinely fun platforming, and a more approachable version of permadeath than your typical Roguelike. The progression never really feels like grinding, the controls are spot-on, even with just a keyboard, and the randomly generated advantages and disadvantages of each new generation keep each playthrough interesting in its own way. If you dig the Metroidvania format, especially, you'll probably find a lot to like here. If you like your Roguelikes "pure," you probably won't care for the permanent upgrades, or the fact that you need to buy a lot of them to unlock new classes. I don't mind it at all, but it definitely makes the game a bit more forgiving than it would otherwise be. That said, it's also a hell of a lot of fun, either way.
The Mac version has one pretty glaring bug. As of the time I'm writing this review, you will usually find yourself having to force it to quit; otherwise, it'll just keep running after you exit, and stay in your taskbar. Not a dealbreaking bug, but a somewhat annoying one. Other than that, it works pretty much perfectly.

I started off playing this game with a lot of suspicion.
Due to the fact it's barely been marketed, I assumed it wasn't going to be anywhere near "fun". Turns out I was wrong, thankfully.
Let's start off with the story; I've always thought that the Mad Max franchise would work best as a videogame, it just has that "weirdness" and exaggeration that you only find in popular game franchises. This game certainly proves--to me at least--that I was right in this belief.
You play as Max (obviously), a guy who has some mental issues (though not really hinted of much). In the first hour or so, your car gets stolen and you are left for dead. Thankfully, you come across a "Black Finger" (mechanic) called Chumbucket. He's a little weird, to the point of sounding like a religious nut towards Max and the car, he even makes one liners towards... urhh... 'romantically' loving the car!
Anyway with Chum's help, you set out to seek revenge and take your car back. The whole storyline is pretty much "We need a V8 engine to proceed". While it's simplistic, it works fine. Let's just say that the ending is quite obvious though.
The fighting system is pretty much what you'd expect in this day and age from an "open world" action game. It's very much a Batman Arkham system, though not quite as refined (more realistic, for example you're not jumping around the screen to keep your combo going). I had some rare instances that it wouldn't even register my key presses (using a gamepad).
There's not much else to say about it, it's pretty much as you'd expect from such fighting systems now days.
It's the car that is the hook here.
Using the various upgrades available, you can customise both the functionality and cosmetics of your vehicle. Like to go at high speed straight into people? Focus on acceleration, top speed and your ram. Like to get close? Make sure to get spikes to help prevent boarders.
While there isn't a massive amount of upgrades, it's still enough to keep most people interested. Vehiclar 'fights' are quite fun, much more so than the repetitive Batman Arkham fighing anyway.
The area you're in is a very, and I mean VERY, large section of desert.
It would take you anything up to 10-15 minutes to drive from the furthest points, depending on your vehicle's upgrades. Doesn't hurt that the game is somewhat nice looking too.
It has the 'Sync Points' that the Assassin's Creed franchise introduced, but with a twist. Enter a balloon and slowly assend. Now instead of just seeing a cutscene and that's it, you have to find everything with your binoculars. It's an interesting mini-game at first, but soon loses it's welcome.
To unlock upgrades for your car, you need to affect each territory's THREAT level. This is done in much the same way Just Cause 2 did; take over camps and destroy stuff. In this case, you're killing snipers, finding and defusing landmines and bringing down 'scarecrow towers'.
There's 3 territories, plus a no-man's land. Each territory has it's own set of the above things. A couple upgrades require to complete side missions too.
In each territory, you have a 'stronghold'. Do side missions and collect required 'parts' to unlock projects. I'd suggest to always build the Cleanup Crew projects as soon as you possibly can. It's a godsend! Projects include health, ammo and water (which is like your 'medipack') refills.
You upgrade Max in very much the same way as the car.
Instead of territory THREAT levels, however, it's your 'rank' that unlocks items. Right off the bat, you should purchase the crowbar; it's required for a lot of looting. You can even get Max to grow a beard, if you're into that.
Scrap is everything in Mad Max, so make sure to loot destroyed vehicles (Cleanup Crew project is useful for this) and camps whenever you can.
You'll need scrap to level up Max, the car and fully upgrade your Strongholds.
Lastly, do not rush through the main story.
You likely will not enjoy your time playing if you do; instead try and work towards uprading Max and the car as much as possible before moving onto the next territory. Various story missions require you to grind anyway, so you may as well do so between missions!

HOWEVER, I'd suggest you wait until a sale of 30% off or more before purchasing due to it's repetitive nature.

When you think of roguelikes, you normally think of randomness, high difficulty, and most importantly, permadeath. Dying in those games is very serious, you lose everything: Characters, stats, items, all gone. In that genre, death really means Game Over. But what if it didn’t have to be that way? Enter Rogue Legacy.
You are a warrior tasked with exploring a magical castle and defeating monsters within, with Castlevania-like gameplay that should be familiar to everyone. The twist is that, when you die, that character is gone, and you start playing as one of their heirs, with different traits and classes. The money and treasure gathered by the deceased are passed on, and you can spend them on upgrades and equipments for the new generations.
The game manages to keep a constant sense of progress with the upgrade system; dying is not the end, it’s the beginning of a new adventure where you’re likely to be better prepared. It’s not just about getting better stats and armor, either, you’ll also unlock new classes and mechanical improvements, like dashes and air jumps.
Your descendants are, however, randomly generated. This goes for both class and traits, the latter of which are characteristics like "Glaucoma" or "Dwarfism" that can be very helpful, irrelevant, or highly crippling. The unreliability inherent to the heirs often forces you to adapt to something that "will do" instead of having the best for the task available, which makes victory all the more sweet.
And of course, it wouldn’t be a roguelike if the journey through the castle was always the same. It changes, but not simply for each game: It changes on every single generation. This is why you don’t want to die too early: You miss the chance to get a lot of loot, and boss rooms are transferred elsewhere. On the other hand, a new character means new treasure to find, so it’s not that bad. It’s fun, both to win, and to lose.
And that is Rogue Legacy: A game that avoids being frustrating, but still without making you feel you’re getting off easy. All the balance in the gameplay elements really shows that a lot of effort was put into making this game, and it paid off, because Rogue Legacy makes for a fantastic roguelike*, and probably for one of the best Castlevanias out there, too.
* “Roguelite”, if you prefer.
PS: Use of a controller is highly recommended.

Don't be fooled by my play time on Steam - I've played a lot more than it says (I owned the physical copy for ages before registering the key here) and I can say it's pretty addicting.
Like most simulators, the game is based on a mundane task, and obviously this is based on driving a truck. Not everyone's idea of a fun time, I know, but it really can become fun if you put your mind to it. Or rather, don't. The reason I love ETS2 so much is that it's so great to just load up on a lazy day that I'm not in college and drive around for a bit. It lets me forget the stress of the real world, and take up someone else's life and just relax. Put some tunes on the music player from your computer, or listen to a nifty in-game radio that covers a lot of stations, even the more obscure ones like Real XS, only available in Manchester if you're listening on FM.
Unlike a lot of other simulators, the presentation is absolutely spot on here. The graphics look excellent and there are plenty of options to fine-tune your experience (even my decent PC has frame issues on the highest settings) but even on lower settings the graphics are better than the majority of simulation games out there. The mechanics are great too, and the physics engine really makes you feel like you are driving a real-life truck.
I do have a couple of issues with the game. One is that the collisions aren't very good/realistic and there is no visible damage to the truck at all. However, if you intend to play the game at all seriously, (i.e. not purposefully crashing into everything all the time) this won't be an issue. The other is that every time there is an update (and that is a lot), my truck gets returned back to my main garage back in Manchester, which is annoying seen as I've already explored the roads around that area (Great Britain). I feel it would be better if your truck was moved to the nearest city, considering they're not too far away from each other.
Aside from those couple of very small problems, ETS2 delivers in every area. Graphics, sound, gameplay and general presentation are well above the rest when it comes to simulators.

While this game is about building a prison, taking care of prisoners and rehabilitating them (as of the last update), to me this game shows everything right about game development. Introversion has taken time to listen to the people who play their game, make videos to show up the updates and highlights of their development process, and try to add as much detail as they can as they go. While it is a "game in progress," it has been an awesome ride this far and I can't wait to see what comes next.
As for the game itself, it's a fun simulation that's only gotten better with time. Your options are many, although your starting funds are few. Persistence pays off in the long run, so it helps to put a few hours aside a day to play the game and make one more goal (making room for more prisoners, implementing a better daily schedule, finally building the visitation room, etc). It will hook you if you are into detailed sims, and maybe even if you are not. Just be careful - this game can suck hours away from you without you noticing.

Another game oozing with really smart game design, Rogue Legacy is probably what you’d get if you crossed Castlevania with a “bullet hell” game like Ghouls N’ Ghosts. Like Castlevania, the main objective of Rogue Legacy is to explore a castle and defeat several bosses within it.
But what sets Rogue Legacy apart and makes it really fun and interesting is that, when you die - and you will die a lot - you get to choose between 1 of 3 children of the character you were just playing to avenge their parent and explore the castle. Each child may have genetic abnormalities or traits that make the game play differently each time. Some will directly affect gameplay, while others are just for flavor. For example, you may have a child who’s a midget. They’ll have a smaller hitbox and be able to go through small openings, but they may also take more knockback. Or you might have a child who’s colorblind. Then the game is played in black and white until you die again. And each time you die, the layout of the castle is randomly rearranged, so it’s kind of like playing a brand new game each time. You’re also free to swap out skills and equipment to experiment with different playstyles if you’re stuck on a boss. Really cool stuff. On top of that, you’ll inherit your items from your parent when they die, but the game makes you spend the money you inherit on upgrading new items or skills before you reenter the castle. So each time you die, there’s a kind of moment where you think “Crap I died…But now I get to choose a new character and upgrade their items and skills!” A neat mechanic because it makes you never feel overly frustrated when you die. Which is good, because this game is hard. And you’ll die. A lot.
I can’t really think of too many negative criticisms of this game, it’s very solid and well designed. Again, not too pretty to look at, but that doesn’t matter to me for a game like this. Maybe the soundtrack was a bit unremarkable, but that’s nitpicking. Check out Rogue Legacy if you can handle a challenge.

This game is amazing if you love Castlevania-style action platformers. It plays very similar to a Castlevania game, with "Rogue-like" elements added in. The gameplay is very simple overall, with the amount of challenge you'd expect from an old-school game.
The gimmick of this game is that each death is permanent, but you choose one of your heirs for the next run. These heirs are all randomly generated, with their own class, magic spell(s), and traits that help or hinder gameplay (or change nothing, but are funny). The castle's layout changes every time you enter as well.
For example, you could choose your son the Barbarian, who is very strong and knocks enemies back further, but is near-sighted, causing the game screen to appear fuzzy except for the vicinity of your character.
Or you could choose your daughter the Paladin, who is good all around, and has ADHD, improving her movement speed. She's also bald, which doesn't affect gameplay, it's just cosmetic.
The game has a good sense of humor with many of the traits, and default Hero names (there's a text file in the game files you can edit to add your own hero names or replace them all).
It does get a little bit grindy once you hit a difficulty wall and need upgrades or better gear to progress if you're stuck, but luckily the game can be played in very short doses, plus you can save your progress and quit at any time.
And once you get multiple playthroughs, in New Game +++ and beyond, you will NEED to be decked out to not die instantly.
Overall this is one of my favorite games I own, and even though I feel I've completed it, I still have the urge to jump in again and try to slay one of the optional hidden bosses or see if I can get to New Game ++++.

Rogue Legacy is an excellent 2D platformer that revolves around the unique generations mechanic. Unlike normal roguelikes, which can lack depth due to lack of character progression, Rogue Legacy allows the player to progress his character's family generation after generation. Each run through the castle will be completely different from the last, simply because each gero is totally different.
Humor is, well, funny, if sometimes politically incorrect and sometimes childish. Easter-egg-esque features (changes in the loading screen to reflect current character traits, changes in in-game text and dialogue to reflect traits like Dyslexia) keep anyone playing or watching entertained, and a collection of positive and negative traits powerful enough to be useful, but not game-breaking, ensure an interesting experience for hours.
The game's story is surprisingly sober in the midst of all this, and though it's simple (presented in a series of journal entires found throughout the castle) it has the desired effect. As it starts out it was amazingly fun to drive around, get to a Stronghold and clearing sites. Eventually though, you realize how limited you are as a player. The melee fighting has you punching light or heavy attacks as well as being able to shoot the shotgun and stab with the shiv. How about being able to throw that shiv, to stealth inside and sabotage some things before assaulting. Things like that.
Strongholds themselves are surprisingly lifeless. No one moves around, it's basically a garage with an added space to it. Sure it evolves as you upgrade things, it adds some cosmetics. It would have been more fun if a stronghold actually was a settlement too, where you see NPC's doing their wasteland businesses.
It has a lot of fun elements, that could have been more fun if they had added some more functionality to it. Overall, it's a very fun game, but it wears off the longer you play it due to the extreme repetition. Storywise, it's more of a guide through the game and you don't really have anything to say about it. So, don't expect any deeper RPG functionalities.
Final words; Having said all the above, the game itself is really, really fun. It feels like a Batman (light) game set in the Mad Max "universe".

Rogue Legacy is a great bit of Metroidvania meets rogue-like fun. It's whimsical, it's challenging, and it even has a decent story that gets really interesting towards the end. I think its greatest fault is its potentially frustrating beginning though. The short tutorial is fine, but unlike another famous rogue-like platformer Spelunky, you probably won't have a "fair chance" at completing even the early content until you grind for a certain number of persistent upgrades. Many rogue-likes and rouge-like hybrids always start you off the same way and just force you to use your skill, wits, and luck to complete any given run. Even though you certainly need wits and skill to get you through Rogue Legacy, you can progressively and permenantly soften the difficulty of different sections by collecting gold, equipment, character classes, and runes. This is great for those who find rogue-likes in general too hard for their tastes, but it does mean that you may occasionally hit difficulty spikes that make you feel like you
to grind before you can tackle further content. (I'd say that each area is roughly tuned to increments of 25 character / upgrade levels. So you probably won't complete your first run of the game until you are about level 75 - 100.) Still, as more stuff unlocks I feel the game gets progressively better and more "fair", so it's worth sticking through the rough bits for the fun bits if you have the patience. By the time you unlock everything, the world is your oyster in terms of how you want to customize yourself for the challenges that still lie ahead.

Have you ever wanted to try your luck at survival in a post apocalyptical hellscape where your only chance of survival is how hard you hit and how fast you drive? Well this might just be the game for you.
Mad Max is a game that is just so gosh darn fun it should be illegal. Using your fighting skills and driving knowhow you manage to rise from the ashes and literally change the world around you for the better. Starting out with nothing and left to die in a sand blasted wasteland Max sets out on a journey of redemption and revenge.
The story is pretty good but don’t expect a huge sweeping arc. It gets you from point A to point Gas Town but you will want to find out how it plays out and trust me, you won’t see the ending coming when you start. I found myself engrossed in Max’s adventure and every time he met a new and interesting character I wanted to learn more about them. Each of them as unique and volatile as the world they inhabit I would have loved to see more of them.
Speaking of the world….. It's big, not just big it is HU….omg so big…GE. It takes ages to drive from one side to the other; if you walked I imagine it would take hours. At first glance it may appear to be somewhat barren and dull but with an almost unlimited supply of places to go and things to do or destroy it will keep you busy for a very long time.
The locations are another high point of this game. No matter how many of the camps or loot locations I went to they were all different. Each and every marker on the map was something new to explore, some small story hidden from the player. A throne made from a whale skull, a container painted up like a present full of…… no spoilers. But I had endless hours of joy just seeing the world for what it was; a literal sandbox…….. yes a pun, get over it I like jokes.
Now the car, your rolling death machine of death or as your new friend Chumbucket calls it “The Magnum Opus.” This thing is a beast, along with Max you take it from nothing and turn it into a killing machine. Every single part of it can be swapped out, upgraded and switched about at any time. This thing is fun on wheels and I had a blast blowing away every single wastelander I saw… another pun I should watch out for that. A word of advice, the harpoon is awesome BUT the Thunderpoon is on another level. Make sure to hit normal people with them, they make a squishing pop sound that is just so very satisfying.
The other half of combat is with Max himself and that is no less fun I can assure you. Whilst being similar to other combat systems, which in and of itself is not a bad thing given how awesome those games are, this time around everything feels heavy. It is however a good kind of heavy. Max has weight and when he smashes a fist covered in a gauntlet made of tools and spiky car parts into some guys face it is very rewarding. The ground combat is vicious, bloody and always left me wanting more. Besides Max being very capable of liquefying people’s skills with his bare hands he also has a small array of weaponry. Razor sharp shivs are especially fun to stick people with but the devastating quad barrelled sawn off shot gun will work in a pinch too.
In conclusion Mad Max will probably not win a GOTY but so what, it is frigging awesome. From start to finish it I found nothing but a heart pounding rampage of bloody carnage across one of the most interesting open worlds I have seen and not once did I think of taking my foot of the gas and slowing down. If you love open words, car combat, post apocaliptica or beating the living snot out of the poor souls that get in your way then this game is worth a buy even at full price. If on sale it is a MUST BUY.

Starting out with nothing and left to die in a sand blasted wasteland Max sets out on a journey of redemption and revenge.
The story is pretty good but don’t expect a huge sweeping arc. It gets you from point A to point Gas Town but you will want to find out how it plays out and trust me, you won’t see the ending coming when you start. I found myself engrossed in Max’s adventure and every time he met a new and interesting character I wanted to learn more about them. Each of them as unique and volatile as the world they inhabit I would have loved to see more of them.
Speaking of the world….. It's big, not just big it is HU….omg so big…GE. It takes ages to drive from one side to the other; if you walked I imagine it would take hours. At first glance it may appear to be somewhat barren and dull but with an almost unlimited supply of places to go and things to do or destroy it will keep you busy for a very long time.
The locations are another high point of this game. No matter how many of the camps or loot locations I went to they were all different. Each and every marker on the map was something new to explore, some small story hidden from the player. A throne made from a whale skull, a container painted up like a present full of…… no spoilers. But I had endless hours of joy just seeing the world for what it was; a literal sandbox…….. yes a pun, get over it I like jokes.
Now the car, your rolling death machine of death or as your new friend Chumbucket calls it “The Magnum Opus.” This thing is a beast, along with Max you take it from nothing and turn it into a killing machine. Every single part of it can be swapped out, upgraded and switched about at any time. This thing is fun on wheels and I had a blast blowing away every single wastelander I saw… another pun I should watch out for that. A word of advice, the harpoon is awesome BUT the Thunderpoon is on another level. Make sure to hit normal people with them, they make a squishing pop sound that is just so very satisfying.
The other half of combat is with Max himself and that is no less fun I can assure you. Whilst being similar to other combat systems, which in and of itself is not a bad thing given how awesome those games are, this time around everything feels heavy. It is however a good kind of heavy. Max has weight and when he smashes a fist covered in a gauntlet made of tools and spiky car parts into some guys face it is very rewarding. The ground combat is vicious, bloody and always left me wanting more. Besides Max being very capable of liquefying people’s skills with his bare hands he also has a small array of weaponry. Razor sharp shivs are especially fun to stick people with but the devastating quad barrelled sawn off shot gun will work in a pinch too.
In conclusion Mad Max will probably not win a GOTY but so what, it is frigging awesome. From start to finish it I found nothing but a heart pounding rampage of bloody carnage across one of the most interesting open worlds I have seen and not once did I think of taking my foot of the gas and slowing down. If you love open words, car combat, post apocaliptica or beating the living snot out of the poor souls that get in your way then this game is worth a buy even at full price. If on sale it is a MUST BUY.
Have fun ^_^

If you're familiar with the Borderlands series, you need not read the rest of this review, because you should already own this game.
If you're not familiar with this series, I'm sorry to hear that. Borderlands as a series (and especially this installation of it) is possibly one of the most thematically well-done franchises I've had the pleasure of experiencing. While the games are immersive and well-orchestrated in their own right, my personal favorite part of the game is the over-the-top, almost comedic amount of guns-n-bullets gusto with which the series is made. No other game made me laugh (maniacally and humorously) as much while murdering countless faceless foes as this series, because that's exactly what Borderlands 2 aims to do. Don't get me wrong - the series is definitely worth playing for the plot and environment as well. However, if you're not excited by dual-wielding rocket launchers and insane gibs, then this series won't give you the same amount of enjoyment that it gives me.
9/10 - This game (or at least a game in the Borderlands franchise) is an essential experience for any fan of the shooter genre.

So first off I have to say the game runs great. For whatever reason, Life is Strange suffered from some serious framerate dips on my PC (1060 / fx8320) even on medium settings, but Before the Storm maintained 60fps at max settings so that was nice.
The characters are all very well acted, and everyone and everything feels alive. The world feels lived in, and everything has a purpose. The music is great, and the game looks pretty darn good as well.
I enjoyed every moment of it, and there were plenty of surprises throughout. Ultimately I don't feel like there were any crazy big moments, revelations or twists, but maybe that'll come in episode two. Even if it stays pretty cut and dry and just fleshes out the relationship of Chloe and Rachel I'd be into that as well. I'm left not knowing what to expect next, but I'm excited to find out!

This game is absolutely worth the purchase for any Life is Strange fan. At first I had a lot of doubts thanks to the new developers, but this game remains 100% faithful to the first game. The story, art, direction and subtle hints are all fruitful and amazing. Despite changing most of the voice actors, Chloe's new VA is quite phenomenal in most scenes while others leave something to be desired. (Rachel's is awesome!)
I also love the fact that this tells Chloe's story, not Max's. But don't mistaken the absence of our 'Everyday Hero' as cutting Max out completely, she still holds a ton of influence on Chloe. I also loved-loved-loved the sound design and soundtrack. Overall, 7/10 from me.

There is still a sense of progression as every time you die, an heir takes your place and you get to upgrade.  These upgrades stick forever so it makes subsequent runs a little less difficult.  Also, every time you die...its because YOU made a mistake.  There are no cheap deaths.  Great game...so glad I picked it up for ~ $3.00 during sale.

Although it's hindred by being a little heavy on the grindy side, Rogue Legacy is an incredibly fun experience. Some of the tightest controls in a video game ever, combined with some great level design and cool concepts earn it a solid 8/10.

Undertale Review:   8/10
This game is using the format of bad graphics, great story-telling. This is why Undertale is such a hit with the fans and the fandom. However, in my opinion, I personally do not like the graphics of the overworld setting, the game is linear in the map fromat insead of adventuring to find the right way through the map. The battle technique is new for the a RPG as in a new way to fight the enemies, however not killing everything in sight is a nice touch added to the game. For the opposing hand, Undertale does pose replay value, sure there are different endings, but after the Pacifist or No Mercy route, you pretty much did all of the game has to offer. The soundtrack is not the best music I have heard, but it would place high if I had ever done a "Top 10 Best Music Soundtracks" probably at 4 or 5. Anyway, in the No Mercy Route, the game is pretty easy since as the game goes further along, you can easily one hit  KO enemies which makes it loses the point of the route, expect two bosses in the game which if you played or seen Undertale, you know who I am talking about. In the end, Undertale has stated that you do not need great graphics to be an awesome game, however after a while, the game loses the value of replaying the game for a different ending. In conclusion, I give Undertale a 8/10, not too bad but not the greatest game I have ever played.

Hm, I'm sure many people will disagree with my opinion here, but I found Rogue Legacy to be somewhat underwhelming.  Or maybe I just don't enjoy rogue likes too much as I really hate the feeling that I wasted hours of my life by dying and starting from scratch.  Then again, I enjoyed FTL more and it was even more "rogue-like" than RL, since its only form of progression was acquiring new ships, while in RL you could build up your RPG stats and unlock classes.  I think the first 30 minutes of RL is quite enjoyable, but the problem is you eventually realize the gameplay is a bit stark and the control is never as responsive as you'd hope.  Many of the skills seem pretty imbalanced or only useful for very particular situations.  I did end up playing RL enough to beat the game once, so I must have enjoyed it to some extent... but overall I guess I was expecting too much for a game to combine the genres of Roguelike, Platforming and RPG seemlessly.
Having recently finished this game, I can whole heartedly recommend it to anyone who enjoys a rogue-like gameplay.  Do not let the initial difficulty stop you from giving this game a good, hard try.

This is a fantastic example of a good truck based simulator game. This has everything anyone could ever want from a game of this type, with great gameplay, good graphics (but well optimised), and most importantly of all, allows complete immersion because of it's incredible realism. There is a wide variety of trucks and load types, and locations in Western Europe and the UK, so you will never be short of things to do. The integration of Steam achievements provides good goals for you to reach in game, most of which will take a large amount of time to do. The only negative from this game that i can think of is that sometimes the game can be a little buggy with AI traffic, but other than that almost flawless. I would give the gameplay 4/5 stars; the realism 5/5 stars; and the graphics 3/5 stars. Overall rating 4/5 stars.

"Oh, what a lovely game! WHAT A LOVELY GAME!"
First of all, let me say that the Mad Max franchise contains some of my favorite films to date. George Miller's imagination and filmmaking is some of the greatest out there. To see the magic from the films transform into a video game is quite incredible.
My experience in the game so far has been phenomenal. I was very excited to see what the game had to offer, and it definitely lived up to the hype. It stayed true to the movies, as well as being it's own adventure. Visually, the game looks beautiful. I was very impressed by Avalanche Studios to create such an immersive world, where you play as the true Road Warrior.
As for the Road Warrior, Max's persona is not protrayed as Mel Gibson or Tom Hardy, but redifined as his own character. The gameplay is fluid, and it's enjoyable to both ride in your Magnum Opus and beat up War Boys. Finally, the mechanics, looting, & progression systems flow very well with the rest of the game.
Overall, this is a terrific game. My favorite aspect of this title is the cars, including customization, personalization, & style. It captures the true spirit of Mad Max and the cars from the films. If you love Mad Max as much as I do, then I encourage you to pick up this game. A truly worthy buy.

When Zynga sells you a game, you know they're just trying to give you pain and charge you money to alleviate that pain temporarily. In Borderlands 2, they don't give you a way to alleviate the pain except by playing more. You have starting weapons that are so terrible it's criminal that anyone would charge you money for them, that gently massage your enemies to death. You have cutscenes that you can't skip. You have a lot of walking between checkpoints and where you died on top of the unskippable respawn animation. (And, by the way, I think it's cheaper to die than to restock your ammunition.) What you don't have in the midst of this is any fun.
If it required skill to kill things efficiently, I'd be okay with that. If it didn't require any skill and I could still kill things efficiently, I'd be happy. But it appears to just take a huge amount of bullets and some hope, and then a lot of time.

I enjoy having the vest wealth of references to all sorts of movies and video games in the past, as well as the color of the enviornments are absolutely astounding the further you play into the story. Gang Beasts is at its best as a novelty party game.  With the right group of friends this physics-based jelly people wrestling is a blast.  Check out some videos of it on youtube.  If you laugh your head off and are desperate to play it with friends then get it.  The fighting is brilliant, and experimenting with all the different combinations of wobbly break dance fighting will earn some big laughs, and plenty of happy shouting when you throw your mate into the grinder and watch him (or her) attempt a fruitless escape.
Its a bit content-light right now, but there is plenty of fun to be had, and there is loads of stuff on the way.
On to the negative.  Its not a game with a great deal of replay value unless you can organise three player matches.
Single player gets boring quickly after you've seen all there is to see.  You will get a lot of laughs, and certain levels will have earned a soft spot in your heart, but right now there isn't much to do past the first 45 minutes of play.
Presumably, this replay factor will improve once story mode and more game modes are implemented, but right now its not a game solo fighters will want to spend $20 on.
However if you have a couple of mates keen to play this with you then get on board.  At 40% off its a blast and well worth the money.  It even has the potential to replace Smash Bros as your go to fighting game with friends.

Prison Architect, though still in alpha is an amazing simulation that i find rather interesting just simpy watching rather than interacting.
To sum this game up you're basically building a prison from the ground up, changing the peramaters and conditions of such prison, watching your choices come into effect and hopefully seeing your prison grow...through blood, sweat and tears, literally. The game can be as easy or as difficult as you like. you are free to build the prison as you see fit; from prison cells to workshops, class rooms to armouries, you are the architect.
At times there

This early access title is supported by both the devs and the community base, through monthly updates and mods (some of which are very nice, i recommend imperial architect if you're a fan of star wars, (

Rogue Legacy is a side scrolling, action RPG platformer through a randomly generated dungeon. It's also a whole bucket of fun. Big thumbs up.
I recommend viewing this trailer.
I also recommend using some kind of controller. God help anyone who tries to use keyboard and mouse.
Gameplay: Run and jump around a 2D world killing things, dodging things, and collecting money to spend on upgrades.
Presentation: Fun and colorful. The crunchy sound effects are satisfying. The flavor is funny, right down to the ever-hysterical run animation; a sword outstretched, head held high, sprinting high-step that all but screams "CHEARGE!"
Gimmick: When you die, and you will die a lot, your character dies permanently. The game ends and you return to the main menu. To continue your adventure, you select one of the 3 generated heirs of your recently deceased playable character. They each have a randomly assigned class and various genetic traits. Some traits are useful, like dwarfism, which lets you access areas a full sized person can't. Some of them are harmful, like near sightedness, which makes things farther away from your character blurry. Some of them are amusing and useless, such as hypochondria, which falsely exaggerates the damage you take... for example, being hit for 10 damage might cause a big red "2,308" to pop up over your head.
Your selected heir will inherit their predecessor's collected money, unlocked passive skill tree bonuses, and purchased equipment. So while the character himself/herself is essentially rerolled upon death, everything aside from their name, class and traits are retained. A quick sample of what the skill tree looks like can be found here:
Dying also regenerates the dungeon, so your offspring don't have to retrace any identical steps.
I wasn't too sure about this game at first. I was terrible at it, and often died before obtaining enough money for my heirs to purchase anything of use. But Rogue Legacy's amusing presentation helped me to stick with it through the initial difficulties. After a couple of hours I was competent enough to make some decent runs and became hooked for good. I'm now 18 hours and 160 dead ancestors in. Still going strong.
You'll get your money's worth here.

First of all, let me say that the Mad Max franchise contains some of my favorite films to date. George Miller's imagination and filmmaking is some of the greatest out there. To see the magic from the films transform into a video game is quite incredible.

The gameplay is fluid, and it's enjoyable to both ride in your Magnum Opus and beat up War Boys. Finally, the mechanics, looting, & progression systems flow very well with the rest of the game.
Overall, this is a terrific game. My favorite aspect of this title is the cars, including customization, personalization, & style. It captures the true spirit of Mad Max and the cars from the films. If you love Mad Max as much as I do, then I encourage you to pick up this game. A truly worthy buy.

Originally I avoided this game, as the fanbase was repulsive. I was sick of being spammed with "Skele-puns" by my friends, but recently, I decided to try it as alot of people I know, Youtubers, and critics had said good about it.
I completed my first run today. It took me approv 9 hours over 3 days, in 2 sittings (I completed it on the third day at 1:05 AM).
This game is great. While it is a short one, theres enough endings to keep you busy, alot of characters to grow to love or hate, and alot (and I mean ALOT) of secrets to get. The boss fights are fun (some more than others, but thats subjective), and the story always seems to touch you emotionally no matter what route you take. The soundtrack is also excellent.
Alas, no game is perfect.
My biggest complaint. The Genocide run.
In this game, theres a run called the "Genocide run". In this run, you kill literally everything. Once you complete it, all other endings are effected. This is a good thing, as it gives the game more replayability, as it doubles the amount of endings you can get. But, this is a double edged sword. There is no ingame way to reset this. You are stuck with these new endings. This locks you out of alot of the games content. While there are (probably) ways to fix this, no one method seems to work for everyone. So, the player is either forced to either not do the genocide run and not see the post-genocide endings, or do it and never be able to start a fresh slate EVER AGAIN. This is, in my opinion, a bad decision on the dev's part. I'm all for your actions being remembered, but being locked out of content is, well, stupid.

It has some extremely solid ballistics modelling and the co-op functionality works flawlessly. That's enough to take you maybe a quarter of the way through the game's much-too-long campaign (let alone the DLC) before the novelty wears off and everybody involved realises they have better things to do with their time.
Borderlands 2 bets everything on its humour (sic) and personality (sic) to carry it across the line when its shallow gameplay has exhausted itself. Unfortunately, that begins and ends with a cast of grating characters who talk and talk and talk and talk endlessly over the in-game radio, spouting overdetermined verbal tics and recycled internet memes in a desperate attempt to present itself as cool and likeable.
Equally grating are the stabs the game makes at post-modern irony; because of course pointing out that the design of your game is bad and then continuing to engage in bad design but On Purpose is hip and nervy and not the least bit obnoxious.
For those who are interested, the game is indeed a very solid PC version, with very scaleable settings that are well-optimized and let you push the visuals well beyond its console counterparts. The PhysX effects are among the most impressive I've yet seen. So if technical concerns were a deciding factor for you then go right on ahead and make the purchase. Most importantly of all, the game offers separate volume sliders for different audio tracks, allowing you to mute the dialogue while leaving the sound effects intact. You'll need it.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 - it may sound like it's gonna be one of those stupid and unnecessary games to play, but it isn't. Euro Truck Simulator 2 is one of the most fun, and probably realistic (by realistic, I mean, it includes Lights, traffic lights, indicators, windshield wipers, retarders for slowing down, and more!) games that I have played to date! The game can be easily modded, and the moving community is still in full swing, about 2 years after it's first release. There are several types of trucks, including Volvo, Scania, MAN, IVECO and DAF, and the map is across Europe, from Britain to Italy, or Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic if you have the Going East! DLC. Also, the DLC always comes along, with paint packs, and cargo packs, but at this point in time, we haven't really seen many packs other than custom paint packs, which I hope will die down, making way for proper DLC. There are many settings for the likes of Cruise Control, Retarders, high and low beam lights, which can also be mapped on a DSD Button Box, for example. I have thoroughly enjoyed my time playing this simulator, and I hope there will be more happy gaming hours to come! Here are my pros and cons of this game currently.
PROS:
-A fun, and realistic simulator
-At the moment (26th December '14) it's incredibly cheap for what it is
-Modding community is very strong
-Full wheel support, along with a shifter, and a button box, also.
CONS:
-At the start, you keep having to do "Quick Jobs", but I believe that they are just a bit boring, as you cannot customise the truck you are driving, because it isn't yours, so I Cheat Engine'd the game :-P
-Can be quite frustrating with the AI, sometimes, you try to let them turn into another road, but they don't move, because they think it's your right of way. Yeah, I know, quite annoying.
-No integrated Multiplayer mode, you need a mod to play online.
So that's about it, overall a great game! You can download some awesome mods, or just download the Multiplayer Mod and drive with friends! Get it for £3.74 (or however much it is) quickly, it's so worth it!
This is a simulator and it's not a pile of rubbish! My mind is boggled! 10/10

Where to start...
Well, first of all, you
play this without knowing anything about the game. Why? Because Undertale is not just a game, it's an
.
Everything you do (well, almost) has a consequence. Will you just blindly kill anything that crosses paths with you? Or will you try to understand what's going on in this world and help the monsters that inhabit it? That's up to you. You choose your own path and, consequently, the monster's.
I've spent many hours on this game, and I always discover something new. I often asked myself "what would happen if I'd done this instead?", and almost everytime I'd discover something new. In the end, it's your curiosity and determination what pushes you to play it again... and maybe do something you don't want to do.
And that's the other part that makes this game an experience: you really end up caring about this world... and hating it. But not hate as "this game is♥♥♥♥♥♥quot;, but as a hate for not being able to keep going and know what'll happen next... or hate towards yourself. It's really hard to explain it without spoiling anything.
But, as a reviewer, I must also talk about the cons.
If you don't check the web, you won't find every secret on this game.
I know I know, that's why it's called
, but there's one that I don't think I would've found if I didn't check the web (maybe if it had unexpectadly closed for whatever reason after talking to a certain character). Anyone who has done it must know what I mean:
.
Also the FUN events. There're random events that appear if the FUN variable has a certain value, but after a lot of runs there're some that i haven't seen. Yes, you can change the value and see it, but it shouldn't be that way. It would be better with a smaller range of values for this variable.
And... that's it. I can't think of any other cons
So, should you buy it? Definitely.

It took me 931 hours to get "bored" of this game. Within those hours I had experiences that I will cherish, meeting people I now play with in discord etc.
I play the game in a way most people dont. I play on "low pop" servers with 20-30 peak time players which allows me to farm and build in peace and the occasional encounter with players become way more significant. Usually people are more friendly on these servers and its also more "noob friendly". I have probably played a different game to those who play on high population with KOS, kids screaming and all the cancer.
What Im saying is there is so much to enjoy in this game beyond the PvP and that this game will 100% be worth your money IF you realize that you will get raided. The question is what do you do when that happens? My tip is to learn from it, improve your next base and adapt. Learning to build bases is a ton of fun as well.
Overall I have no regrets, best 20€ spent ever. I will keep checking what the updates bring and come back to check it out again when they implement some balance changes and more PvE content.

Rogue-like gaming meets Castlevania and a persistant upgrade system.  If your curiouse about Rogue and Rogue-like 'hardcore' gaming then this is an excellent place to start.  While it has the harsh and randomness of a Rogue-like. it also has an underlying persistant progression that all of your characters share and benefit from as you unlock it and a rather unique sense of humor.   There are a wealth of classes and features to play around with as you progress through the game and not much is missing in the way of challenge you'd expect from a game in this genre while still managing to be more approachable by newcomers.
Though it does bare mentioning that if you sit there and grind those manor upgrades you'll soon find the challenge stripped from the game, if only for the time being till your progress catches up with your power.  I recommend not grinding, sure grab all the money and pickups you can per run but -do not- grind.  you may find  that stripping the challenge from the game (even temporarilly) may also diminish your enjoyment of it.

This game is simply genius, extremely well designed. A game doesn't have to utilize the latest and greatest technology to be good. Someone put tons of thought and effort to make this game work and have an impact, and I wholeheartedly believe it did and will.
My personal background: I love Earthbound and RPGs, so yeah I'm a bit experienced and perhaps even bias on the genre. I heard of the game in 2013 with the Kickstarter, though it was a passing glance. Comes September and this game comes out, I'm like "Woah I heard of this game" and got it shortly afterward.
Toby Fox, no matter what he thinks of himself or what others think of him, has made a very clever game with a story to tell. It's use of meta-humor and breaking the fourth wall is essential to understand the story, who would have thought that? There's no other game like this, and my friends, with the same exact games being rebranded as something new every year or so, I'm very happy to say that.
I have no doubt in my mind this game will impact the gaming industry and community in one way or another, with it's very heartfelt story, gameplay mechanics and battle systems never explored before, impressive pixel art, and a soundtrack that takes what made old NES and SNES music so great and adds it's own flare of whatever it wants for it to sound good - there's plenty of beeps and boops, but it's not afraid to pull out a guitar or piano and for it to still fit wonderfully with the rest of the soundtrack.
The characters are simply a treat. While there are a few unlikable characters, they are few and far between, as I can't even recall one on the top of my head. Almost every "enemy" you meet is simply a friend in disguise, just wanting to have fun and talk with you. This game takes an average RPG and says "Why do I have to kill these people?", and it works so flawlessly.
Man, I wish I could articulate my thoughts more.
To those who have been playing video games their whole life, to those just started their gaming experience. To those who love violence and to those who love friendship, to those who love RPGs and hate RPGs, to those who love action and to those who want to just talk...
TO EVERYONE
BUY THIS GAME
YOU WILL NOT REGRET IT, GUARANTEED

After 3 years of development you cannot call this game an Alpha. So this review is for a full game.
This game call itself a "Survival Game", and Yes, the most important challenge here is to survive, you will die a lot of times and for different reasons (Food, Cold, Players, Animals, Etc). Anyway the game is fun, its a great sandbox, you will never know what is going to happen when you start playing.In this kind of games is really important for you to feel immersed in the game, and this game does it really good. Graphics are really good, but as i said before it has a lot of FPS problems, you really need a good PC. Sound is good, its not the best outthere but its really good. The bad side of this game besides its stability and FPS problems is its community, its a PvP community, there are not roleplayers here, and that is a bad thing in games like this.
I recommend this game if you have a good PC and if you like PvP.

While I don't think the game is playable without a controller, once you have a controller, it opens a world of exciting and compelling "rogue like" gameplay.  Each playthrough will have you toying with traits and characteristics you didn't know you needed/wanted.  Often you may even find yourself with things you don't need or want, but are worth the playthrough, just for the experience.  Tight controls round out the experience, as long as you have a controller.
